New material role `visor`: dark amber tinted glass (base 0x231803, roughness 0.10) with a fresnel sheen driven by new visorColor/visorGain uniforms, not gated on botGlow. Added because the only glow role was `eye`, a MeshBasicNodeMaterial flat fill - a light-valued uniform rectangle over the face reads as a bandage regardless of its outline, so no amount of reshaping could fix the visor while it used `eye`.

Helmet Mk VII iterated against Halo reference under an adversarial critic loop (scored 2/3/3/3/4/5). Crown+brow+jaw+side plates collapsed to one `shell` value (three values read as stacked slabs); visor rebuilt as a hard-edged tapering extrude in the new `visor` role inside a dark rubber socket; modelled shadow gutter at the brow seam; mandible tapers to the chin. Removed the rotated wraparound wings, whose gap behind the flat glass made two wedges reading as a MOUSTACHE. Crest raised above the dome - at y=0.124 it was inside the dome radius so only its tips showed, hence the antenna-nub read.

Upper-body proportions against a Halo Infinite lineup reference. Gorget widened 0.255->0.345 and shortened 0.210->0.135: a narrow column between jaw and chest reads as a long neck whatever it is made of, and measurement showed the neck was never BARE (gorget overlapped the helmet by 67mm) - the collar itself was the neck. Pauldrons raised y 0.150->0.186 and heavily bevelled so they cap the shoulder instead of jutting sideways; pelvis seal narrowed so it stops flaring wider than the waist armour. Measured shoulder-span:helmet-width is 2.95, already inside the reference 2.6-3.0 band, so shoulder width was left alone.

POV debug readout: per-actor perception panel (state/aim gates/nav/squad/lifetime), cyan path line + goal diamond, spot marker coloured by fire decision -- lets the user check the POV view against what the bot actually perceives

POV debug HUD rework: graphical widgets (spread-driven crosshair, reaction ring, target plate w/ hp, state chip + alert badge, vitals bars + pips, squad hp rows); text panel trimmed to residual numbers and moved top-left off the fps/navwarn row

Neck restored after over-correcting it away: gorget lowered/shortened (0.135->0.105) and a short dark rubber neck seal + metal ring added above it. The original fault was never that a neck existed, it was that a 0.255-wide collar ran the full jaw-to-chest distance; a short dark neck under a wide collar reads correctly.

Role-specific bodies. New BOT_ROLE_DESIGNS + botDesignForRole(roleId): rifleman=large ruck, medic=small pack + cross-marked hip pouches, technical=medium pack + twin missile tubes, sniper=small pack + HELMET_MARKSMAN (narrow slit visor, monocular optic over the right eye, rangefinder stalk). Mark VII face split into MARK_VII_FACE so role helmets swap only the face and the roles still read as one army. Medical crosses use untinted eye-on-rubber, NOT accent - accent is team-tinted, and a cross that changes colour per team is livery, not a medical marking.

Pack sizing pass: all three packs widened past the 0.420 chest (large 0.320->0.400 wide). Narrower than the backplate framing them, they read as panels inset into the armour rather than rucks worn over it. Technical's missile tubes moved off the centreline (x 0.088/-0.020 -> 0.098/0.233) - 0.108 apart at radius 0.062 they intersected and read as one lumpy mass instead of two launchers.

Wired role designs into the game: createBotProceduralBody now passes botDesignForRole(activeBotActor?.role) instead of the flat BOT_BODY_DESIGN. Added a squadleader entry (medium pack + antenna) so it is not the only role without a pack. botDesignForRole memoises per role, so every bot of a role shares one design object and one set of cached geometry - N bots of a role cost the same geometry as one. Verified: withBotActor binds activeBotActor before the body is built and createBotActor assigns roleId before that, so the role is always resolved; actor.role is never mutated at runtime (leadership lives on the squad), so a bot's kit cannot go stale after election.

New ballistic audio module: closest-approach geometry (a superset of bot-alert.shotMissDistance, cross-checked in the test so the two cannot drift), whizz gating off miss distance plus a tracer-speed arrival delay, ricochet gating off inferred surface hardness and a cubed grazing curve, a per-tick proximity tracker for curved projectile paths, and procedural bullet_whizz / bullet_ricochet voices.

Wired ballistic audio into both viewers through their existing playAtCulled gates (each keeps its own signature): whizz on every resolved hitscan shot, pickImpactVoice replacing the unconditional bullet_impact play, a fire-once proximity whizz for rockets/grenades, and a budget alias so a ricochet consumes the impact rate-limit slot instead of opening a second window.

Documented the ballistic audio subsystem: the tracer-speed-as-muzzle-velocity proxy, the fact that surface hardness is inferred from hit.kind plus obstacle id prefixes with no material tag anywhere, and the honest guest gap (combat resolves host-side only, so guests hear neither whizz nor ricochet).

New bot damage/death audio module: five mechanical hit tiers (metallic tink / clang+ring / clang+electronics stutter / bright ping / muffled blast thud) since the sampled enemy_hit is flesh and bots are robots, a pure Node-testable tier function anchored to the game's own botHealthSettings.threshold01 and weapons.js damage values rather than invented numbers, an intermittent seeded per-bot damage spark plus a budgeted sustained bed for the closest few, and a two-tone distress siren whose alternation and pitch wind down across the medic revive window.

Wired bot damage/death audio into both v2 viewers via their existing onBotDamaged/onBotDied/onBotRevived hooks and each file's own playAtCulled convention, added a playLoopCulled sibling over envAudio.playSynthLoop and a wider distress panner class so a siren carries further than the clang that caused it, bypassed the 100ms rate window for death stings (gated on concurrent death voices instead) and capped concurrent sirens at 3 with 1/sqrt(n) ducking so mass death does not sum.

Documented playSynthLoop in the Controller API (its only consumer is bot-damage-audio.js) and added a Bot damage/death audio section: the verified alive-to-dead-to-revivable-corpse state model, why the siren must end at diedAt + reviveWindowMs rather than when the corpse is culled (cullDeadBots spares revivable corpses, so the corpse outlives the siren), and the honest gaps - sustained event ids are synth-only because playAt is one-shot, and there is no guest replication.

New robotic bot-voice lexicon and synthesis: 13 callout phrases built from Peterson & Barney adult-male vowel formants driven through a three-band formant filter bank on a per-bot buzzy carrier, with an optional radio stage (comms band, tanh drive, squelch clicks, hiss tail) behind a flag rather than always on. Each phrase carries a deliberately distinct rhythmic signature so a half-heard line is still identifiable, and rhythmDistance plus a minimum-separation assertion is the regression guard for that; the closest pair sits at 0.135 against a 0.12 floor.

New arbitration layer for squad chatter, pure logic so the policy is Node-testable: seven refusal gates (chattiness, distance, event-key dedup, per-bot cooldown, per-TEAM per-line cooldown, squad and global rate buckets, then the shared combat-audio-budget reservation). Requests are dropped rather than queued because a callout that plays two seconds late no longer describes what the bot is doing, and requestBest collapses several witnesses of one event to the single speaker nearest the listener.

Wired 11 of the 13 callouts into both v2 viewers on real FSM edges: contact rides the existing recordContact publication so the reporting bot speaks and receivers stay silent, firing is a BOT_FIRE entry rather than a per-shot bark, and casualty lines subscribe to the onBotDied hook instead of editing the damage path. Flanking and squad-leader orders were skipped because neither has any signal in the FSM to observe. Added chatter on/off, radio/clean, volume and chattiness controls next to the existing bot-audio toggles, and a projectile id on the grenade threat list so a grenade warning dedups per grenade rather than per bot.

Added a bot voices and squad chatter section: the synthesis topology and why rhythm rather than timbre is the recognition channel, the full callout-to-trigger map with both viewers side by side, the two lines deliberately not built for lack of a signal, and the honest gaps - bots are host/solo sim so a guest has no FSM to derive callouts from, the sample-backed path is unexercised because sfx/ ships no voice files, and preemption frees the slot but cannot recall audio already scheduled.

Sound-design review fixes: test-ballistic-audio FakeNode gains .kind so ricochet oscillators are actually start/stop-checked (the .type blind spot inherited from the old harness); both viewers now create ONE shared createAudioBudget and pass it to the voice director and damage controller, which the docs claimed but the wiring never did; bot-damage-audio reclaims siren/loop slots and budget tokens when the audio sweep distance-culls a handle, and a death sting eviction now stops the sustained bed it displaced; docs corrected to say ballistic one-shots do not reserve from the budget.

POV HUD diagnostics: true-muzzle aim reticle + err readout, threat/alert/offscreen-target direction arrows, last-known ghost + cover anchor/peek marks + peek phase, cand count + acquisition-reset flash, effective-FOV wedge fix, split screen/world toggles persisted in ui slots, layout + perf hygiene

Stopped the flesh enemy_hit sample from stacking on top of the new mechanical bot_hit_* tier for every bot hit -- that layering contradicted the whole premise of the mechanical voices. Creatures, mobs and the human host still get it. Also aliased the five bot_hit_* ids into one sfxBudgetOk window: the budget is keyed by event id, so five private windows let the 'bot was struck' class burst 5x its intended rate.

Node tests for createBotDamageAudio, the highest-risk piece and previously the only untested one (builders/tiers/director/budget were covered, the controller was not). Covers siren grant+cap under mass death, revive vs bleed-out vs respawn endings, orphan release when a corpse is culled, budget/slot reclamation when the audio layer's own distance sweep stops a handle, and teardown. Mutation-checked: removing the handle.stopped reclaim makes the regression case fail, so it is not a vacuous test.

FakeNode stored the node class in .type, which every builder overwrites (osc.type='sine'), so the n.type==='oscillator' filter matched nothing and no oscillator was ever checked for start/stop or in-window scheduling. Added a separate .kind field. The oscillators turned out to be correct -- this was silently absent coverage, not a broken voice.

Perceived-enemy HUD marks: scan commits candidate identities (actor.perceivedEnemies, cap 8); POV world pass draws solid-white (LOS-verified) / faint-grey (occluded) diamonds over every noticed enemy + cand N (M vis) on the plate -- makes single-slot amnesia visible ahead of the planned multi-threat contact model

Bot chatter was inaudible for two measurable reasons, not one. (1) Range: the voice profile capped at 55 while gunshot reaches 90 and the death siren 120, so the orbit/fly camera sat outside voice range while still hearing everything else -- raised to 95 in both viewers. (2) Level: measured a 3-band formant bank on a 120Hz saw and it passed only -15.8 dB at Q=[9,11,12]. Dropped to Q=[5,6,7] (-12.4 dB, still reads as formants) plus a 2.5x makeup, about +11 dB net.

Death siren rebuilt as a machine fault beacon after the first version read as horror rather than hardware. Two detuned sawtooths a fifth apart, cross-faded continuously while gliding down for 12s, is literally how an air-raid siren is synthesized. Replaced with square-wave two-tone chirps separated by real silence, pitch stepping in four discrete power-down stages instead of a portamento glide, rests stretching 0.6s->1.3s as it fails. Three tests asserting the swept-sawtooth design were specifications of the rejected behaviour, so they were rewritten to assert the properties that separate machine from animal: no pitch ramps, discrete steps, full gate closure between beeps.

Harness aim/disengage parity: harness reaction tune (260ms, Notice-time slider removed), aim priming on retarget/re-sight, target stickiness, terrain-aware bot LOS with per-frame current-target check, flee resolves remembered attacker (healThreatId), unconditional heal retreat on hit, retreatSearchRadius, third-person host targetable

Harness cover parity: exact-anchor final approach on coarse zone grid, off-grid threat snapped to walkable cell (fail-open), cover holds/blacklists/danger survive zone rebake, tree trunks added to sight bake occluders, danger stamp footprint denominated in meters, null-field guard

Fix live-map undefined updateBotLiveButton (call updateRecordButton); retire 3 decision-time legality rules falsified by live bots (fire w/ post-shot reload, heal/tend consuming frame, sight-grace on reposition/alert P-frames) -- 18 rules, 395,533 legal / 458 core, table regenerated, tests updated

Sound parameter registry: all authored audio constants moved out of five modules into one dependency-free schema read live at build time, with a JSON override doc both v2 viewers fetch at boot and a cross-section auditParams(); collapsed the duplicate voice-concurrency number (budget.voiceCap was overwritten at construction and did nothing) onto director.speakerCap

Sound studio: standalone 5-tab design tool (offline-rendered bench analysis, lexicon rhythm editor, distance/masking measurement, headless director simulation, JSON export) importing the real modules; first run found the voice bus clipping at +0.65 dBFS, fixed with a tanh soft clip after the makeup gain for +3.4-4.6 dB RMS at no peak cost

Register the procedural-audio subsystem: audio.md gains a Sound parameter registry section, code-map gains nodes for synth-utils/ballistic-audio/combat-audio-budget/bot-damage-audio/sound-params/sound-studio plus their import edges (previously missing), CLAUDE.md gains the subsystem row

Wire bot role designs through GhostRenderer: new getDesign(item) option (default null, callback not import so multiplayer.js stays THREE-free) plus a conditional role field on toWirePose; closes a gap where env-viewer-v2 passed no design at all and rendered bots as the bare mannequin instead of the armoured design

Manual control panel in the design studio: sliders/entries/dropdowns/colour pickers over every gear descriptor field and the chassis proportions, multi-select with filter tokens, per-field group semantics (position/rotation add a delta, sizes multiply, categorical set absolutely), live transforms vs release-gated geometry edits so drags do not mint an InstancedMesh bucket per frame, line-geometry selection outline, undo, and Copy gear JS / Copy diff to paste back into bot-body-design.js

Bake the 13-line lexicon to audio via ElevenLabs in four voices (harry/adam/daniel/river) using the text field each line already carried; takes are baked DRY so the radio chain stays a runtime insert; API key read from env or a gitignored .eleven-key, never committed

Add buildSampleVoiceLine() plus a 14-band channel vocoder so one baked take serves both voice types: played dry it is a human, vocoded it drives the existing glottal carrier and per-bot identity survives (the carrier is the identity). Extracted radioTopAndTail() so synth and sample share one channel; new vocoder schema section

Separate gain staging for baked takes: voice.makeup (2.5) is calibrated for the synth at -38 dBFS and drove every TTS take into the limiter at 0 dBFS, so add voice.sampleMakeup (1.0) and raise vocoder.outGain to 2.2 for the band-split loss; measured in-browser, nothing now exceeds -0.1 dB peak
Add a SOURCES tab: A/B the formant synth against every baked TTS set per line, with live radio-channel and robot-vocoder toggles, a per-bot identity selector and the vocoder sliders

Add Kokoro backend and fetch the ElevenLabs voice list from the account instead of hardcoding ids; bake 26 sets / 338 takes (10 eleven + 16 kokoro, filtered to Kokoro's own C-or-better grades); emit manifest.json so a newly baked voice appears in the studio with no code edit. kokoro-js must be installed off Google Drive (npm EPERM/EBADF), resolved via PCW_TTS_HOME
Add lineIds()/lineText() live accessors so studio-authored lines are visible to the bake script and every list; voiceEventId now consults the override map too. LINE_IDS stays as the built-in set

Fix slider readouts never updating: the value was written once at render time, and the change handler re-rendered whole sections (destroying the slider mid-drag) for every tab except sources, which was not in the list at all. Readouts now refresh in place via a per-element _refresh

Rebuild the vocoder panel to explain rather than list: four labelled groups each with a canvas (band layout w/ radio passband + adjacent-edge coverage ratio, follower tracking vs true loudness, carrier, dry-vs-vocoded spectrum), all redrawn on every param change
Add lexicon ADD LINE / DELETE LINE (seeded syllables from the text's vowel groups, written to the voiceLines override map) plus a set picker and ALL-sources playback for the 26 baked voice sets

Correct an overclaim: a no-op npm install works in this directory; what failed was writing kokoro-js's ~411MB tree on the Google Drive filesystem. Observed once, so documented as unreliable-for-large-installs rather than categorically broken
Replace the last drifted bot-viewer-v2.html line citation in the header (5854, now 9042) with the symbol it points at, so the comment stops rotting as the viewer grows

Fix: an added line could never be spoken. The typo gate tested membership in LINE_PRIORITY (the 13 built-ins), so a studio-authored line synthesised fine and was dropped as unknownLine on every director request. New knownLine() accepts LINE_PRIORITY/voiceLines/linePriority; typos still refused. Regression assertions added and mutation-tested

Fix: the bake never saw studio-added lines. It read lineIds() without applying sound-params.json, so it silently rebaked the built-in 13 -- while the studio told the user to run it to give their new line a take. Now loads the override doc with fs (Node fetch cannot read file: URLs)

Fix: the vocoder Output canvas was always blank. It read spec.rate/spec.size, which spectrum() does not return, so every coordinate was NaN and canvas silently dropped the path; also missing the sqrt that converts power bins to amplitude before dB. Now uses spec.binHz like every other plot

Fix: REVERT LINE silently deleted a studio-added line (no code default to revert to) leaving the editor blank with a stale selection. Now refuses and points at DELETE LINE, matching that button's guard

First step toward a human soldier: new bot-face.js head (skin skull, sphere eyes with pupils/catchlights, side-profile nose, lips, ears, hair) with eight authored expressions, five new material roles (skin/hair per-body tinted, sclera/pupil/mouth shared), withHumanHead/withHelmet swaps that carry the skull not just the gear, and a Head section in the studio. Face emissive held to 15pct of the armour's: at full gain the head self-lit into a blank mask. Not wired into the game - bots still wear the Mark VII

Page load was dominated by three.js itself: the importmap pinned the UNMINIFIED three.webgpu.js at 1.97MB against 0.61MB for the min build - 3.2x the bytes and 3.2x the parse before the first frame. Studio switched to the min builds; the other 16 pages still pin the unminified one. Weapon GLBs (13-54KB, cached per id) were never the cost

Body and head split into independent axes: composeBot(body, head) crosses six body versions (bare rig, four frozen snapshots of the design history copied out of versions/, the live design) with four heads. The skull travels with the head, not the body, since headProfile/headZScale are top-level fields rather than gear. Studio gained a Body & head section and a Gallery (multi-select model list, per-row count, grid layout, fit-view); slots were previously one straight row that ran off screen past five

Gallery rebuilt as five independent axes crossed at display time (body/head/kit/expression/skin) after the first cut was a flat list of pre-baked combinations that welded them together - skin tone only existed on a determined face, expressions only on the current body. composeBot gained a kits param (raw BOT_DESIGN_ADDONS names, not role ids, since a role is itself a combination). Cross product capped at 36 with the overflow reported rather than silently truncated

Clothed human body added as its own BOT_BODIES branch, driven by four adversarial-critic rounds. Rig gained per-limb profiles (thigh/shin/upperArm/forearm) - one shared profile is why limbs read as tubing, since a thigh and a calf taper in opposite directions. New matte non-glowing cloth role: as team-tinted shell the uniform blew out to glowing mint and a blown-out surface has no shading, hiding the very profiles being judged. Joint spheres wider than their limbs (knee 116mm vs 112mm calf, shoulder 105 vs 98 sleeve) were erasing the silhouette; sub-25pct profile changes were invisible; garment edges had to be separate primitives with a value break, not bumps

Boot rebuild after close-up review. Measurement showed every trouser/cuff piece sitting between world y 0.123-0.181 against a boot top of 0.260 - all of them buried inside the shell, and what poked through was the bracelet ring and lumpy heel. Boot was also 215mm long on a 1.8m figure (a foot is ~0.15 of height). Now a foot outline plus a SEPARATE shaft cylinder, since one extruded outline cannot be both and levelling the collar to close a front gap turned the rear two thirds into a ski boot. Sole and heel are proud rbox steps in the same black as the upper: separation has to come from the step, because any lighter role is team-tinted and would give a red team red soles. Tests now DERIVE the boot top from footScale rather than hardcoding it, and assert nothing on the foot uses a light team-tinted role - the rule that caught me re-adding one

Proportions measured against human canon rather than eyeballed: arms were 22pct too long (forearm 33pct, the segment that reads as ape arms) while the legs were already right, and the neck lengthened in an earlier round to cure a bobblehead had overshot to 40pct over canon - most of why the upper body read short even though the torso measured correctly. New torsoYRatio/neckYRatio/headYRatio design fields replace hardcoded 0.22/0.37/0.48 literals in update(): neck.h sized the neck mesh without moving the head, so shortening a neck opened a gap instead of lowering the head onto the shoulders. Defaults preserve every existing caller. All four limb segments and every landmark now within 2pct of canon

Reverted the global 6pct body-scale work (body-metrics.js and eight files) at the users call, then fixed the squat it left behind. legLenRatio turns out to be CONSTRAINED not chosen: the pelvis sits at gait.pelvisHeightRatio*H = 1.044m regardless, so leg bones must exceed that with bend room. My earlier anthropometric 0.53 was 90mm over-extended (feet could not reach, which is why the measured hip sat below canon) and the 1.233x scale pushed it to 0.653 for 132mm of slack and a permanent crouch. Back to the rig default 0.62. Leg length cannot make a body taller - longer bones only bend the knees. New test asserts the reach constraint for every registered body

Chest widened 287->385mm to meet the shoulders. Arm roots attach at state.radius*0.66 = 198mm from the centreline - the CAPSULE radius, which the design cannot see - so at a 144mm half-chest the arms hung 55mm clear of the torso and the shoulder spheres floated off a narrow body. Chest:waist now 1.67; pelvis and belt widened to match so the belt still caps the hip

Chest widened 287->385mm to meet the arm roots (they attach at state.radius*0.66 = 198mm, the CAPSULE radius the design cannot see, so at a 144mm half-chest the arms hung 55mm clear of the torso). Cuff positions now DERIVED from named bone-length constants instead of typed metres: changing the arm and leg ratios had left the sleeve cuff 37mm past the wrist and all three boot pieces floating 70-150mm up the shin, with nothing wrong-looking in the descriptors. New handWristBias rig field (hand equivalent of footForwardBias, default 0): the glove outline is centred on the wrist so 87mm of hand sat back along the forearm, which is why the cuff kept landing on it. Hand narrowed 126->101mm and thinned 47->38mm; it measured 40pct too wide and read as a mitten

Waist 231->294mm and hips 224->336mm. The thighs hang 252mm apart and are 154mm across, so they span 407mm - the pelvis was 1.82x narrower than the legs sitting on it, and the waist cylinder was a 154mm pipe between a 385mm chest and those thighs. Chest:waist was 1.67 (comic-book V), now 1.31. Belt/hem/buckle widened to suit. Corrected an earlier test assertion too: it required the belt to be wider than the HIP, which was right only while curing the diaper - on a proportioned figure the hips are wider than the belt, so it now checks the belt against the waist it actually sits on, plus a new hip-vs-thigh-span check

Knee/elbow pads rebuilt as a hard shell on the FRONT of the joint with backing, boss, side wings and wrapping straps, after two attempts that read as compression braces. Needed a rig change: new faceBody gear flag plus orientFaceAnchors, which re-rolls a joint anchor every frame via Gram-Schmidt so its +Z tracks body-forward. Rule 3 (arbitrary joint roll) had been forcing 360-degree wraps, and a uniform tube IS the silhouette of a brace - the constraint was dictating the shape instead of being solved. Also learned twice on the way: a lathe is an OPEN shell so the first shaped cap had holes at both ends and rendered as a floating slab, and a pad built entirely in one dark role reads as a single blob however well shaped - the black shell needs a tan backing to show its edge

Pad straps fixed - as tan webbing 4mm proud of an olive trouser they were geometrically present and invisible; now black and 10mm proud. Plate carrier added (PLATE_CARRIER/withCarrier): front and back panels 33mm off the chest, shoulder straps, tan cummerbund at the ribs, four MOLLE webbing rows, metal buckle, and a name-tape patch in the team-tinted accent role so team ID lands on the chest at no extra cost. Needs no faceBody anchor since the torso has a stable front, unlike a joint

Human-scale assault pack added (SOLDIER_PACK/withPack): body, lid, side pouches, compression straps and a lashed bedroll, sitting on the carriers rear panel rather than on the body. The mechs existing packLarge/Medium/Small could not be reused - authored against a 0.360m-deep armoured chest they reach z=-0.490 and would hang 363mm off a 127mm-deep human torso. No shoulder straps of its own: the carriers already cross the trapezius and a second pair reads as a harness. withPads/withCarrier/withPack compose

Plate carrier chest pass from a four-angle critique. Shoulder strap was ONE 310mm-deep box on a 254mm-deep torso - it overhung 28mm each end and impaled the body front to back; replaced by a yoke plus two angled runs per side that each stop inside the panel they feed. Front panel split into a carrier base with the plate pocket stepped forward off it, since one flat slab read as a tablet bolted to the chest. Five vertical stitches added across the MOLLE rows - a horizontal bar array alone is a grille, only the perpendicular crossers say webbing. Cummerbund now closes at the front under the plate with the buckle on the band rather than floating mid-panel. Bedroll moved back and up off the shoulder line, where it had merged with the straps and read as absent

REVERTED the 21:25 plate-carrier chest pass at the users call. It fixed nothing: the vertical MOLLE stitches turned the panel into a waffle grid, and the shoulder strap was rebuilt from a numeric reach check (142mm vs a 163mm panel face) without ever confirming in the render that it stopped skewering the shoulder. Carrier back to 12 pieces. Lesson for the next attempt: the strap dimensions have to be derived from the chest they wrap - torso half-depth 127mm, half-width 193mm, panel face at 160mm - not chosen and then checked.

Plate carrier shoulder strap rebuilt from MEASURED torso geometry instead of chosen numbers. Sampled the torso mesh directly: it spans y -0.270..0.317 with max half-width 0.193, the arm root sits at x+-0.198 y0.216, and at x=0.105 the front surface falls 0.113 -> 0.089 -> 0.074 between y 0.21 and 0.30. That fall IS the shape of the path, so the strap is now an extrude with axis-x - a side profile arcing from the front panel face over a crest 9mm above the torso top to the back panel - rather than a 310mm box driven straight through a 254mm-deep chest. Thinned to 22mm and narrowed to 62mm at the users call.

High-cut bump helmet, sunglasses and face mask added to bot-face.js as independent head-kit lists (withHeadKit). Sized off the measured skull: the ears occupy y -0.027..0.019 so the shell stops at y 0.026, which is what makes it a high cut rather than a steel pot; the shell sits 10-25mm off the skull and carries a brim torus because a lathe has no end caps. New helmetRadius/helmetSurfaceZ exports so shell fittings (ARC rails, NVG shroud, rear pouch) clear the HELMET rather than the head. Sunglasses are TWO plates rotated 0.6rad about Y - the face falls 34mm from eye to temple, so any flat lens stands 46mm off the temples and reads as a welding visor - and use the pupil role, since visor is theme-driven and rendered amber

Helmet reshaped to the ACH reference after the first version read as a bicycle helmet. It was a lathe dome with a brow box and an occiput box bolted on - three objects, not a helmet. Now ONE continuous shell whose rim runs to y -0.022, below the ears at -0.027..0.019, so the lathe itself carries the whole silhouette (mid-cut). Shell z-stretch raised to 1.20, separate from the head 1.10, for 251mm fore-aft against a 199mm skull; matching the head stretch was most of the bicycle-helmet read. Added the two side bolts from the reference and moved the retention dial to the nape below the rim. Sunglasses lens role changed visor->pupil: visor is theme-driven and rendered amber.

Boom mic rebuilt as a connected five-piece chain (hinge boss on the cup face, two arms, elbow ball, capsule at the mouth corner). Both ends of the old single rod were floating: it started 13mm outside the cup rim and ended 54mm above the tip sphere, because a cylinder descriptor names its CENTRE and its axis is local +Y after rotation, so neither end appears in the source. Test now recomputes each link endpoints from its own descriptor and measures the gap to the previous link.

Body kind as a third design axis: BOT_BODY_KINDS/getBotBodyKind/setBotBodyKind behind botDesignForRole, picking the armoured mech or the clothed human soldier per role. Put behind that one function because both viewers already reach the art through it, so they cannot drift. Cache keyed by kind|role and deliberately NOT cleared on a switch, so toggling back reuses cached geometry. Added human-scale role markers (medic crosses, radio mast, launcher tubes) since BOT_DESIGN_ADDONS is authored against the mech 500x360mm chest; all are pack/carrier-mounted so the build guards on the role carrying one.

Wired the armoured/soldier switch into both viewers: a Body dropdown in env-viewer-v2 Combat Bots panel and a cycling Body button in bot-viewer-v2 Body & ragdoll, plus ?botBody=soldier on both. Added GhostRenderer.rebuildBotBodies() and rebuildBotProceduralBodies() because a procedural body reads its design once at construction, so live bots would otherwise keep the old body forever. Both reset bodyLastT/bodyLastPos so the rebuilt rig first frame does not see a multi-second dt.

Added SOLDIER_TEAM_BRASSARD, unconditional on every soldier role. A role histogram of the finished rifleman found shell and trim used ZERO times against 46 rubber pieces - uniform/face are per-body roles and the carrier/boots are untinted - so team identity came down to three plate pieces on the helmet. Band wraps each carrier strap crest in trim, which is both the vivid team role and the one botBodyStyle actually sets (accent is not, so the name tape is one colour on both teams).

New voice bank: loads sfx/voice manifest, spreads bots across an engine's speakers by seed, lazily fetches/decodes takes with a 6-way cap, falls back to the synth while warming; envAudio gains decodeAudio() because an AudioBuffer belongs to its own context.

Added a third Statistics tab, Symptoms: one row per bot, one column per named bug symptom from BB-001/002/003, all raw counts/ratios/booleans with no combined score and no visibility-gating thresholds (a bot with weak evidence still gets a small nonzero value instead of vanishing below a cutoff). Protocol-remediation pass per docs/sonnet-code-protocol.md: snapshotted current state to versions/ (bot-viewer-v2's snapshot is the last git commit, 2026-07-30, not a precise pre-session checkpoint -- noted as a limitation). Updated stale comments/UI text that assumed kills/hits could never populate in live mode.

Statistics panel: the bot selected on the map/sidebar/bot-viewer-v2's ctrl-click now highlights its row in the per-bot/Symptoms tables (reapplySelectedBotHighlight, DOM-patched like the existing stamp-selection reapply, wired into renderStats() and all four places `selected` changes). Fixed dead bots reading alive in the Statistics panel (user-reported, investigated by 3 independent haiku agents that converged on the same root cause, verified against the file). deathT used to mean 'first ever D row, latched once' -- broke in live mode because a viewer connecting mid-session only gets the last BOT_LIVE_BACKLOG rows, so an already-dead bot's first visible row got mistaken for a pre-existing corpse and never counted; separately, revived bots (revives counter already existed, D is not terminal) kept reading dead forever since nothing ever cleared deathT. Redefined death as CURRENT status: new shared scanDeathState(rows) walks backward from a bot's last row to find the start of its current D run (null if the last row isn't D); load() calls it once over the full sorted trace, ingestRow() keeps the same invariant incrementally (enter D sets deathT if unset, leave D clears it) without rescanning. Side effect fixes: deathsCaused no longer credits a kill for a death the victim recovered from, and the blind-death window now evaluates the bot's most recent death instead of always its first. takeMetrics()'s separate deaths counter (compare panel) deliberately left as a historical first-death-only count, a different question from current status.

Logged BB-004: user-reported and screenshot-confirmed bug where knife-committed (out-of-ammo) bots, disproportionately ones that became squad leader by succession, render airborne well above the terrain (body and weapon float together). Read bot-stance.js/weapon-hold-resolver.js/bot-entity.js/updateKnifeMovement to rule out the stance-height-blend system, stale stowed-weapon transforms, and nav-skipping knife-charge movement as causes; flagged mapCollider-vs-terrain desync (possibly via bot-structures.js scattered buildings whose 2D footprints get extruded/terrain-padded by an untraced caller path) as the leading open hypothesis. No runtime repro yet -- investigating, not fixed.

User pushed back that BB-004 (airborne bots) looked like the same bots as BB-001/002/003, which held up: built check-bot-elevation-gap.mjs to recover a bot's never-logged y indirectly (target_dist is a full 3D distance off the same capsule the logged x/z come from, so yGap = sqrt(target_dist^2 - xzDist^2) exposes it). Run against BB-002/003's own trace and today's session, found bot pairs diverging by 566m and 635m while both bots' logged x/z stayed normal and close -- the 635m case grows smoothly and monotonically over 5.7s, matching free-fall kinematics under bot-entity.js's GRAVITY=30 constant, not a one-frame glitch. Confirmed by hand with awk against the raw trace rows. Also proved the falling bot (bot-1578) never once entered BOT_KNIFE, falsifying the original knife-specific framing, and that it recovers normal XZ patrol behavior hours later while presumably still Y-broken (movement/pathing is XZ-only and never notices). Revised mechanism: entity.capsule.y occasionally diverges from ground truth (most likely stepBotPhysics gravity never re-latching onFloor=true) while x/z stay correct -- this alone explains BB-001-003's ghost-combatant/silent-proximity pattern (target_dist explodes past sightSq) AND BB-004's visual floating (mesh position is the same corrupted capsule's midpoint) as one bug, not two. Caught and fixed a dead-bot-heartbeat false-positive in the new checker (frozen post-death target_dist compared against a still-moving target's current position) before it produced a bogus BB-001 citation -- excluded dead rows to match check-bot-target-attribution.mjs's existing convention. Added update notes to BB-001/002/003 cross-linking the unification, with BB-001 explicitly flagged as not yet independently confirmed (its own two trace files don't show the smoking-gun-scale divergence).

User specifically asked whether ground-collision detection behaves differently based on knife-vs-gun. Checked two ways: (1) read map-collision.js's resolveCapsule/resolveOnce in full -- pure capsule-vs-BVH-triangle geometry, zero weapon/tool/state parameters or references anywhere in the file, confirmed via grep. stepBotPhysics passes none either. (2) Added --tol=N and a per-observer-FSM-state flag-rate tally to check-bot-elevation-gap.mjs, ran all 7 available trace files at --tol=30 (above the routine ~3-15m noise floor the default 3m catches on nearly every state). Knife came back clean across every file: 0/76 total severe (>30m) instances, while real severe anomalies concentrated in seek/cover-move/cover-hold/heal/flee. Conclusion: knife is very likely not implicated at all, structurally or empirically -- the knife/squad-leader/no-kills correlation in the original report is most likely pure survivorship bias (what an already-fallen, functionally unkillable bot looks like by the time it's noticed), not a property of the knife state. Documented as a dated update under BB-004.

Wired both viewers' voice call sites to the new intensity/variant system: sentry-cadence lines (firing/cover/moving/overwatch/reviving/no_ammo) read the already-cached alertTierLast for free; six lines that fire from outside the sentry tick (contact/man_down/enemy_down/grenade_out/sidearm/reloading) now call alertEscalation fresh via tierForScore instead of reading a stale cached tier, fixing a real bug where the event that triggered a line hadn't yet been folded into the tier it read. Added test-bot-voice-intensity.mjs (tierForScore ladder, tier-to-target anchors, alert floor, mutation-verified) and extended test-bot-voice.mjs (variant validation/auto-seed/fallback, picker nearest-match + epsilon round-robin + peek-without-commit, per-voice lexicon fallback, all mutation-verified). Bisected the sim spike by measurement instead of by suspicion: split the ?prof=1 HUD's sen phase into A perception / B alerts+cover / C state resolution / D movement (boundary timestamps, since the phases share locals and closures would break scope), then split D again per state handler plus the unconditional weapon/reload tail. First reading off a 20-sample OCR of a firefight recording: D is the entire spike (0.1-0.8ms quiet, 80.6ms peak, 94% of sen) while A stays flat at 0.8-3.3ms, which rules out perception and target selection; C has a smaller independent 6-9ms spike. Also documented that the HUD's sim/body/rnd are smoothed EMAs while these phases are raw, so a sub-phase reading higher than sim is the smoothing rather than a bug. Diagnostic scaffolding, to be removed once the D cost is fixed.

Added a Y-key per-frame perf log recorder to bot-viewer-v2 so spikes can be read directly instead of screen-recorded and OCR'd: Y starts a take, Y again stops it and copies a TSV of every phase timer to the clipboard, with a rising/falling WebAudio cue and a pulsing REC badge in the bottom-left hud row beside the fps counter. Samples after the render await and unsmoothed, unlike the 2Hz smoothed HUD text, and logs an unclamped frame interval because the loop's dt caps at 50ms and would hide the stalls. Own AudioContext rather than envAudio so the cue survives a muted mixer; off-screen staging textarea for the Ctrl+C fallback, blurred on a successful copy because the keydown listener ignores keys while a TEXTAREA has focus and would otherwise deaden every hotkey; 36000-row cap with the dropped count reported in the header.

First per-frame take reframed the whole perf investigation: cpu reconciles exactly with the phase timers but is only 33.8% of the frame, so 66.2% (median 39.2ms) is outside the animation loop entirely and dt correlates with cpu at just 0.42 - sim is 16.9% and senD 6.1%, meaning the phase we had been chasing is worth about 6% of a frame. Added gap (dt-cpu) and gpu columns to the recorder to tell GPU execute apart from browser render work, with trackTimestamp enabled under ?prof=1 since it is construction-only, guarded by try/catch as well as .catch because unsupported devices can throw synchronously inside the frame loop. Added a computed SUMMARY block (median/p90/max/share per phase, senD totals per state, worst 5 frames) and Shift+Y to copy the summary alone, since a per-frame table is too much to paste; rows are now stored as arrays rather than pre-joined strings so the summary can read columns back as numbers. Within senD the spiking states are seek and patrol, not flee.

Fixed a real bug in the perf recorder that the user's own take exposed: gap was dt minus the SAME row's cpu, but dt is the interval that ended when this frame started, so it pairs with the previous frame's cpu - a 116ms frame read as cpu116.2/dt16.9 followed by dt117.3/gap101.6, splitting a spike from its consequence across two rows. Also stopped clamping gap at zero, which had silently inflated the gap total (cpu and gap shares summed to 104.9% instead of 100%); negatives are legitimate because the loop is async and the browser can start a frame before the previous awaited tail finishes. Aggregate shares survived the bug since summing dt-cpu telescopes, but per-row values did not. Documented that gpu overlaps cpu rather than adding to it. Third measurement with GPU timestamps: cpu 18.9ms median (74.7% of frame) and gpu 18.4ms median against a 26.2ms frame, so there are two independent ceilings and 60fps needs both under 16.7ms; rnd command encoding (8.6ms) is larger than the whole AI sim (7.1ms); seek totals 880ms with a 0.6ms median, i.e. a hitch generator with 100ms single-frame stalls rather than an average-fps cost.

Armour far-LOD A/B says leave it off, and the same three takes relocate the combat cost entirely to the GPU. Turning the LOD on RAISED the gpu median 11.3->15.7ms and raised body 1.2->2.1 and rnd 8.1->9.2, because body-part-batches keys buckets on geometry.uuid and never removes them: swapping an rbox piece to its seg=1 twin adds a bucket instead of replacing one, so with both variants live the rbox bucket count roughly doubles and stats.draws rises with it - the LOD trades triangles for draw calls and loses at this bot count. Separately, the LOD-on no-fight vs fight pair (clean on the LOD axis) moves dt 17.6->26.7ms with gpu accounting for +8.3 and cpu only +1.8 while sim's median is identical at 4.8 in both, so combat's frame cost is render-side (flash lights, tracers, blast FX) and not the AI; next A/B is the bot-lighting toggles against gpu. Also noted cpu is already 15.5ms out of combat against a 16.7ms budget with rnd 8.6 of it, and that seek stalls (130.9ms max) are combat-only and untouched by the LOD.

Bot-lights A/B: three back-to-back takes under identical settings gave 28.9/50.0/29.8 fps with cpu constant at 11.7-12.3ms, so the entire spread lives in gap (18.9/5.8/19.2) and run-to-run variance now exceeds any code change we have measured - free-play A/B has hit its resolution limit and further comparisons need the seeded maze scenario (?autoprofile=1&proflayout=maze, mazeSeed 1337). What lights-off did buy is real and repeatable: rnd 8.6->5.1-5.4 and cpu 15.5->11.7-12.3, about 3.5ms of CPU per frame almost entirely in command encoding, though it did not reliably move fps because pacing decides that. dt medians cluster at 17.0 in the fast take vs 30.9/32.7/34.1 in the slow ones with cpu unchanged, which is the shape of frame pacing rather than workload - recorded as the leading explanation, not proven, since take 3's 24-26ms rows do not fit a clean 60Hz ladder. Also flagged that the lights-off fight take (24.8fps, gpu 28.0) is not a regression: it ran 46s vs 16.8s with the roster falling 48->38 and sits inside the demonstrated spread.

Sixth measurement on the smaller maps settles the pacing question: dt clusters hard at 16.6-16.9 and 33.2-33.7 with almost nothing between, which is a 60Hz vsync ladder, so the fifth measurement's pacing reading is now confirmed rather than inferred and the 28.9/50.0/29.8 spread was frames tipping between the two rungs. Mean dt 22.4ms means roughly two thirds of frames land on 60 and one third on 30. That makes cpu's 15.6ms median against a 16.7ms budget the whole story - the CPU is sitting right on the line, so savings there pay off nonlinearly by moving frames down a rung; inside it rnd is 7.3 (47%), sim 4.6 (29%), body 2.5 (16%), and command encoding is both the biggest item and the mechanism that made the armour far-LOD backfire. gap collapsed 19->2.6ms, which restores free-play A/B viability. The seek stalls are gone: senD max 14.4 vs 124.4ms, p90 1.3 vs 9.9, seek total 252ms (1.6%) vs 3635ms (7.9%). Caveat recorded: the roster halved 48->25 in the same change, so map size and bot count are confounded - the seek result is very likely map size (shorter floodFill), the gap and cpu results could be either.

Added a Log tab to the trace viewer's Statistics panel (user request): full chronological state-change log, working for both a loaded file and a live session, filterable by team/squad/role and 'only selected bot'. The existing floating Log panel was live-only (load() never populated it) and unfiltered; factored its event definition (changed slot present, not 'tick') into isLogEvent()/logRowBits() so both panels agree, then added structured logEntries (not pre-joined text) built once per load via buildLogEntries() -- allRows is only ever sorted per-bot, not globally, so this does its own time sort -- and appended incrementally in ingestRow() for live, capped at LOG_MAX_LINES like the floating panel; a loaded file gets no cap since 'full contents of a saved log' means everything. Filter dropdowns reuse the sidebar teamSel/fillTeamFilter 'rebuilt on load, keep selection if still valid' idiom. 'Only selected bot' reuses the app's single existing selected variable instead of a new bot picker, so the three places that set it (map click, sidebar click, live ctrl-click from bot-viewer-v2) now also call renderStats() so the tab updates live when open. Log rows carry no data-row/data-key/data-id, so groupBy/leaderMode/stamping all hide on this tab -- chronological order is the point, not a sortable stat grid.

BB-004 forensic capture: everything shipped so far detects the below-terrain fall and papers over it, but nothing recorded WHY the capsule crosses the sheet, so the trigger is still unidentified. New bot-forensics.js is a pure THREE-free ring recorder (1024 samples per bot over one preallocated 6.29 MB ArrayBuffer, nothing allocated per frame) behind a fourth opt-in stepBotPhysics option, forensics. The sample is taken INSIDE stepBotPhysics because that is the only place preY, the integrated velocity.y before the rescue zeroes it, the raw contact.grounded before the rescue forces onFloor true, and the already-computed ground reference all coexist - sampling from the caller would need a second ground-height call per bot per frame and would lose both pre-rescue values. state_key and t go through the Int32 view deliberately: the packed FSM key maxes at 43,679,999 and float32 is exact only to 2^24, so the float view would silently corrupt reachable state combinations (test case 6 exists to fail that refactor). bot-viewer-v2 records every live bot and dummy continuously from its first physics step - NOT gated on having fallen before, since a first fall would otherwise be the one case with no lead-up - freezes the whole ring into a preallocated 48 KB snapshot on any rescue (first unexported rescue wins, exporting re-arms), names the waiting bot in the #floorwarn banner, and copies it as TSV on Shift+J (plain J unchanged; Shift+J had no prior binding). Export derives gap and ext_dy, the column that separates the three candidate mechanisms: a dt spike means single-frame tunnelling, a nonzero ext_dy means the pair-pushout re-resolve moved the capsule, x/z clustering means a mesh seam. ?forensics=0 is the kill switch and the A/B control arm; the in-browser perf validation is documented for the project owner to run and was NOT measured here.

Added draws/tris (renderer.info.render.drawCalls/.triangles) to the Y perf log, because every remaining disagreement in the perf investigation was about draw-call count and eight review agents all estimated it instead of measuring it. Counts not ms, no ?prof=1 needed, and they cover the post chain as well as the scene. Read after the render await, which is correct because the renderer resets these at the top of the animation loop before the frame callback runs. Appended at the end of the row rather than slotted next to rnd: perfLogSummary indexes rows positionally, so a mid-row insert would silently re-point every line() call. Summary gets its own median/p90/max/min line for them (share-of-frame is meaningless for a count) and draws joins the worst-5-frames list. The point is the pairing - rnd is command encoding, so a change that cuts rnd without cutting draws did not win on draw count.

Consolidated two waves of eight review agents into a verified findings list for planning. Every load-bearing claim was re-checked against source by hand before inclusion, which mattered: eight agent claims were wrong and are recorded in a Disproven section rather than deleted, including the biggest one (that awaiting renderAsync serialises CPU and GPU, refuted by renderAsync being just await init() plus a synchronous render, by cpu being sampled after the await, and by measured dt of 18.7ms against a predicted 31). Confirmed and newly found: effect-renderer.js builds 480 individually-materialled sprites across two blend modes so transparent sorting alternates pipelines; the rig is ~57k triangles a bot (~1.4M at 25) per the code's own comment, and the existing seg=1 LOD twin failed only because buckets are never evicted, so it is blocked on lifecycle rather than being a dead end; renderer construction stacks MSAA, devicePixelRatio and PCFSoftShadowMap as three one-line fill-rate levers; physics and collision are ungated by the think stagger; frameProf.beginFrame() is exported but never called, so any conditionally-run timer carries the previous frame's value forward, which is a defect in the instrument judging everything else. Also recorded nine clean bills so they are not re-investigated. Ends with an A/B sequence that needs no new code, gated on fixing beginFrame first.

Fixed a gap two independent Sonnet reviews of the BB-004 forensic-capture change both found: forensicStateKey was only ever stamped from inside botStateDescriptor, which was reachable only through botStateRecording-gated call paths (default off), so a user reacting to the #floorwarn banner with Shift+J -- the feature's core reactive workflow -- got state_key=-1 on every row unless they had separately turned on state recording first. commitBotActor (the single per-live-bot-per-frame commit point) now calls botStateDescriptor unconditionally, below the botStateRecording gate rather than through it; the function does no allocation or DOM work so this stays cheap, and traceBotStateCode's own downstream call is left as accepted redundant recomputation when recording is on rather than restructured away. test-bot-forensics.mjs (81/0) and test-bot-entity-rescue.mjs (34/0) unaffected since the fix lives entirely in bot-viewer-v2.html's viewer-only commitBotActor, not in the Node-tested modules; browser verification that state_key now populates with recording off is not yet done.

Authored the perf remediation plan from the verified findings list, partitioned into two file-disjoint workstreams (shared modules vs bot-viewer-v2.html) so two agents can implement concurrently without colliding, with four landing-order-safe seam contracts so neither side blocks on the other. Planning turned up three corrections to the findings doc: frameProf.beginFrame zeroes only DEFAULT_NAMES, which are the environment viewer's pass names, so calling it would have been a no-op for this app and the fix needs a frame-profiler semantic change rather than one line; effect-renderer is consumed by four apps not two; and the unbudgeted floodFill is at line 7708, not 7677. Also recorded a tension the earlier LOD post-mortem missed - a per-distance rbox LOD inherently runs both seg variants at once while the population is mixed, so bucket eviction alone cannot keep draw count flat and only a global switch can. Phases 2-4 are gated behind owner-run STOP/MEASURE points because their magnitudes are still estimates; only phases 0 and 1 were released to the implementers.

Phase 0-A: beginFrame() now zeroes every recorded CPU/GPU timer name instead of only the environment viewer defaults so bot-viewer-v2 stops reading stale values for phases that skip a frame; smoothed maps left alone so the HUD EMA still decays.

Phase 0-B of the perf remediation plan: made the instrument trustworthy and installed the A/B levers the measurement sequence needs. frameProf.beginFrame() is now the first statement of the animation loop, so a phase that does not run on a frame will report 0 instead of silently carrying the previous frame value forward (it is a no-op until Workstream A changes beginFrame to zero every recorded name rather than only the environment viewer DEFAULT_NAMES, and either landing order is safe). Added ?dpr=<n>, ?msaa=0 and ?shadowfilter=pcfsoft|pcf|basic at the WebGPURenderer construction site, all defaulting to exactly the previous behaviour: antialias is construction-only so it can never be an in-game toggle, which is the whole reason the fill-rate arms could not be run before. The shadow lookup uses ?? rather than || because BasicShadowMap is 0 and || would have fallen back to PCFSoft for precisely the cheapest arm. devicePixelRatio now goes to the console at boot and into a second perfLogHeader line together with the real render buffer ratio, msaa and shadow filter, since fill cost scales with the square of the pixel ratio and that unknown made takes from different machines incomparable. No PERF_LOG_COLS change - header text only, so perfLogSummary positional indexing is untouched.

Phase 1-B of the perf remediation plan: five confirmed structural fixes in the viewer, no visual default changed. updateNavPathLine writes a preallocated 256-point Float32Array in place with addUpdateRange/setDrawRange instead of disposing and rebuilding a BufferGeometry plus N Vector3s every frame; it is off at defaults, so the point is GC pauses tipping frames on a 60 Hz vsync ladder rather than a measured win. FOV wedge geometry is memoized per rounded degree in a shared Map, which also required removing the fovWedge.geometry.dispose() in disposeBotActor - that call would now pull a shared geometry out from under every other living bot. botVoiceIdentities entries are released on actor teardown, safe because voiceIdentity is deterministic from the id. box(), instancedBoxes() and the terrain mesh set matrixAutoUpdate=false plus one updateMatrix() since applyLayout rebuilds rather than moves. The unbudgeted floodFill in choosePatrolResumeGoal now charges 4 units of REPLAN_BUDGET_PER_FRAME and respects nextReplanAt; because finishInvestigation is its only caller and is never re-entered, a swallowed refusal would have quietly downgraded the bot to patrolPoints[patrolIdx] - often a waypoint behind it - so refusal parks a patrolResumePending flag on the actor and updatePatrolMovement retries next think tick, with a served call clearing the flag either way so a genuine no-reachable-point answer terminates. maxRadius was deliberately not used: the flood band is an axis-aligned box around the start, so any radius small enough to save work can clip a route that detours outside it, and a radius large enough to keep every patrol point reachable is the whole grid.

Added a raycast() capability to body-part-batches.js and two new real effect kinds (blood_spray, blood_splatter) to entity-types/effect.js and effect-renderer.js, then built damage-simulator.html, a standalone single-bot harness (og/armored/human-soldier variants via composeBot) for click-to-fire or random-shot hit-effect tuning against the real bot rig and entity lifecycle, so a later combat wire-up is a spawn call, not a new code path.

Phase 1-A: WeakMap geometry->bucket fast path (kills ~3150 uuid string Map.get per frame in the rig flush) plus bucket lifecycle - empty buckets hide in endFrame and evict from scene and both maps after 120 flushed empty frames without ever disposing the shared geometry so a body-LOD swap becomes subtractive; also repaired the test fake THREE (Matrix4/Matrix3) that the earlier raycast() addition had left throwing.

Hardened the new geometry fast path with an evicted flag on retired buckets so a WeakMap entry that outlives its bucket (or survives dispose) misses instead of resurrecting a mesh already pulled from the scene; covered by an add-after-dispose test.

Carried Workstream A's handoff note into bots.md, which A could not write itself under the file-ownership split, and un-staled B's 'no-op until A lands' caveat now that both halves of the beginFrame fix have landed. Added the ordering consequence the split surfaced: the HUD reads the smoothed snapshot that beginFrame never touches and perfLogSample reads unsmoothed after the render await, so both see real values, but any future unsmoothed snapshot placed before the timed work would read zeros. Also recorded A's correction to the plan's seam contract 2a - at r0.184 an InstancedMesh with count===0 already issued no draw call, so hiding an empty bucket saves render-list and bind-group work in rnd but does not move the draws column; eviction is the part that fixes the LOD backfire arithmetic.

Split the single blood_splatter decal into blood_stain (small high-opacity decal at the wound, tuned down from a big blob) and a new blood_splatter (ground decals at each spray droplet's own resolved ballistic landing point via a numerically-verified time-of-flight solve against injected terrain height, instead of stuck to the body); also retuned blood_spray defaults to high-count/small-droplet/mid-speed/mid-high-spread per user feedback in the damage simulator.

Added a sub30 line to the Y perf-log summary because the owner's actual goal is not mean fps but never sitting below 30 for any considerable time, and median fps cannot express that. Reports frames over 33.3ms with a percentage plus the LONGEST CONSECUTIVE RUN and its duration - the run is the part that matters, since scattered single frames are invisible while a held stretch is what reads as a stall. 33.3ms is the 60Hz ladder's second rung, so this is a rung-crossing count rather than an arbitrary threshold. It also survives the run-to-run variance that made median fps useless here: three identical takes previously gave 28.9/50.0/29.8 fps with cpu constant.

Phase 3-B: rboxlod becomes a 0/1/2 mode with a new global step (?rboxlod=2 plus a Global position on the panel button) that puts every bot on the seg=1 rbox twin. A per-distance LOD is additive by construction - mixed populations keep both seg variants live - so it lost its earlier A/B; a global switch is substitutive, so the seg=3 buckets empty and Workstream A bucket eviction removes them, which is what makes tris fall without draws rising. Applied in botCullBegin rather than botFlushSkipped so the camera/debug focus actors swap too, and leaving global walks every body back to seg=3 so no focus bot strands on the cheap twin. Default stays off: the twin flattens chamfer highlights, which is the owner aesthetic call. perfLogHeader now names the live rboxlod arm so takes self-identify (header text, no PERF_LOG_COLS change).

Phase 2-A: the two 220/260-slot sprite pools become two instanced draws. Previously every visible puff was its own THREE.Sprite with its own SpriteNodeMaterial, so a firefight encoded hundreds of transparent draws with hundreds of bind groups, and the two blend modes made Three alternate pipelines while walking its sorted transparent list. Now each pool is one Mesh over an InstancedBufferGeometry with instPos/instColor/instSize/instAlpha and instanceCount = live sprites, uploaded once per frame exactly like the existing line/point buffers. The plan prescribed instanceMatrix + instanceColor; that does not work - SpriteNodeMaterial.setupPositionView builds the vertex from positionNode plus positionGeometry and never reads positionLocal, so an InstancedMesh instanceMatrix has no effect on where a billboard lands at r0.184. Per-instance data therefore rides on the material nodes instead, which also drops the dead identity matrix (16 floats and a mat4 multiply per instance) that the prescribed layout would have carried. Smoke IS sorted: normal blending is order-dependent and instancing gives up Three per-sprite depth sort, so smoke is written to staging buffers and gathered back-to-front, with the camera taken from onBeforeRender (last frame - one frame stale, and it keeps the API frozen with no camera parameter). Glow is additive and order-independent so it is never sorted. API unchanged, so all five consumer apps need zero wiring changes.

Recorded two corrections the Phase 2-A implementation surfaced. BLOOD_POOL still carries finding 1's defect in a worse form - 160 individual transparent DoubleSide quads with no forceSinglePass, so Three renders each twice for up to 320 draws; it is free in bot-viewer-v2 because the bots are robots but is a live cost in damage-simulator and environment-viewer, so it was correctly out of Phase 2-A's scope rather than missed. Also fixed the consumer count for effect-renderer.js, which this doc got wrong twice: five live consumers, not two as first written or four as the plan said, with damage-simulator the only one exercising the blood kinds and therefore the one whose QA the API freeze was actually protecting.

Wired the damage-simulator hit-FX stack (hit_spark + blood_spray + blood_stain + blood_splatter) into every damaging hit in the v2 harness, as a compatibility proof before any further decal work. Zero new imports - the harness was already running effect-renderer.js for blasts. Three details drove the shape: colour must be passed explicitly because pushEffect writes a raw wire object and never runs EffectEntity.create(), so the blood-kind default would not apply and blood renders orange; there are three damage sites not one (applyBotDamage, the applyCombatDamage dummy branch, detonateBlast's victim loop), and detonateBlast calls neither applyBotDamage nor emitBotDamaged, which is why the more decoupled onBotDamaged subscription was rejected; and the spray normal needs a second reference point, because bot capsules are strictly vertical and every non-bullet path passes a hit point taken from the victim's own capsule, so dx/dz are exactly zero and the naive capsule normal degenerates to straight up on every knife kill. Bullets thread resolveHitscan's real normal through source.normal; knife falls back to the attacker, blast to source.origin. Blood FX toggle under Body & ragdoll (not Explosives - it fires on bullets and knives too), saved as bloodFx via boolOr. effect-renderer.js deliberately untouched: BLOOD_POOL's 160 DoubleSide quads saturate around 22 concurrent hits and growing it would have grown the exact pattern Phase 2-A exists to remove. Splatter count cut 10 to 6 caller-side instead; the ceiling is left in place as the thing this pass is meant to measure.

Phase 2-B: the blood decal pool becomes the third instanced draw, closing the defect Phase 2-A left behind. It was maxBloodDecals separate Mesh + MeshBasicMaterial pairs, DoubleSide with no forceSinglePass, so a saturated pool encoded up to 2x that many transparent draws - free while only damage-simulator exercised blood, no longer free now that bot-viewer-v2 spawns it on every hit. The constraint that shaped Phase 2-A does NOT apply here: MeshBasicNodeMaterial builds its vertex from positionLocal, which positionNode replaces, so per-instance geometry is expressible. Still no instanceMatrix - each instance carries its two in-plane axes pre-scaled by size (instTan/instBit) and the corner is centre + geomX*tan + geomY*bit, which is 6 floats and no matrix multiply against 16 floats and a mat4. The basis needs a helper axis that swaps to +X on near-vertical normals or the cross product collapses on ground splatter, which is every blood_splatter quad. Alpha comes from an explicit texture(softTex).a rather than riding materialColor, since the soft ramp is the only thing feathering the decal edge. Not depth-sorted unlike smoke: decals lie flush on solid geometry so overlap is coplanar, and they are all the same dark red. Cap moves 160 to a maxBloodDecals option defaulting to 512, additive so all five consumers are unchanged. Motivation is not perf tidying - bleedout drips and growing blood pools are persistent decal producers, so one bot bleeding for 20 s would have blown a 160 cap alone.
Splatter count back to the wire default 10 now that the decal pool is instanced and capped at 512; it had been cut to 6 only to buy headroom against the old 160.

Added six new voice-line events (spawn, hit, grenade_hit, near_miss, ally_hit, death), wired to real signals already in the code rather than new tracking: hit/grenade_hit split on applyCombatDamage's existing cause field ('bullet' vs 'blast'), near_miss hooks the existing near-miss report write (_nmVisit), ally_hit mirrors man_down's witness scan but off non-fatal onBotDamaged, death fires from the victim itself inside the existing onBotDied casualty handler, spawn fires at the end of each per-bot spawn path. death's lines are pure vocalizations (AAAGH, NOOO, wordless gasps) rather than phrases, since a death cry is a reflex not communication, per explicit user correction after an initial draft used narrated lines like 'I'm hit' for a fatal event; hit/grenade_hit similarly mix wordless pain reactions with tactical follow-through rather than always narrating the wound. All six landed in the existing alertTier-driven intensity path (VOICE_INTENSITY_FRESH_LINES) rather than a new HP-fraction-driven one - reusing the mechanism the other 13 lines already have was simpler and sufficient. New rhythms required real rework after the first pass: five of six landed inside already-crowded 2/3/4-syllable duration clusters (test-bot-voice.mjs's pooled MIN_RHYTHM_DISTANCE check caught it), and two (hit, grenade_hit) were shorter than grenade_warn, which an existing assertion requires to be the shortest line in the lexicon. Full authored per-intensity-band wording (table drafted in chat, low/mid/high per event) is not yet baked into sound-params.json's voiceLexicon - only the single neutral base line shipped in code; the bulk-bake pass (bake-intensity-variants.mjs-style) is still pending for these six.

Baked all six 2026-08-05 reaction lines (spawn, hit, grenade_hit, near_miss, ally_hit, death) for all 10 ElevenLabs voices via new bake-reaction-lines.mjs (420 lines, 0 failed) - same single-pass pattern as bake-intensity-variants.mjs, kept as a separate script since these lineIds had zero prior customization. Also made four of the six (hit, grenade_hit, near_miss, death - the involuntary reflex/pain reactions, not ally_hit/spawn which are deliberate radio chatter) always play clean and positional regardless of the radio toggle, net-team flat playback, or the chattiness dial, per explicit user correction: 'someone wouldnt cut their radio on the make a death sound.' Chattiness required three separate exemptions in bot-voice-director.js, not one - the top-level chattiness<=0 mute, the squad/global rate buckets (which independently scale their max to zero at chattiness 0), and cooldownScale() (which stretches cooldowns at low-but-nonzero chattiness) - the first fix alone still left reflex lines silenced via the rate buckets, caught by a new test rather than assumed fixed. New REFLEX_LINES export in bot-voice.js is the single source of truth both the director and both viewers read, rather than duplicating the four-line list.

New materials subsystem: four portable TSL material demos (dissolve, hologram-visor, damage-overheat, foliage-sss) behind a single create()/handle contract, plus material-viewer.html as a demo loader and a Node contract suite (138 assertions, 0 failing). Demos import only three/three-webgpu/three-tsl and never touch the DOM or a scene, so the viewer and the game consume the identical module; the viewer's Port tab generates the paste snippet from the current tuning. Sourced from a 5-agent survey whose API claims were then checked against the shipped r0.184 build rather than trusted - three failed: curlNoise() does not exist (asserted independently by two agents, one of which had built a proposed material on it), fbm/hexTile/textureGrad are likewise absent, and the post-fx nodes (bloom/ao/dof/fsr1) live in three/addons/tsl/display/ not three/tsl, so one agent's UnrealBloomPass recommendation was the wrong pipeline entirely (post-fx.js:10 already uses the TSL bloom node). The survey's two top-ranked ideas (iridescent + anisotropic bot shells, priced at 2-4h each) were dropped after reading body-part-batches.js:29-48: the instanced bot rig is plain MeshStandardMaterial, not a NodeMaterial at all, so those need a MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial migration of the exact path that measured 37fps at 90 bots - a perf project, not a material task. All four shipped demos therefore stay off that path. Two TSL traps hit during authoring and recorded in the docs: Discard() silently does nothing unless recorded inside an Fn() body, and mx_fractal_noise_float's octave count is a shader loop bound so it is baked via a new meta.rebuildOn convention instead of exposed as a uniform. Viewer follows the tree/plant-viewer 3D shell plus environment-viewer's in-game panel language (wui tokens, vertical tab rail), deliberately omitting backdrop-filter per the perf note in environment-ui.js. No GPU frame measurements taken and nothing wired into the game yet; both stated as open in the write-up.

Added a click-to-place test marker (ground raycast against a y=0 plane, height read from groundHeight/terrainField) behind a new Place Marker button: arm it, click the map, a floating octahedron drops at that point and follows terrain height. Deliberately minimal first step of a squad-orders exploration (see plan file) -- no team/order/persistence logic yet, just proving the ground-click mechanic before reusing it for base placement and point-directed squads.
Corrected the blood-pool note: Phase 2-A did instance the decal pool (forceSinglePass added), and the blood kinds are live in bot-viewer-v2 by default rather than confined to the damage simulator.

Added reflex range/volume sliders: REFLEX_LINES (hit/grenade_hit/near_miss/death) were audible across most of the map because playBotVoice reused the same wide-range panner profile and volume as ordinary radio chatter. Both viewers now carry a separate mutable REFLEX_SFX_VOICE panner (ref 2.5m/max 12m/rolloff 2.5, live-tunable, not routed through SOUND_PARAMS.ranges) and botReflexVolume, selected in playBotVoice when REFLEX_LINES.has(lineId); sayBotLine/sayBestBotLine also pre-filter reflex requests against botReflexRange before calling the director, since the director stamps a line's cooldown the moment it grants a request and release() on a culled/silent playback does not undo that stamp -- letting an inaudible far-away reflex request through would have quietly burned that line's cooldown for a hit nobody heard. Also fixed a pre-existing duplicate 'chattiness' key/statement in bot-viewer-v2.html's settings save/restore block while touching that code.

Conforming blood stains phase 1: new bot-body-hit.js resolves a shot to a per-part surface hit and a stable attachment handle, blood_stain gains an optional attach field resolved through an injected resolveAttachment (same pattern as terrainHeight) so a stain rides the bot instead of hanging in mid-air, and the decal pool gets an irregular seeded mask because the old radial one made the per-decal spin a visual no-op.

Harness could show neither defect it was meant to judge: added a pace toggle (its bot never moved) and a capsule/parts/mesh hit-source toggle (its click-to-fire was already more accurate than production hitscan).

selectBotTarget now picks by risk (proximity x danger, danger decaying over the report window instead of cliffing) instead of nearest, with the stickiness margin converted from a distance ratio to a risk ratio to match; added an ally-threat pile-on discount via existing squadMembersNear so a squad does not dogpile one shooter while other visible enemies go unanswered (self-threat is unaffected, already self-filtered)

Fixed thigh decals flipping to the far side of the leg on a 180 turn: placeSegment oriented limbs with the shortest-arc rotation, which carries no roll, so a near-vertical bone got a near-identity frame regardless of body facing and its local frame was world-locked. Same solve now runs in body space and is rotated by the body orientation - rigid with the body, invisible on the mesh since limb geometry is a lathe about Y with equal X/Z scale.

Phase 2 Mode A: stains sized from the hit part's cross-section (new partCrossSection) instead of a fixed 0.15m, which measured 1.6x the width of a forearm and 0.6x of the torso. Also made pushBlood's surface lift a parameter - the flat 1cm was over a tenth of a forearm's width, so stains hovered off the body; blood_stain now scales it to its own size and ground splatter keeps 1cm.

Phase 2 of the squad-orders exploration: ctrl-click-selecting a bot (existing selectedBotActor, previously purely visual) now also arms it for direction -- placing a marker while a bot is selected sends that bot to the marker via a new updateCommandMovement, wired into the out-of-combat dispatch ahead of formation/medic-cohesion so an explicit command overrides passive follow behavior until it arrives, then falls through to whatever the bot would normally do. Selecting a squad leader drags the whole squad for free since followers already track the leader's live position, not this dispatch choice. Note: skipped the versions/ pre-edit snapshot this round (edited before remembering to back up) -- prior state is still recoverable via git and the phase-1 snapshot, but flagging the process miss rather than fabricating a before-copy.

Phase 3 of the squad-orders exploration: replaced the phase-2 armed-button marker flow with an RTS-style control scheme -- plain left-click on a bot now also selects it (selectedBotActor, previously only set by ctrl-click), and right-click on the map opens a small floating context menu (Move here / Hold here) at the cursor, dismissed by clicking away, pressing Escape, or issuing a command. Move is the existing arrive-then-clear behavior from phase 2 (combat pre-empts movement elsewhere and does not clear the command, so a fight en route is not a cancellation). New Hold mode adds a commandMode flag to updateCommandMovement: on arrival it does not clear commandGoal/commandTargetId, so the bot parks indefinitely at that exact point -- proto-defense, since it still fights on contact (higher-priority FSM branch, untouched) but returns to holding afterward instead of resuming patrol. Marker color now reflects the live order (amber=move, cyan=hold) for feedback at a glance. Removed the now-redundant Place marker button/panel section.

Added a third right-click command -- Double time here -- alongside Move/Hold: adds a doubleTime ctx flag to bot-stance.js chooseBotStance that forces STANCE_RUN for a bot in the patrol state (only patrol
column5: so it cannot fight the aim/seek crouch table or any higher-priority rung; 6 new Node assertions cover ordering against forcedCrouch/holding/seek/aim)
column6: then wires it in bot-viewer-v2.html as commandMode==='run' -- true for the directly commanded bot AND any live squadmate (looked up via squadId
