Arrival behavior matches move (clears and resumes default) since run is just move plus a stance override; marker now shows a third color (orange) for the live order.

summary: Bots walked jerky and puppet-like because the gait scheduler is purely reactive -- feet wait for a trigger distance then snap through a swing, so nothing above the ankles knows a stride is happening (no arm swing, square hips, feet flat to the ground normal, bob that collapses to zero in double support). Added body-locomotion.js: a THREE-free cyclic pose layer that derives a stride phase FROM the scheduler own footfalls (left lift pins phase 0, right 0.5, stride period measured from alternating lifts, corrections bled in rather than snapped) and emits contralateral arm swing, pelvis roll/yaw, counter-rotating shoulders, speed-scaled torso lean, continuous two-dip bob/sway, and heel-strike/toe-off ankle pitch. Companion GAIT_DEFAULTS.stepOverlap lets the trailing foot lift before the leading one lands, removing the plant-pause-plant cadence. Ships OFF (naturalLocomotion false, stepOverlap 0) so env-viewer and bot-viewer are untouched; body-preview.html is the tuning harness and turns it on with full sliders plus a Movement dynamics toggle it was previously missing. Split _pelvisQ (mesh, inherits the prone blend) from _hipQ (sockets, stay upright) so prone hips do not move. 28 new Node assertions; continuity is tested by quadrupling the frame rate rather than by delta magnitude, since a 0.62 rad swing legitimately moves ~0.07 rad per frame at 60 Hz.

Verified the new locomotion layer against the two bot render paths before it gets switched on there, rather than assuming portability: instanced bodies are fine because body-part-batches flush uploads part.matrixWorld (the ankle rotation rides along with every other pose change), and bot-viewer-v2 rig LOD striding is fine because the stride phase is locked to lift events rather than free-running, so a coarser sampling grid gives a bounded error instead of drift -- measured ~3% of a cycle at 60 Hz, ~7% at 30 Hz (>18 m), ~13% at 15 Hz (>45 m). Promoted the LOD check from a throwaway script into 4 permanent assertions (32 total).

Phase 2 Mode C: GPU depth-projected stain decals. A box reads viewportDepthTexture to recover the world position of whatever solid surface is behind each fragment and paints only inside its own bounds, so the decal wraps instead of floating. Wired as a third stain size-mode with a project-depth slider and a debug view that paints reconstructed world position as a 1m colour grid - the MSAA/PostProcessing depth-sampling risk cannot be checked without a GPU, so the debug view is how it gets checked. Stains are withheld from fx.sync while Mode C owns them, at the call site, so the frozen sync signature is untouched.

Catalogued every section and control in bot-viewer-v2's #ctrl panel (29 sections, ~330 controls, ordered by write date), then had three independent agents propose an information architecture from the same brief to test for convergence. All three landed on tabs plus a persistent zone, and independently agreed on six specifics: pull the 6 perf/LOD toggles out of Bot controls, consolidate POV debug widgets/markers + Squad overlay + Nav grid into one overlay card, promote the three buried scenario presets, split the ~53-control Visuals card at its existing subheads, keep the terrain pipeline order, and keep the label-carries-state toggle idiom. Approved structure: 6 tabs (Session/Bots/World/Debug/Visuals/Audio) with roster-before-tuning ordering, pinned camera+readout+search, no advanced disclosures. Design only -- no panel code changed yet.

Rebuilt the v2 control panel from one flat 29-card column into 6 tabs plus pinned chrome, per the approved IA. The enabling change is an inversion: SECTION_PLAN declares every card up front in display order and header() now only re-points ctrl at an already-built body, so ~2900 lines of control-building code keep their file order while the panel renders in a different one -- and two parking arrays let a card be assembled from several places without moving code. Consolidations all three review agents reached independently: 6 perf/LOD toggles out of the spawn card into a Perf/LOD card, every overlay toggle (POV widgets/markers, squad overlay, nav grid) into one Debug overlays card, the 3 buried scenario presets promoted to a World strip, the ~55-control Visuals card split on its own .ttl markers into 4, Map layout + Maze structure merged. Added search, ★ jump-chip pinning (no DOM moves, so collapse-state restore still works), and a compact class; ui slots gained activeTab/pinned/compact and read section state from ctrlRoot so the pinned readout is included. New static test locks the plan (31 checks) since the panel cannot run in Node.

Split the point-command menu's flat commandMode ('move'|'hold'|'run') into two orthogonal toggles: commandGoalState ('move'|'hold', arrive-and-resume vs. arrive-and-park) and commandDoubleTime (a plain movement-style boolean), so all four combinations are reachable -- previously double-time-then-hold couldn't be expressed since 'run' and 'hold' were mutually exclusive. The right-click menu now has an independent Double time checkbox (persists across openings, doesn't close the menu or require a point) above the Move here/Hold here goal buttons; marker color gained two more states (move+run, hold+run) to show both axes at a glance. updateCommandMovement's arrival branch and the sc.doubleTime stance-ctx computation now read the two separate variables instead of one enum; bot-stance.js and test-bot-stance.mjs needed no changes since the doubleTime ctx flag was already style-only (203 checks still green).

Fixed sniper bots firing into the sky: the FSM confirmed the shot on the entity's yaw/pitch but the round left down the RENDERED barrel, and nothing forced them to agree at the instant of the shot. updateBotWeaponMount is the only thing that ever puts pitch on the weapon rig (the rig itself gets yaw-only Euler), it runs after updateBotSentry in the frame, and it skips its solve while carrying, mid-reload, and on rig-LOD frames (every 2nd past 18 m, every 4th past 45 m) -- so shots followed whatever pose the gun was last left in. An unsolved m24 hold sits ~6 deg high, a near miss at 20 m and a visible skyward tracer at 200 m; the m24's magazineSize 1 makes every sniper shot a first-shot-after-a-2s-reload, the longest unsolved window. fireBotShot now solves the barrel onto botAimPoint before reading it; BOT_COVER_MOVE/BOT_COVER_HOLD/MEDIC_MOVE/MEDIC_TEND joined the mount's aiming set (the first two fire at STANCE_RUN, i.e. down a walk carry pointing 67 deg right and 17 deg down); and botHasAimPoint is now cleared when the target dies, having previously been set true and never false. New source-parsing test locks all four invariants -- it fails 4/4 against the pre-fix snapshot in versions/.

Grenade evade now takes cover and holds until the blast; added evadeExitScale hysteresis so bots stop chattering across the ring edge, and a post-blast aim settle so they no longer snap back into combat the frame it detonates.

Closed the "not all settings save" gap. Audited every persistent let the panel reassigns against the text of all three capture functions: eight controls were never captured, and they shared one cause -- the capture functions enumerate fields by hand, so a control added without a matching line works and silently isn't saved. All six Perf / LOD toggles (think stagger, rig LOD, flush LOD, behind-camera cull, body hide, armour LOD) were missing because they began as ?riglod=0-style URL flags and were never treated as panel settings; the tab refactor gathering them into one card is what made it legible as a whole section not saving. Also fixed: hit-volume overlay and the recorder's trace tick. Armour LOD restore repeats the button's own order (walk bodies back to full detail, then re-band) or a body left cheap by the old mode stays cheap, and restores rboxLodStep so the next click continues the cycle. Ruled out: no captured key is dropped on apply in any group, and no settings object is partially captured. New source-parsing test re-derives the panel's writes and fails on any capture function misses, with a reasoned TRANSIENT allowlist (live actor refs, reload timers, take state, botLiveEnabled which opens a websocket) plus a stale-entry check.

Phase 0 of the height-aware LOS plan: a "Hit volume" debug overlay to verify, against a live bot, the claim that the whole head is outside the hit capsule. Draws the hit capsule (green wireframe, from projCapsuleInto -- the scratch twin of the combatCapsuleFor descriptor resolveHitscan is actually handed), the RENDERED head's world bounds (magenta, read off body.joints.head's own geometry rather than recomputed), and an amber ring on the capsule's exact top plane; enabling it logs measured metres-above-feet and window.reportBotHitVolume() repeats that on demand. Capsule geometry is built per (radius, shaft) and cached with the shaft quantized to 2 cm because scaling a unit capsule non-uniformly turns the hemisphere caps into ellipsoids, and the cap is the thing being measured -- the ring is placed from unquantized numbers so the measurement stays exact. Groups allocate lazily per actor and join the existing teardown. Audit behind it found three systems each reducing a bot to one point at chest height: fieldSaysHidden prunes candidates before any ray because nav-visibility.js discards each blocker's real height above SIGHT_BLOCK_HEIGHT, the sentry LOS is a single eye-to-eye ray at 1.32 m, and the hit capsule ends at 1.80 m while the rendered head runs 1.786-2.020 m.

Spine gradient for the locomotion layer: waist/torso/neck previously all copied one _upperQ so the upper body twisted as a single block hinged at the hips. Each now takes a share of the twist and lean via a new spineOrient(out, frac), frac being its height above the pelvis over the shoulder line (0.29 waist / 0.65 torso / 1.0 neck), with body.spineCfg.falloff as the exponent and a Spine falloff slider in body-preview. Crouch hunch stays ungraded in the shared _upperBaseQ since it is a whole-torso pose; _upperQ is still the full shoulder-line rotation and still drives the head. Tests unchanged and green (32/19/30).

Added a break-contact order: right-click menu gained a Break contact checkbox (commandBreakContact, propagated to squadmates like double time) that lets a move/hold command actually pull a bot out of a live fight, which previously wasn't possible -- combat states (aim/fire/pursue/cover) fully pre-empted updateCommandMovement with no way in. Implemented as a new orderOverride rung in chooseBotStateName (bot-activity.js), placed below every self-preservation rung (flee/heal/knife/committed cover/close-self-threat spin all still win) but above the whole firefight-reflex tier (pursue, fresh cover entry, aim/fire, ally-hit cover-move, lost-sight chase), landing on BOT_PATROL so the active command takes over immediately. Deliberately a hard disengage (bot stops shooting) rather than fire-while-retreating, to keep the first version simple. 20 new assertions in test-bot-activity.mjs verify both the override and every self-preservation rung it must not touch; all existing bot-activity/bot-stance tests stayed green.

Ported the conforming-blood-stain work out of damage-simulator.html into bot-viewer-v2.html's real combat hit path, behind two cost dials in Body & ragdoll. Wound hit: Cylinder/Mesh picks where the wound point comes from -- Cylinder keeps the free point combat already produced from the bot's one 0.3 m capsule (floats off the limb, no part information), Mesh re-traces the shot through a new refineWoundHit() into resolveBodyHit({refresh:true}) for the true surface point, its normal, the hit part's cross-section and an attach handle, at one AABB walk per damage event rather than per frame. Wound stain: Fitted/Projected picks how it is drawn -- Fitted is effect-renderer.js's quad sized 0.55x the part cross-section clamped 0.03-0.16 m, Projected hands stains to projected-decals.js. Mode exclusivity is enforced in updateEffects() by filtering blood_stain out of the wire list into a reused scratch array before sync(), since that runs every frame over up to 900 effects. createEffectRenderer now gets a resolveAttachment closure that looks the bot up in botActorById, so a stain rides the part it was left on; spawnHitBloodFx takes the victim entity and the shot source point so all three callers (applyBotDamage, the dummy-target branch, the blast loop) can supply a ray. refineWoundHit returns null when the victim has no instanced rig or the ray misses the mesh (the capsule is fatter than the body, so a graze can pass beside it) and every caller falls back to the capsule point unchanged. Both toggles round-trip through the save/load slots. Also documented projected-decals.js in fx.md, which the Mode C build had left undocumented.

Turned the cyclic locomotion layer on for bots: naturalLocomotion:true at the single createProceduralPlayerBody site, plus four new botMovementSettings fields (locoEnabled, locoAmount, stepOverlap 0.22, spineFalloff) applied through applyBotMovementSettings so they reach every per-actor body and ride the existing save/load slots. locoAmount scales every cyclic amplitude off LOCOMOTION_DEFAULTS at once, so the layer can be A/B dialled to zero without losing the tuned ratios between channels. Three new sliders in the Movement tuning panel.

Decoupled bot selection from camera movement: the plain left-click handler used to both select a bot (for the right-click command menu) and unconditionally snap the camera into follow/POV on it, which fought with using that same click purely to target a command -- selecting a bot to command it kept yanking the view around. The click handler now only calls setSelectedBot; camera movement is opt-in only, via the Follow/POV buttons, the V/P keybinds (both now target selectedBotActor when set), the auto-follow toggle, or cycling with ]/Nearest. Flagged in docs as a narrow fix, not the camera-system overhaul the user separately called out as its own future task.

Added a Grenade debug overlay toggle: hysteresis band rings, instanced blast-shadow cells, per-bot cover vs open-ground destination lines, and post-blast aim-settle bars, so the evade rewrite can be seen rather than inferred.

Gave every panel control hover text ahead of a public release: 71 of 146 named controls had none, and two shared factories were bare by construction -- createBotMovementSlider had no title parameter at all (so all 12 Movement tuning sliders were tooltip-less) and the Music FX loop ignored one (6 sliders). Wrote the missing ~83 descriptions in plain language aimed at someone who has never seen the app, adding the title parameter to both factories and a 7th field to AUDIO_EFFECT_DEFS. The spec-table cards (aim, stance, explosives, terrain, voices) already had full coverage; an earlier arity check reported gaps there but was miscounting multi-line calls. Also repaired the mojibake in the 'Run speed x' label, which now matches the UTF-8 multiplication sign used elsewhere in the file. New test lists every control the panel creates and fails on any without a title, checks each shared factory both accepts and applies one, and checks positional spec tables row by row -- the gap was previously invisible because a control with no tooltip looks identical in code to one with.

Gave riflemen an overhead insignia (grey diamond) -- the only role with none, since ROLE_RIFLEMAN.insignia was null and the spawn code only builds a marker when one is set. Also split the squad-leader chevron off actor.roleInsignia into its own actor.leaderInsignia field: previously setSquadLeaderMark early-returned for any role that already carried an insignia (the medic cross, the spawned squad-leader class's own chevron), so a promoted medic/sniper/technical -- or, after this change, a promoted rifleman -- showed only its class icon with no leader indication. The two markers are now fully independent and stack (leader chevron above the class marker) so whoever is actually leading a squad shows both regardless of their underlying class. bot-roles/bot-squad/bot-activity/bot-stance/panel-layout tests all stayed green (no test asserted the old null insignia).

Added five toggleable diagnostics to the existing Movement debug overlay so the cyclic locomotion layer can be judged rather than guessed at: a stride-phase dial over the head with ticks at the two expected lift points, fading footfall flashes at each real lift, hip/mid/shoulder twist bars that should scissor in opposite directions, a 3s pelvis trace, and a support line that goes green in double support. Trace and footfalls are sampled every frame by a new sampleBotLocomotionDebug() rather than in the 15 Hz geometry rebuild -- at 15 Hz the bob aliases into a sawtooth and short swings are missed, so the overlay would have reported exactly the bug it exists to disprove. Exposed spineCfg.frac from player-procedural-body so the twist bars read the real fraction table instead of recomputing the falloff curve and drifting from it.

Wrote the missing design-studio workflow doc (run it, the critique loop, the three stall-breaking inspection tools, full __studio API) and wired it into the CLAUDE.md table and code-map DOC_LIST; the two existing sections now point at it instead of implying they cover usage.

Added audible responses to the player right-click command menu: order_ack (solo/non-leader bot confirms a move order, e.g. 'moving out'), order_ack_squad (a commanded squad leader confirms for the whole squad with plural framing, e.g. 'we're oscar mike'), order_follow (nearest living squadmate replies 'roger'/'yes ma'am'/'hooah' 350-650ms later via a real setTimeout, guarded against a scene reset or squad wipe mid-delay). Wired only into bot-viewer-v2.html's issueCommand/announceOrder since environment-viewer-v2.html has no command menu yet. Three new lineIds authored with three different syllable counts (3/4/1) specifically so they land in separate rhythm-uniqueness buckets rather than competing for room in the crowded 3- or 4-syllable clusters; all rhythm/grenade_warn-floor assertions passed on the first attempt this time. Not added to VOICE_INTENSITY_FRESH_LINES -- a player's click doesn't change the bot's combat situation, so the sentry tick's cached alertTierLast is exactly as fresh as a recompute, and it's what makes a mid-firefight order read as a shouted 'GOT IT!' instead of a calm 'affirmative' for free. Wording variety (8/6/3 phrases respectively) drafted for a new bake-order-lines.mjs script (dry-run verified: 170 planned across 10 voices, 0 skipped, 0 failed) but the real paid bake was deliberately not run without the user's go-ahead -- the synth voice already speaks each line's one canonical phrase regardless, so the feature is fully audible before baking.

Blast damage now respects geometry: blastExposure casts 3 rays from the blast centre up the victim capsule (shins/torso/head) and scales damage by the fraction unblocked, so low walls are partial cover instead of the old damage-through-anything radius test. This is what makes the new grenade cover hold actually worth doing. Panel toggle, default on.

Fixed a gap left by the earlier select/camera decoupling: updateCameraButtons() gated the Follow/POV/Frame buttons on hasActor = !!getCameraFollowActor(), which doesn't know about selectedBotActor, so with auto-follow off and nothing ever followed yet the buttons stayed disabled even though a bot was selected and their click handlers already used the selection -- auto-follow (or a prior follow/cycle) was effectively required just to unlock the buttons. V/P keys were unaffected since they call setCameraMode directly. Widened hasActor to also accept selectedBotActor, had setSelectedBot call updateCameraButtons() (selection isn't on the per-frame path so nothing else repainted the buttons on click), and widened frameCamera's default actor the same way so F frames on the current selection too, not only on whatever's actively followed.

Rewrote the grenade evade destination as one scored cell scan: shadow-DEPTH bonus (not just past the boundary) so bots stop parking one step inside cover, enemy-visibility penalty so they stop diving out of a blast into a firing lane, clearance margin off the blast ring edge, and stable per-bot jitter so a squad does not converge on one cell. Replaces the corner-map cover search, which could never fix the edge-parking since a corner anchor IS the boundary.

Fixed Follow mode losing track of its bot while the user rotated or zoomed the orbit camera: updateCameraRig's CAMERA_FOLLOW branch computed a smoothed cameraFollowAnchor every frame but skipped writing it into controls.target/camera.position whenever cameraRig.userInteracting was true, so the orbit pivot sat frozen mid-drag/mid-scroll while the bot kept moving, then the camera snapped to catch up on release. Hoisted the translateTarget call (which carries the pivot and camera together by a pure translation, touching neither orbit distance nor direction) above the userInteracting early-return, so only the distance/occlusion resolution below it stays gated on release -- that's the part that would actually fight a live drag/scroll. No unit-testable surface; this is live OrbitControls interaction timing, verify visually.

Fixed the real reason panel settings appeared not to save, which was never a missing capture field: saving took three separate clicks (maze/bots/ui each had their own Save and there was no combined one), and nothing survived a page reload because the apply functions were only ever reached from a Load click. Added an 'everything' slot row (captureAllState/applyAllState, ordered maze then bots then ui since the maze rebuild clears the roster and ui cannot be undone by the others), a Restore last session button backed by a 3s-debounced autosave plus a pagehide flush, and a disk mirror: createSlotSection gained an optional onSaved hook wired to a POST to the new /api/save-slot-export endpoint, landing every save in bot-viewer-saves/ (gitignored, one file per save). The mirror is fire-and-forget and a throwing hook is swallowed -- the slot is in localStorage before the fetch runs, so losing a save because the server was down would be worse than the problem it solves. Restore is offered rather than applied automatically, which would fight a deliberate reload-for-clean-slate. New test drives createSlotSection against a stub DOM and checks the client filename against the regex serve.py actually compiles, since that contract spans two languages with nothing else linking it.

Logged BB-005/006/007 for this session's grenade bugs: evade released instantly at the ring edge (boundary chatter + instant combat resume), blast damage ignored geometry, and evade destination scored only distance (edge-parking + running into firing lanes). Each notes it was found by user observation plus code read rather than a trace, and which claims are inferred vs confirmed.

Logged BB-005 through BB-008 from the perception/hit-geometry audit. BB-005 is the user-observed "head exposed over cover is never targeted", recorded with its three independent mechanisms (the baked-field prefilter discards blocker height above SIGHT_BLOCK_HEIGHT and rejects at every height for zero raycasts; the LOS ray samples one eye-to-eye point at 1.32 m; the hit capsule ends at 1.80 m while the rendered head runs 1.786-2.020 m) plus a note that only the Phase 0 diagnostic overlay has shipped and the geometry is still computed rather than observed. BB-006 RIG_HEAD_TOP_FACTOR is the head anchor not the head top, so stance capsule scales derive from a body 0.11 m short. BB-007 nav-visibility's terrain eye height is 1.6 against a live 1.32 and its comment claims they match. BB-008 the hitscan players list holds only the shooter's current target, so every other bot is bullet-transparent. All four are code-audit provenance with no .tsv trace, which the entries say plainly rather than inventing trace citations. BB-005 also carries a correction: resolveBodyHit gained a real bot-viewer-v2 caller at 12:05 today (FX path only, via refineWoundHit inside spawnHitBloodFx), so an earlier claim that only damage-simulator called it is no longer true.

Ran the real (paid) bake-order-lines.mjs bake for order_ack/order_ack_squad/order_follow: 170 lines across all 10 ElevenLabs voices, 0 failed; manifest grew to 26 sets / 1588 takes. Confirmed via the background task's real output rather than assumed from the prior dry-run. Full bot-voice/bot-voice-bank/sound-params test suites rerun clean afterward.

Body-preview tuning now saves to disk instead of printing JSON into a log panel for hand-copying: new serve.py routes /api/save-body-tuning (POST, writes body-tuning/body-tuning-[label-]stamp.json) and /api/list-body-tuning (GET), following the existing save_slot_export/save_maze_layout pattern including the filename allowlist regex, non-JSON body rejection and -N collision suffix. Verified end to end against a scratch server: save, list, static fetch-back, collision suffix, and rejection of both a ../ traversal filename and a non-JSON body. The payload carries a full ui slider snapshot alongside the semantic cfg blocks, and Load restores the snapshot -- re-deriving the panel from the cfg blocks would silently drop every slider with no cfg field behind it. serve.py must be restarted for the endpoint to exist.

Correction to the 20:05 row: the IDs it claims are wrong. Concurrent grenade work had already taken BB-005/006/007 while I was reading the file, so my four entries were renumbered BB-008 (head exposed over cover, the user-observed one), BB-009 (RIG_HEAD_TOP_FACTOR is the head anchor not the head top), BB-010 (nav-visibility terrain eye height 1.6 vs live 1.32) and BB-011 (hitscan players list holds only the shooter's current target), and moved above the grenade entries per the newest-on-top convention. Phase 0 of the class-to-damage-language seam: a new pure bot-damage-class.js holding DAMAGE_CLASS_DEFAULTS merged into three rows (human, armouredHuman, robot), classForActor to resolve one from an explicit per-actor override or todays global body kind, and the two pure gates shouldShowBlood/shouldShowSmoke. Built now, wired nowhere, because all four planned damage-FX features wanted the same what-is-this-made-of answer and would otherwise each have grown their own bodyKind branch -- the tables whole point is that no call site ever branches on a class id string, only on capability fields. The armour-breach flag is a ONE-WAY LATCH rather than the hysteresis band used elsewhere in the viewer: blood is decided once per discrete hit, not per frame, so the flicker a band prevents cannot happen, but a medic healing a bot must not make it stop bleeding -- armour once breached does not un-breach. Kept off the 9-char state code deliberately (its latch slot is at 5/5 bits and this does not need to be greppable in a trace). 43 checks in test-bot-damage-class.mjs, including a mechanical assertion that no two classes have identical field sets, since a class distinguishable only by its id would force call sites back into the branching this exists to prevent.

Made the blood-decal cap a runtime dial with a live usage readout, because 512 was picked without ever being measured against a real fight. effect-renderer gained setBloodDecalCap(n)/stats()/resetStats(): the cap is a buffer size and an InstancedBufferAttribute cannot grow in place, so a change is a full pool rebuild (old mesh removed and disposed, sync repopulates from the wire list next frame) -- which is why the slider fires on change rather than input. pushBlood now counts what the cap refused instead of silently swallowing it, and both per-frame and high-water counts are exposed; projected-decals got the same dropped/peak/droppedPeak counters. bot-viewer-v2 has one Decal budget slider (32-4096) driving both pools, reading back cap, live count, peak and drops, repolled at 4 Hz alongside the squad roster rather than per frame, and saved into the slots. The drop count is the number that makes a cap defensible: a cap is only right when drops stay at zero while the peak sits meaningfully below it. 20 new checks in test-effect-renderer (rebuild not resize, no leaked pool mesh, buffer really resized, clamping on negative/garbage/absurd input) and 7 in test-projected-decals.

Authored four damage-FX plans (wound-centred blood stains, limb loss, per-class damage language, blood pools and fire), one per idea, written in parallel against a shared architectural brief so they are comparable, plus a README index. The index records the finding all four hit independently and I then verified: body kind is a single global (BOT_BODY_KINDS has two entries, _bodyKind is one module variable, setBotBodyKind swaps the whole roster), so mixed human/armoured/robot fights are impossible and every idea needs a per-bot class field first. Also verified and recorded: per-part hit resolution reaches the FX path only (refineWoundHit's single call site is inside spawnHitBloodFx; damage still resolves against one capsule and is flat), spawnHitBloodFx runs before health is decremented in both applyBotDamage and detonateBlast, and the shared budgets are maxBloodDecals 512 covering stain+splatter as one instanced draw, a separate 256 projected pool, and botCorpseCap 24. Implementation handed off; nothing built.

Grenade veto rings now use the same occlusion as the damage model via an injected blastReaches hook (wired to blastExposure itself, not a copy), so sheltered allies stop vetoing, sheltered enemies stop counting toward the cluster, and a sheltered thrower can cook one around a corner. The cheap self pre-gate became occlusion-aware too or it would have silently overridden all of it. 24 assertions, mutation-verified.

Wired the damage-class table into the hit path and added health-driven bleed intensity, as ONE change because both needed the same spawnHitBloodFx signature (amount added) and the same three call sites -- applyBotDamage, the dummy branch and the blast loop. spawnHitBloodFx now resolves a class per target and gates hit_spark on cls.sparks, the three blood kinds on shouldShowBlood, and a new small grey smoke_puff on shouldShowSmoke; actor.armourBreached carries the one-way latch and reviveCombatBot is the only thing that clears it. New pure bloodIntensityForHealth(hp01) in effect-renderer scales the droplet burst and ground splatter from a 3-droplet trickle at full health to today's 28-droplet burst at zero -- its values at hp01=0 are EXACTLY the constants that were hardcoded before, which the test asserts, so the mapping can only remove blood from light hits and never changes what a lethal hit already looked like. Health after the hit is predicted by hpAfterHit rather than read, because all three sites spawn FX before decrementing health on purpose (the FX lead the state change); an immortal dummy is pinned to the lethal end so it does not read as untouched forever. Both halves are independently switchable (Damage class, Bleed by health) and off is byte-for-byte the old behaviour, which matters because the default body kind is armoured -- turning classes on stops healthy bots bleeding until 35%. Spark colour deliberately left unpassed so the existing spark look is unchanged. damage-simulator got the matching class buttons plus synthetic health/breached sliders, driving the same two shared functions; its existing spray/splatter sliders now act as the full-intensity ceiling that health scales toward. 15 new checks in test-effect-renderer.

Authored the model-studio plan: a target-agnostic spec edited by the studio, with bots as one emitter among several, taking img2threejs stages 1/2/4 and rejecting its build half (SkinnedMesh + per-component materials cannot go through body-part-batches).

Medics now make contact when treating: TEND creeps to MEDIC_CONTACT_RADIUS (0.85 m) instead of stopping at the 1.7 m latch radius, and both tend poses reach a real contact point on the patient (live capsule chest, or death site for a revive) clamped to arm reach. Split the pose by tendUnderFire: gun-up standing medicHold under fire, holstered two-handed kneeling medicAid out of combat. Also ported the danger-in-cost revive-gate fix to environment-viewer-v2.

Wound centre: both decal materials now darken their own middle so a stain reads as a puncture with blood radiating out rather than a flat red smear. New wound-mask.js holds the shared constants and the CPU twin woundCoreFactor; unlike the other CPU/GPU twins it IS imported by the files it mirrors, but only for the constants, so the fitted quad pool and the projected boxes cannot start from different defaults. The mix is driven by the decal's own geometry, NOT by the stain texture's alpha -- the obvious shortcut, and wrong: makeStainTexture's seven fused lobes sit at r 0.10-0.26 from centre with radii up to 0.20, so alpha hits 1 in patches well away from the middle and colour driven from it would paint scattered blotches instead of one wound. Distances are in decal half-widths so they hold at any stain size, and instColor.mul(darken) darkens whatever colour the instance carries instead of forcing a blood shade, which is what lets blood_splatter share it and keeps a future non-blood decal on the same pool working. Three live uniforms per material with a setWoundStyle write API, declared outside makeDecalPool so a setBloodDecalCap resize cannot reset them; damage-simulator got inner/outer/darken sliders that write both materials, and re-applies the style when the projected pool is rebuilt for its debug toggle. Known limit recorded in the doc: the uniforms are material-wide, so a later decal kind wanting a different core on the same pool needs a per-instance attribute. 26 checks in test-wound-mask.mjs including a 1e-12 match against the TSL smoothstep formula across the whole quad.

Reworked the experimental command wheel from a Q-press toggle to a hold-drag-release gesture on the middle mouse button: Q conflicted with fly-cam descent, and the old click-to-toggle model closed the wheel before the double-time/break-contact toggle spokes ever showed their new state. controls.mouseButtons.MIDDLE is now permanently freed from OrbitControls dolly; each spoke resolves via elementFromPoint at pointerup and toggle spokes repaint their fill from a live isActive() getter every time the wheel opens.

Kneel stance (state.kneel) built into the body module and the tuning harness; bots not wired yet. Modelled on prone, not crouch, since kneeling is a distinct pose rather than a shortened standing one: kneeling on one knee, rear knee grounded under the hip, front thigh horizontal and shin vertical. Precedence prone > kneel > crouch, each gating the ones below, and the locomotion layer fades by (1-pw)*(1-kw). Two departures from proneCfg: offsets are multiples of thighLen/shinLen rather than absolute metres (a kneel is a closed chain and the skeleton is one fixed size for every body, so metres would stretch limbs), and the knee is AUTHORED rather than solved -- solveLeg gained kneeTarget/kneeWeight because no pole angle reliably puts a kneeling knee on the ground. Split pelvisYK out of pelvisY so the upper-body stack rides the kneeled hip instead of floating at standing height. New test-body-kneel.mjs (26 assertions) checks both chains close within 5% of true bone length for both handednesses plus the shape properties that separate a kneel from a squat; the harness panel shows the same closure error live, since the sliders can author a chain that does not close and placeSegment would hide it by stretching.

Fixed: ground splatter was getting the wound centre too. blood_stain and blood_splatter are ONE instanced draw sharing ONE material, so the material-wide wound uniforms darkened the middle of every thrown droplet as well -- a droplet on the ground is not a puncture. Added instWound, a per-instance float that multiplies the core factor: pushBlood takes it as a parameter (defaulting to 1), drawBloodStain leaves it at 1 and drawBloodSplatter passes 0. The three uniforms still set the SHAPE of the core for the whole pool; the attribute decides which instances have one at all. This is the per-instance attribute the previous change had documented as a known limit, arriving one kind earlier than expected. projected-decals is untouched because it only ever receives stains. 6 new checks in test-wound-mask.mjs asserting a synced stain writes 1 and every instance a splatter produces writes 0.

Body kind (Human soldier vs Armoured bot) was never saved. Root cause is a class my earlier audits structurally could not see: the control calls setBotBodyKind imported from bot-body-design.js, so the state lives in that module and NO assignment exists in bot-viewer-v2.html to find -- every scan I had run looked for assignments. captureBotState now records getBotBodyKind() and applyBotState restores it after the procedural-body switch (rebuilding rigs is pointless while bots are capsules), guarded on an actual change like the weapon/ammo setters since a rebuild walks every live rig, and refreshing the damage-class label which resolves from body kind. Extended the coverage test with an imported-setter pass: any set* imported from another module and driven by the panel must have its getter reach a capture function, with an ACTIONS allowlist for genuine actions (resetScoreboard). Also relaxed the tooltip test, which flagged decalBudgetInput though its row carries the title and title inherits to descendants -- that row-level idiom is deliberate so the label and value hover too.

Medic self-heal is now role-blind (rifleHeal pose + crouch like every other bot; forcedCrouch no longer exempts medics) and a revive got its own read: triangle-eased ~1.7 Hz chest compressions vs the heal's steady press, both hands stacked when out of combat, a cyan fused-kit mesh in hand instead of the white-cross pack, and a kneel even under fire

The harness's cursor-over-orbit-camera scheme does not survive pointer lock, so the wheel reuses this file's own tool-radial idiom: spoke picked from accumulated movementX/Y, goal taken from lgRaycastTerrain under the crosshair, target bot from pickBotAtScreen at centre. Two 5-agent parity audits of bot brain/nav across bot-viewer-v2 vs environment-viewer-v2. Round 1 ran against the live tree while the parity agent was editing it and ripgrep was timing out on the Drive mount, so three headline 'missing' findings were false and agreement between agents concealed rather than caught them. Round 2 re-ran against a frozen local-disk snapshot with a two-method rule for absence claims; no false absences survived. Confirmed open: heal threshold 0.60 vs 0.35, EYE_LIFT 0.85 vs capsule-top (plus an internal self/target inconsistency in the port), grenade self pre-gate missing its occlusion term, evade hysteresis called with 3 args, medic contact creep, think-cadence stagger. Command layer already fixed post-snapshot.

Fixed bots standing still on open terrain until an enemy appeared. With no patrol points the only goal is an explore point 80-300m out, which usually fails to path; the nearest-walkable retarget then picked a cell in a DIFFERENT nav region, so A* failed again and the empty path cleared the goal in a loop. nearestWalkableInGrid now takes a region and the zone branch passes the bot's own, and a failed explore goal routes through the same local fallback a cut-off patrol point already had (previously gated behind points.length>0, unreachable on terrain). Removed the two stale 2026-07-19 TEMP diagnostics - [botpath] instrumented the local-window branch, which Phase D had replaced on terrain.

Fixed the freeze on switching body kind: rebuildBotBodies destroyed every rig while a corpse mid-ragdoll is posed from it each frame, and the ragdoll LOD branch was the one path that dereferenced bodyProc unguarded - throwing every frame from inside the async animate loop. It also leaked a live-corpse budget slot since only _retireRagdoll decrements it. Retire the ragdoll before dropping the rig, guard the branch, regression-test both.

Fixed a self-inflicted ReferenceError: removing the stale _botPathDebugCount declaration left two more uses of it in requestBotPath's fallback/empty log lines, so every patrol path request threw. Both removed. Added a per-cause walkability tally printed with the zone bake ([bot zone walkability]): the first real bake reported only 4744 of 65536 cells walkable across 85 stranded regions, and the counters say which test (water/slope/trees/dressing/mesh) is rejecting them instead of leaving it to be guessed.

Revised the creature target: generateBodyPlan already produces arbitrary skeletons, so a creature is a bot with a derived anchor list rather than a new mechanism. Remaining costs are extracting the plan/IK from the 5455-line sim (DOM-coupled) and the fact that creature segments are individual meshes, not batched.

Found the real reason bots froze on open terrain, by instrumenting the bake instead of reasoning about it: botMeshBlockedAt rejected 92% of 65536 zone cells. Its probe capsule floats 2cm above the sampled ground while map-collision only reports grounded on actual contact, so `blocked = !grounded || pushed` condemned every accurately-sampled open cell and passed only the ones where mesh rises into the capsule. Dropped the !grounded term; lateral push is the whole signal. A first attempt that seated the probe 3cm into the ground was falsified by its own test (0.077m lateral push on a 45deg face vs 0.05 tolerance) and abandoned - the test keeps it as a negative guard and checks the shipped rule at the real 31deg slope limit. Also swapped a JSDoc block that had ended up describing the wrong method after bodyFor was inserted above it.

Adversarial review found bots reached guests with no role: toWirePose reads bot.role but the viewer only set rec.role, and only the host's own ghost path patched pose.role in. Guests therefore rendered every bot as the bare default rig (no medic cross, launcher tube or sniper helmet) and drew no role insignia. One line at spawn sets bot.role; added a wire-contract test asserting toWirePose emits every field the overhead overlay reads, since nothing covered the wire producer at all.

Leashed bot exploration to spawnPos. exploreHeading is rolled once at spawn and every goal is 80-300m along it, so bots walked a straight line outward forever: a live roster showed six of twenty-one stranded 600m-1.1km out on coastline the 384m nav zone never covers, while the fight stayed within 150m of the player. leashedExploreAim turns the aim back toward spawn past BOT_LEASH_RADIUS 140m and caps the hop so it cannot overshoot onto the far side, rather than clamping to a boundary bots would pile against. Interim until bots gain real map spawn locations to belong to. Test simulates 40 hops both ways (unleashed ends 3km+ out) and guards its copy of the pure helper against drift from the viewer.

Fixed bots walking up to each other and freezing in PURSUE. Two causes, both in the pursuit path. pursuitStandoffGoal rejected every approach bearing another pursuer had CLAIMED and fell through to the direct point, which is only reached when it is unwalkable (offset 0 is tried first) - so in a converging group everyone after the first got an unpathable goal; it now shares a walkable claimed bearing instead, since crowding is what the separation steering is for. And updatePursuitMovement swallowed path failures entirely (unlike patrol, it never touched pathFailCount), while PURSUE can only be exited by getting CLOSER to the target - so a bot that could not move could never leave the state and reported failCount 0 while frozen. It now retries toward the target's own ground snapped into the bot's own region, and counts a real failure so the existing escape ladder engages.

Spawn authoring for bot-viewer-v3: there was no way to say where bots come from beyond side mode's hard half-and-half split of the map. Spawn markers are now the general mechanism - a team-owned point bots appear at, with a base being just a marker that has a compound built around it, so free-form clicked markers and side-mode home points are one record and one vocabulary. Two armed click tools (place marker / place bot) commit on an empty-ground left-click through the existing wheel-arming path so they collide with no current gesture; findBotSpawnPoint gained a marker stage between the squad anchor and the team side, re-picking per pass so one blocked marker cannot starve a team; base build now builds a compound at every marker with markerRegion orienting each gateway toward the map middle. A squad that spawns at a marker garrisons it: out of combat that replaces patrol so the squad stays put, intruders are still engaged because every combat state sits above that rung, pursuit goals are clamped to the ring so nobody chases off the map, and only a manual order clears it. The pure half lives in bot-spawn-markers.js so the environment viewer port is a straight import.

Track A0: limb identity for a hit part (handles the visual/internal side mirror and gear as a hit target) and hoisted the rig re-trace out of the FX function so anatomy no longer depends on cosmetic toggles.

Added the ecobrutal theme plus procedural cast concrete on wall/cover materials (form-panel grid, board grain, tie holes, aggregate, rain streaks, moss via the shared mossWeight law, base algae). Ported env-viewer's grass and understory plants into bot-viewer-v3 as bot-flora.js, plus new hanging wall vines. Placed in one pass over the arena instead of env-viewer's chunk streaming; blades/plants inside walls, cover and spawn pads are dropped via a new backward-compatible grass.js acceptFn and a gridded blocker index.

Fixed the Flora card throwing on load: header() only re-points at a card SECTION_PLAN already built, so the new card needed a plan row (visuals tab, after Sky detail). Updated the two panel guards that caught it - the layout test's expected card list, and slot coverage, where syncFloraPanel is a syncer rather than a setting (the values it pushes ride in the ui slot via visuals.getLookState).

Fixed plant distribution after the first browser look. Bug: a chunk is square and an arena is a rectangle, and floraChunk anchored the square at a corner, so a third of the plants grew in a band off one edge - isBlocked cannot reject those because off-map correctly reports nothing blocking, so the plant filter now tests inRect like the grass path already did. Also set an explicit clumpRadius (the default is chunk.size*0.16, meaningless on one arena-sized chunk) and added wallAffinityMask so plants mass against the concrete as in every reference.

Cut the juniperMound/pinkflowerBush sprigClump shrubs: the crossed-quad technique needs an alpha-cutout foliage atlas that was never drawn, so they rendered as bare opaque rectangles (the pink and green slabs). Fixed UNIT 1/30 -> 1/100, which sized a single leaf right but let stem height accumulate over 5-8 nodes into 3-4 m plants; the 4 herbs now measure 0.28-1.22 m. Added the missing sRGB->linear decode on vertex colours (grass.js already did this via THREE.Color), behind PLANT_COLOR_SRGB so it reverts in one character - the hexes were authored against the undecoded render and now read darker. Added the height and colour assertions whose absence let both bugs ship.

Flora controls: grass density max 60 -> 180 (blade cap raised 240k -> 720k to match, or the slider would lie); per-species height/density via a dropdown plus two sliders, height baking through a new createPlantPalette heightScale option and density reweighting the species table; and a Vines subsection with distribution (clump strands into bunches), leafiness and branching. Fixed floraFor aliasing FLORA_OFF's per-species maps by reference, which would have let one theme's edit poison every other.

Added elevated geometry so the map has the two architectural moves the eco-brutalism references are built on. New slab primitive {x,z,w,d,y,h} renders and joins the BVH collider but is absent from pointInWall and sightBlockers, so bots walk and shoot under an overhang rather than pathing round air. wallRun now emits lintels over doorways and full windows (sill as cover, since a sill behaves as cover), and a new portal structure kind gives the underpass form. Slabs reach flora as their own vine-host list so vines hang off soffit edges without grass treating them as keep-outs.

Audit items 3 and 5. Moss now runs on the GROUND via groundMoss() in floorMat/terrainMat, gated on upness through the shared mossWeight law - it was previously only on wall caps, which on 0.3 m walls is a strip you cannot see; cap mask widened and gains raised too. Vine leaves relaid into the wall plane facing outward like real ivy, which fixes the black cards (a horizontal card seen from below takes no key light under DoubleSide) and replaces the flat diamonds with lobed 5-point fans, 8 per strand, with woody red-brown stems.

Grass density slider read as a lie on large maps: the maths is genuinely per-m2, but BLADE_CAP silently thinned the field above ~160 m at the default density (200 m map got 17/m2, 260 m got 10.2/m2) and above ~63 m at the top of the slider. Cap kept - it is a memory ceiling on one merged mesh - but surfaced: flora stats now carry askedDensity/builtDensity/capped and the Flora card reports the density actually built, warning-coloured when the ceiling binds. Also wired grass.js's setFade, which had never been connected, to the view-distance slider.

summary: Blade ceiling is now a flora setting (bladeCap) with a number-entry box in the Flora card rather than a constant I picked arbitrarily. Tooltip and the capped readout carry the measured cost curve (~40 ms rebuild at 240k, ~100 ms at 720k, ~170 ms at 1.2M on a 900-wall 200 m map, roughly linear; ~176 bytes a blade), so the trade being made is visible at the point of choice.

Placing a spawn marker with base build on now runs the layout rebuild itself, so the compound walls appear on the click instead of only after the user found some other control that happened to trigger a rebuild. Forces keepBots true regardless of the rebuild toggle, since placing a marker is not a change of map and must not clear the roster, and skips the rebuild entirely when base build is off or the rooms layout is active, where no compound would be emitted anyway. The rebuild is still whole-map; only region labelling genuinely needs to be, so an incremental nav-grid/corner-map path is the fix if the logged cover bake proves too slow to sit behind a click.

Plan for a standalone flight harness: the arcade aerodynamics (AoA, lift, four-term drag, dual stall model) and the AI craft steering already exist in the html-game-v2 repo and port cleanly, so the new work is converting camera-directed glide into stick-flown attitude, a HUD, and a units pass against our terrain scale. The GitHub CesiumJS flight sim is reference-only; its terrain stack conflicts with our CDLOD and its license is non-commercial.

Made the cyclic locomotion layer togglable in v3 so a weird-looking walk can be A/B'd against the reactive foot scheduler alone. locoEnabled has been read by applyBotMovementSettings since the layer shipped but never had a control, and the Cyclic amount slider that stood in for one was not a true off: locoAmount scaled eight amplitudes but not armSpread, so at 0 the arms still drifted 5cm outward. Added the On/Off button above the slider, scaled armSpread with the rest, and corrected the slider's tooltip which claimed 0 turned the layer off entirely.

Research pass over the qosf awesome-quantum-software list. A first portability screen rejected all ~400 projects (Python/C++, wrong scale) and that screen was the wrong test: re-reading for transferable algorithms rather than importable packages found five worth reimplementing. Strongest is a decision diagram over bot-state-code.js, whose own header already describes a 0.906%-dense discrete space and one axis that was authored wrong - canonical BDD form makes FSM-refactor equivalence a DAG comparison. Also SPSA to close the tuning loop on creature-stats.js metrics, Krotov-style optimal control for ragdoll pose transitions, MWPM for medic repair decisions, and PyZX-style rewrite-to-fixpoint on the model-csg graph. QUBO solvers, QRNG, chemistry and lab-control sections rejected with reasons.

Revised the flight plan for the answers given: sim-based arcade-leaning, three craft classes, player and AI flown, targeting environment-viewer-v2 and bot-viewer-v3. Drones, birds, and planes are different physics rather than one model retuned, so the design is a rigid-body core with pluggable airframes supplying thrust, lift, and control-authority curves; the charge boost is dropped because it fights energy management. Integration goes through entity-registry as an aircraft entity type, which buys host-authoritative replication, and the underestimated cost is that our ground bots cannot target anything airborne.

Research pass over fan-ziqi/robot_viewer, a Three.js WebGL robot description viewer. Four scouts ran blind to this repo first and about a third of that round was dead on arrival - they proposed an entity registry, an id-to-object map and blob URL revocation that all already exist here - so a second round re-ranked against a verified inventory. Optimization findings went six to zero, correctly, since a static model viewer has nothing to teach a game already doing instancing and LOD. Three items survive as one piece of work: a shared undo stack (no harness has one), their cubic Bezier keyframe timeline over weapon-pose-controller.js which is confirmed linear-only, and drag-to-pose joint manipulation which our editors already have the raycasters for. Also noted serve.py sets no COOP/COEP so SharedArrayBuffer is header-blocked, though that is worthless until there is a worker to offload to.

Added a demos/ folder with two evaluation pages built from a raymarched-SDF three.js demo by Drin (@DrinLajci), credited in every file. sdf-creature.html reimplements it in TSL and then answers what it is for here: a mock start screen whose four portrait cards are quads placed over their own getBoundingClientRect, since the project has no portraits, avatars or loading visual anywhere. volumetric-smoke.html A/Bs a bounded density march against the billboard pool effect-renderer.js ships, reusing projected-decals.js's depth reconstruction so the march clamps its exit to scene depth - that one line is why the volume meets the floor along a curve where the quads cut a straight line. Fullscreen marching was rejected for the game itself: it competes with the rasterizer and cannot coexist with CDLOD terrain, the forest and 90 instanced bots. Both TSL graphs were built headlessly against node_modules/three to check the node API; neither is wired into anything and neither has a committed test.

Audited dgreenheck/webgpu-claude-skill, which turns out to be a Claude skill and Cursor rule pack rather than a library, so there is nothing to vendor and the transferable value is the doc set plus a checklist of TSL surface we never touched. Six Haiku agents split the docs and I re-checked every node name they returned against node_modules/three/build/three.tsl.js, which was the right call: perturbed, Case, toConst and atan2 do not exist in r0.184 and were all recommended. Real gaps confirmed by hand are that device.lost appears nowhere outside vendored three.webgpu.js so a driver hiccup silently desyncs multiplayer hosts, there is no AA node at all and the renderer antialias flag is suspect now that PostProcessing owns the target, and the MRT normal pass our own post-fx.js:5 comment already defers to v2 is what gates selective bloom, GTAO and SSR. Rejected N-body particles, workgroup tiling and GPU readback, the last because forest-gpu.js:306 already records rejecting it. Nothing was implemented.

Made the blob in demos/sdf-creature.html follow the cursor and fuse into the body, which is the interaction the original demo by Drin (@DrinLajci) was actually about - the still image read as a fixed cheek marking, so the first version authored it as one. The blob is now an ellipsoid at a uniform world position smooth-unioned into the body every frame, with sliders for radius, the smooth-min k, and depth through the torso. Pointer motion carries the blob and a held button turns the creature, since the merge only reads if the blob can be dragged across the body. summary: Addendum to the NPC design suite plan, then an adversarial review of the addendum that overturned its central claim. The addendum correctly diagnosed that P1's refcounting does not bound cache growth - a permanently-alive NPC never drops to zero refs - but prescribed copying body-part-batches.js's frame-based eviction, which is wrong because the geometry cache is a build-time structure: every cache.get() is in the construction path and the draw path never consults it. Touch-on-draw fails too, decisively on the LOD twins at player-procedural-body.js:1047 where the unselected twin is never drawn by construction, so a fully visible NPC would render a disposed buffer on the first setGearLod swap. P1 is now build-time retain/release with a sweep of unreferenced entries clocked on design edits. The review also surfaced the mesh-vs-instanced fork as the real P0 above the cache work, a missing targeted bucket-drop API in the batch pool, that step 2's reconfigure path does not exist, and that the ?v= pins currently isolate two separate geometry caches rather than being cosmetic. summary: SPSA optimiser (item 2 of the quantum-software research pass) plus a gait-tuning demo. spsa.js is a pure leaf: SPSA, finite-difference and random-search baselines behind one eval-counting harness so a best-so-far-vs-evaluations plot is fair, unit-space normalisation so mixed-unit sliders share one perturbation size, and calibrateSpsa - which matters more than expected, since every gain I picked by hand diverged and calibration beat all of them. Demo tunes 9 kinematic gait params against noisy metrics; 32/35 runs across 7 target speeds x 5 seeds land fully supported within 20% of target and 34/35 beat a hand-authored trot. Two results recorded against the demo overselling itself: at n=9 SPSA and finite differences tie 16-15 (the advantage is dimensional - n=20 synthetic gives 0.007 vs 2.06), and the first objective was exploited outright, pinning freq/stride high and duty low for 10 m/s at 44% support, because an unbounded speed reward outweighs any bounded penalty. Target-speed objective fixed it; the exploit is kept as a toggle. Widening phase bounds to fix a clumped-phase local optimum measured worse and was reverted.

Made the cursor blob in demos/sdf-creature.html a light source and gave it a collide mode. The light glows on the blob surface, casts a shadowed coloured pool on the body and leaves an analytic halo in the air; its shadow ray is bounded short of the blob own surface, because the blob is part of the field it lights and otherwise occludes itself completely. Collide stops the blob at the surface, dents the body under it and flattens it against the contact, with body give and blob give as complementary shares of the requested press. Contact cannot be solved in the shader - it needs the body distance at the blob centre, inside the same map function that would supply it - so it is solved once per frame in new demos/creature-collision.js, a hand-synced CPU twin in the same style as forest-cull.js and deliberately coarser (no mouth cut, no tooth). The first implementation pushed the centre out along the body gradient and was wrong: deep inside a smooth-union field the gradient stops pointing at the nearest surface and a centre dropped in the torso was ejected downward through the legs. Replaced with sphere-tracing the centre along the cursor ray, which never evaluates the field deep inside. New test-demo-creature-sdf.mjs covers it in 87 checks including a 600-ray sweep asserting the blob never ends up inside the body, which is the check the gradient-push version failed. The dent depth is capped at 0.6 blob radii and that cap is asserted: the dent adds to the field so past that the gradient exceeds 1 and the march overshoots into holes.

Standalone flight demo testing the plan claim that drones, birds and planes need three airframes over one shared rigid-body core, before any of it touches env-viewer-v2 or bot-viewer-v3. Forces integrate onto velocity and attitude is a quaternion driven by commanded body rates with lag, so energy management and stalls fall out of the equations without an inertia tensor. Terrain is analytic with a JS/TSL twin behind clipmap rings, which also settles the plan Phase 0 questions about terrain at speed and a cloud deck you can climb through. A headless run of the extracted model caught five bugs that would have read as vague wrongness on screen rather than as faults: trim seeking zero AoA and so zero lift, trim with no speed reference riding a dive into the ground, flap thrust aimed upward so the bird levitated its own flight path into a stall, an AI target swept faster than any craft could fly, and an inverted bank sign that parked the heading error at 180 degrees.

Rebuilt the flight demo height field after the terrain read as parallel furrows in flight. The separable sin(x)*cos(z) form was only half of it: every octave used a z/x frequency ratio near 1, and sin(A)cos(B) with A close to B is one diagonal plane wave plus a long beat, so all four octaves ran as near-parallel corrugations. Replaced with 16 plane waves spread by the golden angle at a 1.28 frequency ratio, domain-warped so wavefronts meander, with the warp Jacobian checked to stay above 0.43 so the field never folds. 16 and 1.28 came from a sweep rather than taste. Two metrics had to be thrown away first: autocorrelation scored both fields at 0.93 because it measures smoothness rather than repetition, and plain slope-by-direction scored both at 2.4x because the 7 km landform terms drown out the fine corrugation. Only a high-passed direction test separates them, 5.2x to 2.5x, and the residual is inherent to a small sum of plane waves.

Band-limited the flight demo height field by distance, which was the actual aliasing the stipple came from and which the previous change caused. A clipmap doubles its cell size every ring, so 16 waves reaching down to a 243 m wavelength left ring 4 sampling at 1.4 per wavelength, under Nyquist, and the fold showed as moire whorls over the whole distance. Each wave now fades out as the local spacing approaches it, full at 8 samples per wavelength and gone by 4, keyed on DISTANCE rather than ring index so overlapping rings agree about the height and the seam cannot crack. Physics still gets full detail, since heightAt takes spacing 0 by default. Worst sampling per ring goes from 1.4 to 4.9. The metric that first said this was a non-issue measured height variance, which the 9 km landform waves dominate; slope is what a shaded surface shows, and by slope ring 4 was 22.5 percent contaminated.

Fixed collide mode in demos/sdf-creature.html: it stopped the blob at the surface but still smooth-unioned it, so the two stayed one continuous fused surface just slightly further out. Phase mode is two behaviours at once - interpenetration AND fusing - and collide has to undo both or it undoes neither. Collide now drops the blend radius to a hairline so the shapes keep their own silhouettes and meet at a crease; the fillet is replaced as a contact cue by the dent, the squash, AO in the crevice and the key shadow the blob casts. The two modes drive the same uniform from separate sliders since they want opposite things from it. Found and fixed a second defect in the same lines: sminM blends the material id linearly, so a seam between id 0 and id 3 walks through ids 1 and 2 and painted eye-white and horn-orange bands across the fused join. Renumbered so ID_BLOB is 1 next to ID_SKIN (the only blended pair) and gave every other union a hard id pick via a new sminHard, keeping the shape fused while the colour changes on a line. Widened the palette weight band to exactly one slot, the largest width where a non-neighbour still contributes nothing. Verified by sweeping the id range for contamination, rebuilding the TSL graph headlessly, and re-running both the 87-check collision suite and the unprojection check.

Terrain shading in the flight demo was reading the WRONG vertex position. Setting material.positionNode makes three assign that value into positionLocal during vertex setup, so every later read — including whatever normalNode and colorNode pull into the fragment stage — gets the displaced world position rather than the [-1,1] grid coordinate, and multiplying that by the ring half-extent again gives sine arguments in the millions. The landforms stayed correct because positionNode itself is evaluated before the substitution, which is why this read as an antialiasing problem for three rounds. Now reads attribute(position) directly, the way cdlod-terrain.js does. Added four terrain debug views (lit, flat unlit, normals, lattice checker) so the next artifact gets pinned to a layer instead of guessed at. Ruled out first, with numbers: float32 precision in the height field costs 0.003 degrees of normal error in the play area and 0.15 at 400 km out.

Replaced the SPSA demo's invented kinematic quadruped with the real thing: gait-objective.js drives stepGait from player-procedural-body.js headlessly (Contract 3 is what makes that possible) over a speed sweep on procedural terrain, and scores real foot states - swing foot through the ground, planted foot outside leg reach, both feet airborne, stride asymmetry/irregularity, float, jitter. What is tuned is GAIT_SPEED_MODEL itself, so the baseline is the shipped least-squares fit rather than a straw man: it scores 3.644 of a 4.0 ceiling and SPSA reaches 4.000/3.934/4.000 over three seeds (finite diff 3.762/3.644/3.991, random 3.644/3.958/3.749 - SPSA loses one to random at only 8 params). Three objective bugs found by running it, not reading it: ground clipping never fired because the terrain had no stride-scale wavelengths, leaving lift unconstrained; the clean reference then still missed it by using one terrain phase while only the noisy objective randomised phase; and a cadence floor was needed since nothing stopped the search winning by vibrating. Also found GAIT_DEFAULTS.lookAhead is declared and read nowhere - excluded from the tunable set. Harness uses unscaled LEG_WORKSPACE_DEFAULTS so its reach numbers describe one body, not the shipped fit; nothing written back to GAIT_SPEED_MODEL. Fixed the reported slider bug too: session controls rebuilt the search AND paused it, so every drag looked inert; they now preserve run state, and preview speed / iters-per-frame apply live.

Combat pass on the flight demo: gun, proportional-navigation missiles, flares that can steal a seeker, per-class hit points, crash and kill explosions with smoke trails on damaged aircraft, afterburner, and a HUD combat layer with target boxes, lock ring and diamond, off-screen arrows, gun funnel, weapon state and a heading-up radar. AI gained engage and break modes: lead pursuit on the player, guns only inside a tight cone at short range, missiles only on a full lock, and a perpendicular break with flares when one is inbound. AI circuits now centre on the player rather than the world origin, which is why they were easy to lose. Bullets are swept against craft rather than point-tested because a 940 m/s round moves 15.7 m per frame against a 6.5 m target and a point test measurably catches only 36 percent of real hits. Guidance, intercepts against straight and turning targets, decoy behaviour, lock cone bounds and time-to-kill all checked headlessly.

summary: Reviewed both explosion implementations and rebuilt demos/volumetric-smoke.html around what the review found. effect-renderer.js line 3 already says it is a port of html-game-v2 explosion look, so the useful question was where they drifted: v2 has a pooled dynamic light, a wireframe shell sphere, 900 instanced shrapnel tetrahedra with trails, 80 spark cylinders and a 2600-slot pool of low-poly SPHERES for smoke, against our billboard core, line-streak shrapnel and 260-slot sprite pool at ten puffs per blast. Neither has scorch or crater. The demo now runs an instanced pool of blasts in one draw with centre/radius/phase/tier as instance attributes, the same pool shape effect-renderer already uses, which is also what makes it fit replication - a blast is eight floats against ten hashed puffs. Fireball is no longer a separate layer: it is a heat term inside the same density field, so it is occluded by its own smoke as it decays, which an additive billboard core cannot do. Added a ground pancake and mushroom cap that deform the sampling space rather than adding lobes, so they cost nothing per step, and the depth clamp means a deck-level blast cannot reach through the floor - v2 has to detect that case and lay a separate flat quad. Extracted html-game-v2 reserveExplosionVisualTier to a new explosion-tier.js with test-explosion-tier.mjs (34 checks, constants asserted as literals so retuning is deliberate); it is the one piece of that codebase this subsystem should adopt outright, because our pools overflow silently and strip random sub-particles from every live blast at once where the tier system degrades whole later blasts. Tiers drive march step count, since that is the only quality dial a march has. Shrapnel, sparks, embers and the ring are deliberately left alone - thin fast near-sub-pixel work where v2 instanced geometry is the stronger answer. Also noted for whoever takes this further: bot-viewer-v3 already ships projected-decals.js and already exposes ?msaa=0, so the unresolved depth-under-MSAA question can be answered there without writing any code.

Split the flight demo threat warning into two sounds, because being locked and being shot at mean different things: a slow low siren while something holds a lock on you or a SAM is tracking, then a beep that quickens as a missile closes and goes solid half a second out. Simulating a closing missile rather than listening caught two problems. Time to impact is not monotone, since closure collapses near a near-miss, so the warning was measurably relaxing from a 0.089 second gap back to 0.65 at the worst possible moment; the rate now takes the smaller of the time-to-impact and range estimates and is ratcheted so it can only speed up. A pure ratchet then screams forever when a missile overshoots and keeps tracking while opening range, so the ratchet only holds while the range is shrinking.

Lean-into-step slider read as dead because its only feedback was geometry too small to see: the lean is 3.5 deg at the default 2.05 m/s preview, so a full-scale lead is 13 cm or about 15 screen pixels (7 px at 1 m/s). The effect was real the whole time - score 3.644 to 3.889 across the slider - just invisible. Now the top walker's score is recomputed live on every slider change and shown in its label with the delta, its leg-past-extension percentage is shown at the nearest swept speed, and the pelvis-to-balance-point offset is drawn as a measured bar with the distance printed on it instead of a faint dashed tick. Also documented that Preview speed 5-6 is where the geometry becomes visible (33-38 cm of lead).

Three additions to the flight demo. A miss now gets its own sound: the two-note cabin chime an airliner plays for an alert, a struck ding-dong falling G5 to C5 in soft sines, fired when a missile that was tracking you stops tracking you while you are still flying. It is suppressed on the three ways of pretending you got away with something - the blast damaged you, you are dead, or a second missile arrived with no gap - because the beeping merely stopping carries no information. The ordering detail that mattered is that the had-a-threat read has to happen before the loop that clears every flyer threat, since that loop is the only thing still holding last frame value; reading it next to the reassignment gets null every time and the chime never plays. Second, an enemy respawn toggle: hostiles stay dead when it is off (allies and the player always return) and destroyed ground sites rebuild after 30 s when it is on, which closes the previously flagged gap that nothing on the ground ever came back. Two separate code paths respawned an AI, a 2.5 s crash timer and a 4 s dead timer, so gating one would have looked like it worked until an enemy crashed instead of being shot down; both now go through one mayRespawn. Third, undefended base structures - HQ, hangars, fuel depots - in their own cluster outside the SAM ring, drawn dashed on the HUD so the shape says what it is and the dash says it cannot hurt you. They share the existing range-0 early exit rather than adding a special case, and the radar is deliberately not marked passive since it has no gun but is what gives every other site its full reach. The depot blast hit a real limit: the volumetric march is priced per covered pixel, so the puff radius is a fill-rate budget and is now capped at 24, with an oversized blast falling back to the full sprite count to fill out what the volume no longer covers.

Promoted lean-into-step from the demo to the real rig so it can be seen on a v3 soldier bot, default off. The hip handed to the gait scheduler is built inside player-procedural-body.js's update(), so no caller could shift it - the change had to live there. update() now passes a balance point (pos + lead along the DIRECTION OF TRAVEL, since that is where the mass goes while the spine's lean follows facing) via two new pure exported helpers, leanAngleForSpeed and stepLeadFor, which are headless-tested and which gait-objective.js now imports instead of keeping its own copy, so demo and rig cannot drift. Knob is movementTuning.stepLeadScale, default 0 and asserted to be an exact no-op at every speed and body height. bot-viewer-v3 exposes it as a Lean into step slider in the movement section; it rides the existing botMovementSettings spread so save/load and slot coverage needed no change. Note this is distinct from the existing movementTuning.maxForwardLead, which is the mirror image and explicitly render-only: it clamps how far the drawn body may drift ahead of its support and never feeds back into where feet are aimed.

Downed aircraft in the flight demo are now three events instead of one: a fireball where the hit landed, a burning fall on its own ballistic integrator with a tumble biased toward roll, and a detonation at three times the air-burst radius when it arrives. Building it exposed an existing bug - poseMesh set mesh visibility unconditionally every frame, which quietly undid the hide in killFlyer, so downed aircraft were not vanishing, they were hanging frozen in the air until they respawned. Fire and smoke needed separate emission clocks for pool arithmetic rather than taste: smoke lasts nearly 3 s against fire 0.32 s, so on a shared clock one wreck would hold 97 smoke sprites alive against a pool of 96 and starve every other effect on screen. The safety timer was nearly its own bug at 22 s, under the measured 27.6 s a 2400 m kill takes, which would have detonated a high wreck in mid air; it is 45 s now and snaps the wreck to the ground if it ever fires. The chase camera cannot ride a 3.6 rad/s tumble, so a downed player gets a stabilised frame with the heading frozen at the moment of the kill. Respawn waits for the wreck on both AI paths, and a kill at the ground skips the fall. Also raised the evade chime from 0.085 to 0.22 against the missile beep 0.06.

Added a smoke-persistence slider (0.6-14 s) to the volumetric explosion demo. The single LIFE = 2.6 constant was doing three jobs at once - fireball duration, growth rate and how long the smoke hangs - so lengthening persistence would also have given a fireball that burns for fourteen seconds. Split it into fixed HEAT_TIME (0.52 s) and GROWTH_TIME (2.6 s) on absolute time plus a slider-driven per-blast life that only stretches the fade tail; at 2.6 s the envelope is numerically identical to the curve it replaced. Blasts snapshot the value at spawn so a drag never retimes one in flight, the auto loop moved to a fixed 2.99 s cadence so a long setting visibly stacks overlapping clouds, and a long-lived cloud keeps expanding and rising slowly rather than freezing. The billboard path normalises against the same per-blast life, so the A/B still compares technique and not envelope. 28 Node checks over the sliced life-cycle code.

summary: What is in the flight demo sky is now a roster with a stepper per opponent class and four presets (solo, training, mixed, combat), so you can choose what you are fighting instead of always getting the same six aircraft. The axis that mattered turned out to be armed rather than airframe: an unarmed opponent never fires, never locks, and is never picked as a target by any other AI - that last rule is what makes training actually work, since otherwise allies clean up the target drones while you are still lining up. Two unarmed classes, a trainer plane that is slower and lower than a bandit and still breaks from missiles, and a target drone that barely moves and does not evade at all. Both are painted high-vis orange and drawn dashed on the HUD, reusing the rule the undefended ground structures already established that dashed means it cannot hurt you, and the HUD counts armed and unarmed separately. Solo and training also switch the ground sites off, since a preset that leaves a SAM battery running is not a training mode. Two things fell out of it: several small circuits cannot share a centre, because eight target drones on a 90 m ring centred on the player would fly through each other, so any circuit under 600 m is now centred on the unit own spawn point (measured worst-case separation 539 m against a 180 m diameter); and respawn scatter has to scale with the circuit radius, since plus or minus 3 km is the same fight for a bandit and gone for a practice target.

Water plane z-fighting the terrain in the flight demo, fixed with reversedDepthBuffer on the WebGPU renderer. The water is one plane at y=0 and BASE_OFFSET pushes the low ground to straddle it, so the two surfaces sit centimetres apart over much of the map. Three defaults to a depth24plus attachment with the standard 1/z mapping, which at near 0.5 far 30000 resolves 0.75 m at 2.5 km, 2.98 m at 5 km and 11.92 m at 10 km - with a 5 cm gap it stops separating them past 700 m, well inside the visible range. Setting the flag does two things in r0.184 and it is the pair that matters: it reverses the mapping and switches the default attachment to depth32float, giving 0.25 mm at 5 km and 0.40 mm at 10 km, four orders better. Both facts were read out of the shipped three build rather than assumed, including that stencil defaults false so it never needs the depth32float-stencil8 device feature. Rejected the obvious alternative of raising the near plane: precision scales as z squared over n, so that is a 10x fix (1.19 m at 10 km) where a 30000x fix was available, and reversed depth also makes precision independent of near so the tight 0.5 near plane can stay for cockpit view. The WebGL2 fallback needs EXT_clip_control and three drops back with a warning, so the stats panel now reports the depth mode actually in use rather than the one requested.
