NPC-suite step 2: damage/hit-FX as the first mode (port of damage-simulator.html) - variant switch via applyWholeDesign, per-body reset off the geometry bus, drivesMotion tick+flush + new afterFrame hook, effect-queue flush on dispose; shell loop gained beginFrame + afterFrame

Replaced the flat flee-or-shoot coin flip under a committed drone with a proximity gradient: each bot rolls its nerve once per drone and breaks when that roll falls under threatFleeShare * sqrt(nearness), nearness being 0 at the edge of the blast ring and 1 at the impact point. So the squad does both at once - the ones at the edge shoot, the ones underneath run - and the mix shifts toward running as the drone closes. The decision escalates and never reverses inside the ring, because a bot that talks itself back into standing still mid-run reads as broken; running ends by LEAVING the ring, where the existing evadeExitScale hysteresis drops the threat and the same frame's chain hands the bot to air defence with the drone still overhead.

Added solveTwoBone, an analytic two-bone IK that is TOLD which side the knee bends toward, because the user reported the bug legs looked unrealistic and the measurement was worse than the impression: FABRIK left the knee below the hip-to-foot chord 63% of a 60 s walk (84% on the front legs), femur pointing down at a median -28 degrees where the drawn pose has it up at +24. Not a convergence failure - two segments plus a target admit a whole CIRCLE of valid knees and FABRIK picks by resuming from wherever it was, so every one of those poses satisfied the constraints it solves. Also clampLegTarget, which bounds a foot target by angle rather than distance. Both additive: KinematicChain is untouched and the sim still uses it.

canWalkLegMove's re-step veto compared against a hardcoded 0.1 m, which is a LENGTH and so has to scale with the creature - it is a sixth of the demo bug's whole leg span and wider than most of its strides, so it silently forbade the step and stranded the leg. Now gait.restepEpsilon ?? 0.1, which reproduces the old number exactly when unset, so port-creature-system.js is unaffected.

Wired the bug rig onto the analytic solver with a measured pole (the authored knee's own offset from the authored chord, so the parked pose still reproduces v1 exactly) plus two limits: swing bounds where a foothold may be PLACED, reach bounds the SOLVE. Knee inversion 63% -> 0% at every leaf radius, and no leg ever snaps straight. reach 0.99 chosen off a cost curve with a corner: p95 foot error 14 mm and no near-straight leg, against 4 mm less error but the straight-leg snap back on 7-8% of samples at 0.999, and 43 mm at 0.94.

FOUR APPROACHES TRIED AND REMOVED, recorded because all four are plausible and three made the demo visibly worse. (1) Reach as a placement bound crowded the feet under the body, shrinking the support polygon until three of five wander seeds slid off a 1.4 m leaf. (2) Reach as a step trigger fired continuously once nothing kept a planted foot near the limit, the scheduler vetoed every candidate, and all five seeds left the leaf - a limit may drive a trigger only if something also keeps the value near it. (3) A turn brake moved p95 swing 49.3 -> 45.9 degrees across its whole range, noise, while one setting left the bug unable to turn back from a rim at all. (4) Setting `uncomfortable` from the swing limit also freezes steering and cuts speed, so the bug walked straight off. HIP SWING IS THEREFORE STILL UNBOUNDED at p95 ~48 degrees; it needs a gait-level answer (yaw per stance period) and is open.

Joint limits panel: a checkbox that switches the SOLVER as well as the bounds, plus swing and straightness sliders and a live inversion readout sampled on every sim step rather than on the stats refresh, since an inversion is a transient. The checkbox had to switch the solver - relaxing the bounds alone leaves inversion at zero, because the pole and not the bound is what fixes the knee, so the comparison it invites would have been between two correct poses. Reads 0.0% on, 59.5% off.

Tests for the solver (2240 poses: knee never on the wrong side of the pole, bone lengths exact to 1e-16, unreachable targets stay bent at 163.7 degrees rather than straightening, four degenerate pole/target cases) and for the rig at three leaf radii. Every joint assertion is paired with "and the bug is still on the leaf": a falling bug reports plausible angles right up to the equator and nonsense after it, so three of the removed approaches would otherwise have looked fine. Also asserts the old behaviour is reproducible on demand. 364, 105 and 82 checks.

Three gait-objective checks failed after the rig change and all three were UNDER-POWERED rather than real regressions: at duration 3 the condition-difficulty ordering inverted by 0.07 (at 7 s it is 7.80 against 5.04) and comfortV showed a 0.0041 spread while it moves the penalty by up to 0.298 measured directly. Raised the sample lengths. The third was a genuine change and an improvement: the objective now has a mild opinion about step lift above 0.02 through the reach term, where it previously had none, so the assertion was rewritten to record which way it points.

The run-or-shoot nerve roll was keyed on the drone id, which is right for a munition (spawned per launch, fresh id) and quietly wrong for the one reusable bomber, whose id lasts the whole match - the first hover-drop of the game decided every bot's reaction to that airframe permanently and the proximity gradient stopped applying after one encounter. Threat ids are now per attack RUN via a runSeq that bumps on each entry into a terminal state.

A bomb already off the rack was invisible to the evade system - the projectile filter only admitted grenades - so bots stood still underneath live ordnance for its whole fall. It cannot use sim.life as a fuse (that is the 8s flight cap, which would report six seconds left on a bomb one second from landing), so the fall is solved ballistically and the ring is drawn where the bomb will land, carried forward by its horizontal velocity. Not flagged air: you cannot shoot a falling bomb, so there is no run-or-shoot choice about one.

Two air-defence fixes with one cause. blastDamageDrones was pure distance while ground victims had gone through blastExposure since it was written, so a blast on one side of a wall damaged a drone on the other. And the shooter dropped its target on a SINGLE occluded frame with no lock margin, which restarts the airNoticeMs recognition delay - a drone bobbing behind a roofline, or two at similar range, left a bot perpetually half a second from firing and never actually shooting. pickAirTarget gained lockId/lockMargin and the LOS break now needs 600ms to count.

Damage and blast radius were the one pair of numbers not snapshotted at launch - read live at detonation, so tuning damage mid-sortie changed the bomb already falling and could differ between bomb one and bomb two of one pass. Also passed minTargetRange into the cluster pick: the launch gate checks the seed, and the pick could then choose a neighbour up to a seedRadius nearer the operator, inside his own blast. And corrected a doc error of mine: bot-contacts.js is NOT unconsumed, latestContactNear already feeds every bot's lastKnownTarget including the operator's - the real gap is that its radius is measured to the reporting ally, and a standoff operator sits outside 18m of whoever is spotting.

Bomb drones are now a finite resource: each loss counts against bomberReplacements (1 spare per operator by default), and past that he has no aircraft for the rest of the match. Reusable had also meant free - a destroyed bomber came back at full HP with a full rack after 4s forever, so air defence against it bought seconds, while the munitions beside it were a hard stock. Only a drone removed by updateBotDrones counts; Ground every drone is a debug button and must not spend spares. The readout shows spares and munitions left, since an operator with nothing coming otherwise looks exactly like one with an aircraft on the way. Also documented that bomberCooldownMs paces the first launch and replacements only - an established bomber relaunches off its own rack and is paced by flight time plus reload.

Per-bug SIZE. scaleBugGait applies Froude similarity rather than a multiply: lengths as s, speeds and times as sqrt(s), angular rates as 1/sqrt(s). Multiplying the timings by s instead would make every size take the same number of strides per metre and they would all move like the original - the "shrunken elephant" this module header already warned about, applied within one species. The dimensionless list is where the mistakes are: body height is a fraction of the leg, lookAhead multiplies an already-scaled distance, and the rotation lerps are blend factors not rates, so none of them move. createBugRig applies it so a caller cannot resize and forget the gait; setScale re-derives from the unscaled table because sqrt applied twice is not sqrt applied once.

The field now speaks ONE frame. The body was in authored space and the legs in world space, which worked only while both were the same size; with a scale in play it would have meant multiplying some terms and not others. The rig hands over unit-authored joints (jointsUnit) so the whole field evaluates at size 1 and the scale is one multiply on the way out - a rotation plus a uniform divide is a similarity, so a distance there times the scale is the true distance and the march stays safe. Also removes the mixed-frame hazard that made the eyes render as flat discs.

MULTIPLE BUGS, six slots, each with its own pose, size, colours and eyes. Every per-bug field is a uniformArray so the field can be evaluated for an index that is a value rather than a literal; verified against the shipped build before designing around it. One bounded march PER BUG rather than a min across all of them, so a pixel only pays for bugs its own ray crosses, and each march is truncated at the nearest hit so far. sceneMap - which the 16 shadow, 4 occlusion and 4 thickness taps call - rejects distant bugs by their bounding sphere first, which is exact rather than heuristic because abs(p-centre)-radius is a lower bound on the distance to that bug.

Save and spawn: settings are plain JSON-able data (hex strings, not THREE.Color) so a bug IS its settings, saving is JSON.stringify to localStorage pcw:sdfBugPresets and spawning is a clone. Slot 0 is the draft the panel edits, so a spawned bug stops following the sliders - which is what makes several different bodies possible at once. Bugs do NOT collide; creature-collision.js would give separation but that is a behaviour change and was not asked for.

FLAT LEAF (idea 4a; walking round the whole orb is 4b and not started). The rig gains flatGround plus a groundShape option, and setGround replaces setSproutR because radius and shape cannot change independently - the solver closes over the height function and the leg segment lengths are solved against it. In the shader "flat" is the SOLID inside radius R below y=0, not a zero-thickness disc: a disc would be unsigned while the dome is signed, so the two shapes would disagree about which side of the surface a shading tap is on. Bounded by a radius rather than an infinite plane, which would fill everything below the horizon and take the out-of-focus background with it. Three other things follow the shape and would each be quietly wrong if missed: the leaf normal, the crown ramp (a height on a dome, so a radial falloff on a plane), and the rig ground.

THE FIRST VERSION OF THE NEW TEST WAS PARTLY VACUOUS AGAIN, and the canaries caught it this time rather than a user. Measured against this build: If and Loop callbacks run EXACTLY ZERO times outside a shader build, so a throw planted in the innermost march loop left the file reporting 88/88; and TSL does not throw, warn OR error on a missing argument, so the arity canary passed too. Fixes: the work moved into functions the test calls, and the arity burden moved to the static checker via a balanced-paren scan of every bugMap call site (a regex was tried first and matched none of them, reporting "0 call sites found" as a pass-shaped result). Two more checker rules were canaried and found weak: a hex-string rule that new THREE.Color satisfied, and a count-gate rule that a single test() passed because the other unrolled loop still matched. 12 of 12 canaries now caught.

reset() takes an optional place so several bugs can stand on one leaf without being stacked at the origin. The body height is the authored height ABOVE THE GROUND AT THE PIVOT rather than an absolute y: an absolute y is wrong everywhere but the origin, and a ground-relative height would have been a hair off at the origin and broken the v1 parity test, which asserts the parked pose to 1e-15.

Two gaps found by asking whether the new structure kinds actually spawn in the viewer. First, bot-viewer-v3's mix dropdown still listed the four original kinds, so colonnade/slot/rampart/corner/terrace shipped 2026-08-10/11 were reachable only by accident under Mixed and could not be isolated - added all five plus a test that scans both viewer sources and resolves reachability THROUGH generateStructures rather than guessing plurals, proved to fail against the old list before accepting it. Second, terrace emits only terrain pads, and both viewers default terrain to off, so a terrace rendered nothing while still burning a placement slot and its separation radius - measured at 10.6% of Mixed placements over 60 seeds. Added STRUCTURE_DEFAULTS.padTerrain (default true, so no existing caller changes): when false, kindsForMix drops pad-only kinds from mixed but never from a mix that named one, since an empty map is a worse answer than a flat one, and returns a dropped list so a UI can explain itself. v3's tooltip now says terraces are invisible with terrain off when it placed some anyway.

FIXED A BLACK PAGE I SHIPPED: "Invalid PipelineLayout ... While calling CreateRenderPipeline". Cause: every uniformArray is a BufferNode and therefore its OWN binding, and WebGPU guarantees only maxUniformBuffersPerShaderStage = 12. Giving each per-bug field its own array made 32 of them. Packed into one vec4 array with a stride of 16 per bug plus one for the joints - two bindings - with SCALAR_AT and COLOUR_AT tables so the CPU writer and the shader reader cannot drift apart. The padding that makes this free was noticed BEFORE the failure and dismissed as "not worth packing at six bugs": true about bytes, irrelevant to the constraint that actually applied. Nothing in Node can catch this - the graph builds and every array is valid - so the static checker gained a binding-budget rule that counts arrays structurally, including the case that produced 32 bindings from 2 literal call sites.

Raised the bug cap from 6 to 24 after the user asked why it was 6 - the answer being that I guessed. Measured: the CPU walk is 6 us per bug per frame (48 bugs = 1.7% of a 60 fps frame) and the packed uniforms are 544 bytes per bug, so the 64 KB binding WebGPU guarantees holds about 120. What 6 was really protecting was the SHADER, because the per-slot work was unrolled in JS: a march per slot whether or not it held a bug, plus one gate compare per slot inside sceneMap, which every shadow, occlusion and thickness tap calls. So the unrolling went instead - Loop(u.bugCount, ...) emits a real dynamic loop (verified in the three source: a node param builds as the end expression), which makes the shader size independent of the cap and an empty slot free rather than one compare per tap. bugCount became an int uniform since it is a loop bound now. 24 slots is 12.8 KB, a fifth of the floor. The checker gained a byte-budget rule derived from MAX_BUGS and BUG_STRIDE, and a rule that both per-bug loops are bounded by the live count rather than the slot count; five canaries, all caught.

Added a GitHub Pages homepage. Pages was already enabled and building from sp1-webgpu-renderer-migration at root, but the repo had no index.html, so msankofa.github.io/workshop-webgpu served a 404 and every viewer had to be reached by typing its filename. index.html lists all 43 tracked browser-runnable pages grouped by subsystem, with search and subsystem filter chips, reusing the code-map.html palette and GROUPS colours so the two agree on subsystem identity. Descriptions were taken from each page's own title/headings and CLAUDE.md rather than invented; the four pages that call 127.0.0.1 (server-tool, voice-line-studio, weapon-viewer-v2, and the optional telemetry helper in environment-viewer) carry a local-server badge so a remote visitor knows what will not work. Every href was verified against the working tree before pushing.

FIXED THE BLACK BALL. A dynamic Loop index is a WGSL variable named literally "i" - every single-parameter Loop in this build names it that, whatever JS destructures it to - so the march Loop nested inside the per-bug Loop declared a second var i that shadowed the bug index, and bugMap in there was evaluating the STEP NUMBER as the slot. Step 0 read bug 0, step 1 read an unused slot, and an unused slot rotation rows were zero, which maps all of space onto the body pivot inside the shell: the ray hit on its second step and the whole bounding sphere rendered as a smooth black ball, shaded from that slot black colours. Legal WGSL, so no error and no warning. Both per-bug loops now capture the index with i.toVar("bugIndex") before any nested loop can shadow it.

AN UNUSED SLOT IS NOW INERT RATHER THAN A LANDMINE, which is the half of that failure worth separating. Left at new Vector4() a slot holds the worst content available: zero rotation rows make the field a constant taken from inside the shell, and w defaults to 1, so the bound is a unit sphere at the origin - exactly where the camera points. That is what turned one shadowed variable into a ball across the frame instead of nothing. clearSlot gives every slot an identity rotation, scale 1 and a zero-radius bound 10 km under the leaf, and removing a bug clears the slot it vacated, so the live count is no longer the only thing between a slot and the picture.

Pinned the fact underneath rather than the symptom: the Node test asserts against the shipped three that both an outer dynamic Loop and a nested numeric Loop name their index "i", that the names collide, and that the index arrives as a bare name resolved where it is used - so if a later three makes them unique the test says so and the captures stop being load-bearing. WGSL scoping itself is unobservable in Node, so the static checker carries it: no bugMap call may pass a raw loop variable, both loops must capture, the hit slot must be recorded from the capture, and clearSlot must exist and run. Also made the call-site scan skip commented lines, because the page quotes the broken call on purpose. 8 of 8 canaries caught.

Wrote the trap up where the next TSL page will meet it, and swept for other cases: demos/volumetric-smoke.html nests two marches (its inner loop renames the index in JS, which does NOT rename the WGSL variable) and clustered-lights.js has two loops, but none reads an outer index inside an inner loop, so v2 was the only live case.

Shipped the panel state with the repo so the hosted page opens configured instead of stock. The save slots could never do this: they are localStorage, so they are per-browser and reach nobody. bot-viewer-presets.json carries the two 'all' states from the bot-viewer-saves mirrors (that dir stays gitignored) as captureAllState payloads, so applyAllState reads them untranslated. Presets sit in the same dropdown as the numbered slots but under a preset: value namespace, so a repo update can never overwrite a user's slot 1; they are read-only, and Save/Delete refuse rather than silently redirecting the write somewhere the user would not find it. Handed in via setPresets() because they arrive from a fetch after the panel is built.

The first-visit seed applies a state automatically, which is exactly what the autosave refuses to do, so the exemption was made narrow and then pinned rather than left to reading: it is skipped when an autosave or any 'all' slot exists, it writes pcw:bv2:presetSeeded so it runs at most once, blocked storage counts as a RETURN visit (the failure direction that leaves the panel alone), a missing or unparseable file returns silently so the viewer behaves exactly as before presets existed, and a preset that throws while applying does not mark the seed done so a bad file is retried instead of swallowed. ?preset=1 forces, ?preset=0 suppresses. Known cost, accepted not fixed: the seed runs after the initial applyLayout, so a first-time visitor builds the map twice; sequencing the fetch first would put the whole boot behind the network.

Multi-surface column query for volumetric maps: raycastAll (DoubleSide twin mesh so cave ceilings are not culled) plus map-surfaces.js naming every standable floor, its headroom and whether it is open to the sky - heightAt describes only the roof of a cave world.

generateStructures takes an optional site() hook so scatter can seat structures on imported ground: refusals retry like a clash, accepted sites lift the rects onto floorY and report a skirt depth, and pads are suppressed rather than flattening an authored landscape.

Fixed the tree viewer showing all four leaf species on every single leaf card in authored mode. leaves.atlas is not optional once leaves.map is a sprite sheet - null means the card stretches the WHOLE 2x2 sheet, so one leaf shows oak and aspen and ash and pine at once, which is what the screenshot's mixed foliage was. Every other consumer derives the grid from the texture set (forest-palette, environment-viewer and creature-viewer all do leafOpts.atlas = {cols, rows, cell: spIdx % cells}); tree-viewer was the lone exception and never set it, so its authored mode had never once been right. The grid now comes from texSet.leafAtlas in applyTexSetToOpts, and the pin toggle only chooses between one cell for the whole tree (now the default) and a random cell per leaf, instead of deciding whether the atlas is used at all. resyncAtlasControls runs BEFORE applyTexSetToOpts so a loaded species' own pinned cell survives the rebuild. Worth recording that the previous change - the atlas row flip - was a genuine canvas-y-down vs UV-v-up inconsistency and is still right (verified flipY reaches copyExternalImageToTexture on the WebGPU path), but it was almost certainly NOT what the first screenshot showed: a null atlas explains both screenshots, and I should have checked which atlas the viewer actually passes before reading leaf shapes out of a dark render.

column5: Airframe registry: mesh/circuit/enginePitch/idleThrottle/armable moved onto the descriptor and validateAirframe added so a fourth craft fails loudly instead of silently flying as a bird.

summary: Air-to-ground: two bomb types with real drag ballistics plus a CCIP pipper that shares one integrator and fixed substep with the store so predictor and projectile cannot disagree (0.7-1.3 m over a 15 s fall). Bombs are the first weapon carrying a per-instance def and a kind-keyed inventory; OFFENSIVE entries now carry their own fire call instead of an if/else dispatcher.

Aircraft studio phase 1: parametric layout deriving mass/wingArea/hitRadius/chaseDist/size from shape plus derived anchors and wing hardpoints. The falsifying test found three places the drawn craft is not the flown craft (plane wing 1.87x oversized; bird body 1.87x oversized; bird wing 30 pct undersized) and proved one density per aircraft cannot work.

Seated structures now emit a foundation. footprintAt seats the floor at the highest sample so no ground pokes through it, which left the downhill side hanging by exactly the skirt - a building on any slope visibly floated. The block is sized from the structure's real XZ bounding box rather than the radius circle, and spans skirtDepth plus a 0.3 m bury so ground curving between samples cannot show a gap. Kept in its own `foundations` list so consumers of `slabs` are untouched. Measured while testing: `radius` under-reports true extent for buildings/obstacles/colonnades/portals because canopies and cover push past the core shape; minSeparation 5 absorbs it, so the pinned invariant is that foundations never overlap.

surfaceDecks turns the multi-surface query into nav-grid decks, which is what makes a cave navigable rather than merely placeable. nav-grid already had the level machinery (attachLevels, the key space, keyAt's refusal semantics), so this is a producer walking the same cell lattice buildNavGrid samples and emitting every standable surface the grid's own heightAt does not already describe. Tested against the real nav-grid, not a mock: a bot paths along a tunnel at tunnel height, over the hill at hill height, and finds no route between the two.

Wired the surface query into env-v2: rebuildMapSurfaces after the collider, decks into buildLocalNavWindow when the map can hold more than one floor (volumetric export or structures present, ?levelNav overrides), and ?structures=N scattering seeded cover whose site hook is footprintAt. createMapCollider gained extraRoots because the collider is baked before structures exist and would otherwise let bots and bullets straight through them; the query is rebuilt after, since it borrows the BVH. Structures default off - the second BVH build is real and nothing else in the viewer expects the geometry yet. Not yet seen in a browser.

Aircraft studio page plus the mesh builder. Layout and mesh share one pair of corner functions so drawn and measured extents cannot diverge; every part is named by its anchor so focusPart works without a humanoid joint dictionary. Live rebuild (9 meshes) and a performance table measured off the shape. Found and fixed a fin winding bug (mirrored/opposite-handed slabs render inside out) and added the authority speed row after finding the plane loses its controls at 47.8 m/s against a 27.0 m/s wing stall. Fly it round-trips a design into flight-sim via localStorage.

Fixed crash on load: installPanelTheme takes a CSS SELECTOR string not an element (it scopes the stylesheet it injects). Also renamed the slider rows to .srow because the theme styles #panel .row as a space-between flex and its runtime-injected sheet wins on source order.

Second load crash: G survived in the thrust/weight row after the perf formulas moved out. Root cause was mine - the new perf section had declared its OWN RHO_SL/G_ACC beside the identical constants in flight-airframes.js, so there were two definitions of gravity. aircraft-layout.js now imports and re-exports them instead.

Panel would not scroll: workshop-panel-theme.js makes the panel root a flex column with overflow hidden and expects a .panel-body child to be the scrolling region, which the markup did not have. Same pass fixed colours (the default theme is a LIGHT panel, so the hardcoded dark text was wrong) by moving to its CSS vars, and opted the button rows out of its width:100 pct button rule.

Built an A-10 from the layout schema as the real test of it. Reproduces published span/length/wing area/empty weight/top speed within 0.1 pct and flies its own AI patrol. Three things only a fourth aircraft could expose: exhaust had to become a list (twin engines); published STATIC thrust gives a 990 km/h A-10 because flight-model has no thrust lapse, so the descriptor carries thrust at operating speed and says so; and two bench probes were measuring themselves (top speed rode the altitude clamp, 180-degree reversal never triggers because a fixed wing peaks at 173). Added levelTopSpeedOf, solved rather than flown.

Moved structure scattering off URL flags and into the panel. URL-only was wrong: env-v2 has a control system with controlRegistry save/load, and a flag no one can find is not a feature surface - 'default off' and 'undiscoverable' are different things. New Map structures section (count/seed/mix/headroom/max-slope + multi-level nav auto-on-off), shown only on an imported map since the procedural ground has no collider to query. Rebuilds debounce 400 ms because each one re-bakes the collision BVH; clearMapStructures tears the group down and restores the map-only collider first so a slider change rebuilds instead of stacking. Readout reports placed-vs-refused, refusals being the point of seating against the real surface. URL flags kept as starting values per the existing convention.

Per-aircraft guns: GUNS table plus gunFor, flyer carries f.gun and its own magazine, rounds carry their own damage, aim assist and AI reach both read the shooter gun. A-10 gets the GAU-8 (65 rps, 1430 dps, 1174 rounds). The high rate exposed that fireGun is called once a frame so the fire rate was silently capped at the frame rate - cooldown now accumulates rather than resets, bounded by MAX_BURST and a floor on the decrement, and the bullet pool went 320 to 768 because one A-10 burst keeps 232 rounds aloft.

Made Pokemon Stadium ROM models walk, which they cannot do as shipped - the cartridge has idle/attack/faint/entrance and no walk cycle, and follower-Pokemon and wild-mob mods both rest on that gap. New glb reader (no THREE, so the mapper is Node-testable), an auto-mapper that names the unnamed boneNN skeleton, and a retarget onto creature-locomotion.js. Four things only real models exposed: bone ORIGINS are not joints (a Rattata hind leg pivots sit inside the body while its geometry stands on the floor), so joints are derived from where vertex clusters meet and the retarget writes world matrices rather than rotations; legs must be found by their FEET and walked up, because a mane tuft makes a thigh a branch point and cuts one Ponyta leg into three chains; the knee must split where the halves are EQUAL, since |l1-l2| locks a foot out of the annulus (19 pct drawn-foot error to 1.6); and GAITS.walk assumes bent legs on a metre-tall body, so ride height, stride envelope and top speed are now derived from each model rest pose. Also found a size-independent 44 mm float in the height spring - it damps against a velocity that already contains this step gravity - invisible at 1 m, a third of a Rattata ride height. Planted feet land within 0.00 pct of a leg at p95 over 4 models and 8 seeds. Models recovered from the session pokedex viewer, no ROM needed.

Gave the walker a control surface, because the first viewer had three checkboxes for a module whose numbers are all derived and all interacting - standExtension shrinks the stride envelope, which lowers the top speed, which changes how far a planted foot drifts, and no one can read that chain off the source. Every knob moved onto walker.tuning behind retune(), which re-derives the gait in place: same leg objects, ground swappable mid-stride, creature never stops walking. 17 sliders plus pause/step/trails/support-polygon overlay and live readouts. Went from 4 shipped species to 14 and two of them exposed a real bug: the sim DISCARDS the height-spring force whenever the support normal tilts past 45 degrees, which is survivable on four legs and fatal on two - Charizard, Pikachu and Sandshrew sat on their hard floor 100 pct of the time, walking on their bellies. Now the sideways part is clamped instead, plus an uprightSupport knob standing in for ankle torque (1 for bipeds, 0.5 above, 0 restores the sim toppling). Seel and Sandslash went 64 and 79 pct of ride height to 100. Tests now walk all 14 species and swap a sloped ground under one mid-stride, which closes the flat-ground-only thread.

Made foot tapping and foot dragging measurable instead of arguable, then swept the tuning space for them. New pure detector module (no THREE, no DOM) scoring both from the scheduler observables plus the drawn foot, which applyPose was computing and throwing away - the gap between the drawn foot and the gait foot IS the drag. Validated against synthetic traces with known answers first, which caught two of my own design errors: the skate noise floor was on the slide in metres, making the whole metric speed-dependent so a creature dragging at a tenth of walking pace read as clean (the floor belongs on the denominator), and stride was normalised against strideEnvelope, a per-creature MINIMUM over the legs, which made real strides read as 116 to 616 pct and left the tap detector unable to fire at all. The sweep then found three defects that had been shipping. One, the re-step veto in canWalkLegMove falls back to a flat 0.1 m and the walker never set it - five times Rattata's whole 20.5 mm stride envelope, so no leg could step until the body had dragged it 100 mm, and eight of fourteen models had a median step travel of 100 to 104 mm whatever their size. Two, reachMargin 0.92 sat ABOVE reachStress 0.90, so every fresh foothold was born already flagged as overextended. Three, the support normal's sideways component was unbounded - magnitude clamped at 4g, up to 4g over root two of it sideways, settling near 24 m/s against H_DRAG on creatures topping out at 0.1 m/s - and Ivysaur and Seel ran at 189 and 208 pct of their own top speed, clamping 58 to 65 pct of planted frames. Against the SHIPPED defaults: species dragging 4 of 14 to 2, worst species clamped planted frames 34.8 to 2.0 pct, median stance skate 9.2 to 4.4 pct, Seel ride height 70 to 94 pct. The 12 of 14 figure that appears in the sweep is an INTERMEDIATE regression - scaling the guard to the creature but leaving it small is worse than the unscaled 0.1 m, and that is how the boundary was located; the flat 0.1 m happened to be near the right size for these particular models and would not be for a model half as big, which is the actual bug. Tapping turned out to be structurally unreachable - zero in about 70 configurations including savage terrain with the concurrency cap, cooldowns and re-step guard all off - because advanceLeg copies stepEnd into leg.end on landing and the trigger measures distance to the TARGET, so a freshly landed foot is at zero error by construction. Both halves of the detector do fire independently on real data, they just never coincide, and a test asserts that so a clean result cannot be confused with a dead instrument. Two bipeds still skate about 13 pct of planted frames; that needs a balance model, not tuning.

Made the two failures visible on the creature and told the user which slider owns each one, because the previous pass could measure tapping and dragging but only reported them as two lines of text after a four second window - you could see the walk was wrong and not which foot or which knob. Three new pure exports, all Node-tested. gaitHeadroom PREDICTS from the tuning rather than measuring, so it answers on the frame a slider moves: the stride budget (a leg covers two envelopes per cycle, a cycle lasts as long as every leg needs a turn) fixes a hard ceiling on body speed, deriveTuning already clamps maxSpeed to exactly that and then multiplies by speedScale, so speedOverrun above 1 means the surplus comes out of the planted feet. Risk is the WORST of its three terms, not their sum, since each is sufficient alone and the advice has to name one knob. Scored as a classifier over 12 settings x 14 species via the new sweep predict mode: 83 pct recall, 76 pct precision, and the misses are almost all Pikachu and Charizard whose tuning is clean and whose drag is the balance model - so the panel shows prediction and measurement side by side and says out loud when they disagree instead of presenting either as the answer. createLegWatch scores each leg every frame for the markers, smoothing over PLANTED frames only since a swinging foot is meant to move. Its drag score was initially normalised off the mean slide, which made a leg amber at 12 pct mean slide on a creature the report called clean - colour and word disagreeing about the same walk - so it now uses skateFrames over dragFrameLimit, the verdict's own numerator and threshold, and the frame fractions get a 1.5 s time constant against the ratios' 0.4 s because averaging a 0-or-1 sequence at 0.4 s strobes. Also capped the per-frame skate ratio at 4x: its denominator is allowed to be tiny, and on a collapsed creature one frame scored 837176737 pct and the exponential average never recovered. diagnoseGait returns ranked advice naming exactly one knob and one direction each, with a test asserting it never asks for restepFraction up and down at once (it has a rule in each direction - too small drags, too large starves). In the demo: foot rings coloured and sized by score with a separate colour for running out of leg rather than sliding, a stick drawn from where the gait thinks a foot is to where the solver could draw it, skid marks fading over 2.6 s, screen-space callouts on failing legs only, and a coach panel with both gauges showing their arithmetic, the measured verdict, advice cards whose button nudges the named slider 8 pct of its range, and a before/after filled in when the next window completes. New sweep watch mode prints per-leg scores headless with a TUNE override, because at the shipped defaults nothing clamps and the gap stick never appears - a marker validated only by looking at it is not validated.

Found from a screenshot of the foot trail, not from a number: at a gallop the trail is a sharp high-frequency zigzag rather than a series of arcs, and it reads as a leg snapping back to its foothold at an impossible speed. It is not a scheduling failure. advanceLeg lerps the foot along its arc with a half-sine lift and the whole step was lasting THREE TO SEVEN RENDERED FRAMES - 3.7 to 7.1 at a walk, 2.8 to 5.3 at a gallop - so three frames of an eased arc is two interior samples and what gets drawn is a triangular spike. The motion is right and finishes before it can be seen. Two hypotheses were checked first and were both wrong: legs are NOT over-stepping (body travel per step over two stride envelopes, which is what a step is worth, comes out 0.63 to 1.20, so the steps are earned) and the drawn foot almost never reverses (0.0 to 0.5 per second), so the zigzag is the lift arc side-on rather than the foot hunting. Two floors now sit under stepDuration. strideNumberMax 0.5 is biomechanical - a leg is a pendulum so its natural rate goes as sqrt(length/g), and stride frequency times sqrt(span/g) is what makes rates comparable across models differing threefold in size; real animals are 0.2 to 0.4 walking and about 0.6 galloping, and gallop here measured 0.68 to 1.00, off the top of the range. It is computed from the LONGEST leg, not the shortest: reach is limited by the short leg because a foothold it cannot make is useless, but timing is limited by the long one because a longer pendulum swings slower - sizing it off the short leg let Growlithe, whose legs differ 44% in span, cycle at 0.60. minStepSeconds 0.10 is perceptual and deliberately does not scale because the eye does not, and it is the frame-rate floor in disguise (0.1 s is six frames at 60 Hz). Cooldowns are stretched by the same factor the floor applied since they hold a fixed ratio to step duration and that ratio IS the turn-taking. Steps now last 6.0-7.6 frames walking and 6.4-12.7 galloping. THIS WAS ALSO WHAT THE TWO BIPED SKATERS WERE DOING: Pikachu and Charizard were sliding on about 13% of planted frames and are now at 1.5% and 4.2%, the whole set is 0 of 14 dragging with median stance skate 0.0%, Charizard's peak swing speed at a gallop went 28.8 leg spans per second (9.2x its own body speed) to 11.0, and gaitHeadroom's recall against measured drag went 83% to 95% because the misses WERE this bug - the arithmetic could not see it since nothing in the tuning was wrong. Cost is real: everything walks about 25% slower, because it was previously covering ground by cycling its legs faster than a leg that size can cycle, and speed has to be bought back with stride envelope rather than step rate. Separately, GAIT=gallop now runs the whole sweep on the other gait, which had never been measured, and it was badly broken - 14 of 14 dragging, 9 of 14 carrying themselves under 85% of ride height, half of all planted frames past full reach, bodies at 147% of commanded speed, and half of all steps having a stance under half a step duration, which is one half of the tap detector firing at 50%. Single cause: GAITS.gallop sets maxConcurrentFraction 0.5, which on a quadruped is two feet airborne and two down, and two grounded feet are a LINE - the support polygon has no interior, bodySupport tilts the normal instead of holding the body up, and the creature drops through it, the same collapse already documented for bipeds. New supportPolygonFloor 3 caps concurrency so a polygon survives; six legs are unaffected (three down of six is still a triangle, so Paras keeps its tripod) and bipeds are exempt. Gallop went down 9 to 1, height 81 to 98%, stance 0.1 to 1.2 step durations, short stances 50 to 0%, skate 19.3 to 5.3% - fixed as a COLLAPSE, not as a gait: it still drags 14 of 14 with 46% of planted frames past reach, and needs the same investigation walk got. One correction to a previous claim: under gallop with uprightSupport 1.0 and before the cap, the sweep reported tapping on one species, the only instance ever measured; it disappears with the cap in, so tapping-is-unreachable holds only for creatures that are actually standing up. Also fixed the species walk test, which asserted net displacement in METRES - scale-dependent (0.3 m was 1.9 leg spans for Rattata and 0.76 for Paras, so it quietly asked far more of small models) and it penalised a slower creature twice by giving it more time to turn away from its start. Now path length in leg spans.

Turned the walker demo from one creature into a stage, because tuning by trial needs comparison and comparing one setting against another by remembering what the last one looked like does not work. The page was built around a module-level `current` that the overlay, fault markers, measuring window, coach panel, camera and every slider's apply closure read directly; `current` is now a POINTER into a stage Map rather than the only thing there, which kept the solo readouts working unchanged. Each creature owns its own slider vector - that is the part that makes a stage worth anything, since two creatures tuned identically tell you nothing one would not - so selecting pulls that creature's settings back into the panel and a slider writes into the vectors of whatever the scope covers. New pure Node-tested stage-roster.js holds the three things that are easy to get subtly wrong and impossible to catch by looking at the screen. resolveScope: an EXPLICIT this-creature/this-species/all selector rather than something inferred from the selection, since 'make this one slower' and 'make them all slower' are different intentions, and no selection resolves to NOTHING rather than to everything - a slider that quietly retuned the stage because a click missed is the kind of thing you notice three trials later. pickCapsule: click selection against a capsule per creature and never against the meshes, because these models put vertices at 10x in bone-local space so their bounding volumes are wrong (which is also why the viewer disables frustum culling everywhere) - and writing the ray-segment math here instead of using Raycaster.distanceSqToSegment is what let a sign error in it (w must be origin minus segment start, not the reverse) get caught by a test rather than showing up in the browser as 'clicking does not select'. aggregateReports: the group panel as COUNTS AND RANKINGS, never means, because every metric in gait-diagnostics is normalised against the creature it came from, which is what makes them comparable and exactly what makes averaging one across a Rattata and a Paras meaningless - 'three of eight are dragging' is a fact, 'the stage drags 14 pct' is not - and a creature whose window has not closed counts as measuring rather than as clean. Spawning clones rather than reparses: GLTFLoader.parseAsync runs once per species and SkeletonUtils.clone makes each individual, sharing geometry and materials and duplicating only the bone graph; plain clone(true) shares the SKELETON so every individual would be posed by whichever walker ran last, same reason environment-viewer uses it. Two costs controlled deliberately - markers and overlay draw only for the selected creature unless asked, since each creature's are several objects per leg with culling off and get submitted every frame regardless of view, and the shared skid pool ages ONCE PER FRAME rather than once per creature, which would have made trails fade N times faster the more creatures you added. Scoring still runs for everyone, drawn or not, since a stage exists so several settings can be judged at once. Reports now carry the id of the window that produced them and a stale one is discarded: without that the panel keeps showing the PREVIOUS settings' numbers under the new settings' name, which is worse than showing nothing because they look plausible. Measuring window is now a slider. Camera does follow-selected, frame-the-group or free; Tab cycles selection, a adds, x removes.

Search loop plus two theme toggles. Twenty interacting knobs are not tunable by reasoning about them, so the panel now supports tuning by trial: reset, tune, randomise with a percentage, better/same/worse per trial, named setpoints and a log of everything tried. TUNE IS A REAL OPTIMISATION, not a lookup table - gaitHeadroom scores a candidate from arithmetic with no simulation, so hundreds fit in the time it takes to draw a frame, and optimise() is coordinate descent with shrinking steps. Coordinate-wise on purpose: every improvement it finds is attributable to ONE knob, and a search whose answer is a twenty-dimensional jump says nothing about why it is better. Its objective has two terms and the second is not optional, because minimising predicted risk alone has a trivial answer - crawl - so risk is weighted heavily and ties are broken by the stride budget in LEG SPANS PER SECOND, which makes the cost mean the same thing on a Rattata and a Paras. Result is 'the fastest settings the detectors do not complain about', which is what the user asked tune to target rather than their own rating. A percentage means different things to different knobs: a share of the slider's range is right for a quantity with a natural zero and wrong for a multiplier (30 pct of speedScale's 0.2-to-3 range is 0.84, which doubles a knob at 1 and obliterates one at 0.3), so multipliers move in LOG SPACE. A test scrapes the demo's slider list and asserts every tunable knob appears in the KNOBS table, since one added to the panel and not the table would silently never be randomised. Transfer across species is the other half of that table: most knobs are already fractions of something the creature owns, which is the whole point of deriving the gait from the rest pose, so they carry by construction - the four that do not are worldHeight/roamRadius/footGround (metres) and supportPolygonFloor (a count of feet), and applying a setpoint across species NAMES what it dropped, because a setpoint silently losing knobs reads later as a broken search loop rather than a units mismatch. minStepSeconds looks like it belongs on that list and does not, being deliberately unscaled. Rejection is a TOGGLE defaulting to off per the user: headroom's precision is 74 pct so a quarter of what it flags walks cleanly and those sit on the boundary worth exploring; rejects are logged either way so a better rule can rescore them. Trial rows keep the human verdict and the machine metrics SEPARATE and never fused, since merging destroys the only interesting question in the data - whether they agree - which pearson answers once enough rows are rated. metrics:null is a legitimate state and every reader filters for it; what must not happen is a row picking up the numbers on screen, measured under the PREVIOUS settings and entirely plausible-looking, so each trial records the window id it waits for and metrics attach only when that exact window closes, on the creature it ran on rather than whoever is selected by then. tuningMatrix normalises against each knob's DECLARED range rather than the trials' spread, so an existing point never moves when a new trial arrives. Log caps at 800, drops oldest first, counts the drops, and survives a full quota by keeping rows in memory for export. Also fixed gaitHeadroom reporting maximum tap risk on a walker that had been retuned but not yet stepped (dt of 0 read as zero frames per step) - it now assumes 60 Hz, which matters because the tune search evaluates exactly that state hundreds of times. Themes: a night and a day scene palette from values the scene already had, so switching cannot change what the gait does; skid marks fade toward white instead of black on the pale ground and a retired mark is collapsed to zero length rather than coloured out, since colouring out is invisible on one palette and a stray dark line on the other. Panels can switch to the look environment-viewer and bot-viewer-v3 share via the existing workshop-panel-theme.js, which reads the same saved pcw:uiTheme colours - that stylesheet also owns the panel's POSITION and docks right, which is wrong for a page with a panel on each side, so a small override restores the layout and bridges the details/summary markup onto its .sec card look.

User pointed out the tuning work rests on two untested assumptions - that the mapper picked the right bones and that the idle clip is compatible with walking - and that without checking them everything downstream is inaccurate. Both are partly false and the second is worse than that. THE CLIP IS AN INPUT TO THE GAIT, not a layer on it: the walker writes leg bones after the mixer so whatever the clip does to the spine is carried into the hips the legs hang off, and the viewer strips tracks targeting leg BONES but not tracks targeting the bone a leg is ATTACHED TO - on Rattata the last spine bone IS the front legs' attach. Measured across all fourteen models, EVERY clip animates a leg attach or an ancestor of one, and stripping the leg-bone tracks changes Tauros's hip disturbance by exactly zero. Against the stride envelope, which is the distance a foot actually has to work in: Seel's idle moves the hips 4.0x the envelope, Tauros 2.6x, Nidorino 1.8x, Growlithe 1.1x - four of fourteen have an idle that is a second walk fighting the first. AND THE SWEEP NEVER RAN IT: neither sweep-gait.mjs nor test-stadium-rig.mjs creates an AnimationMixer, so every number in the docs was measured with a still spine while the demo plays the idle by default - two different systems, and I had been quoting one while the user watched the other. On best-clip: the idle is usually already the quietest so the choice is defensible, but Paras's reaction_182 is 5.0 pct against idle's 12.4, and Charizard has an idle_alt nobody had looked at at 32.6 pct against 6.5. MAPPING: feet are on the floor on every model, which is what the mapper is demonstrably good at, but three real errors and zero mapper warnings anywhere. Sandslash's four legs are TWO LIMBS - rows 0 and 1 share their first three bones, so the mapper walked one forelimb out to two claws and called them two legs; every other check passes it because both chains reach the floor, both are a sensible length and the left/right spans match beautifully, being the same limb. Pikachu's left leg is six bones and its right is four, one having run on into something that is not a leg, and the spans match to within 0.2 pct which is exactly why a span-based symmetry check passed it. Every model also has bones near the floor in no leg (4 on Rattata, 8 on Ivysaur), probably toes but unchecked. Found one real bug on the way: readAccessor ignored accessor.normalized, and every animation rotation in these files is a normalized int16, so quaternion components came back near 23000 where 0.707 was meant - composed and chained down four bones the first audit run reported hip travel of 1e19 leg spans. Fixed in stadium-glb.js with the spec's clamp. The rig mapper is NOT affected since the only normalized accessors in these files are animation rotations, which it never reads, so the mapping findings stand independently. What this means for the earlier numbers: the MECHANISMS hold (a three-frame arc renders as a spike whatever the leg span, two grounded feet are a line whatever bones they belong to, a guard under one envelope drags) but the MAGNITUDES are conditional on the mapping being right for that species and on there being no clip. New pure rig-audit.js plus audit-stadium-rig.mjs runner and 11 Node checks.

Skeleton view plus a real bug in the search loop the user spotted by asking the right question. THE BUG: randomising with scope 'all' gave every creature the SAME settings - randomiseSelected drew one vector from the selected creature and applied it to everything in scope, so a stage of eight ran eight copies of one setting, which is all the cost of a stage and none of the comparison. Randomise and tune now run PER CREATURE, each perturbed or optimised from that creature's own values and each logged as its own trial, so one press is N trials. Tune especially has to be per creature since stride envelope and leg span differ per species and the best settings for a Rattata are not the best for a Paras. Reset stays shared because the defaults are the same numbers for everyone and what each rig derives from them still differs. Setpoint apply now decides transfer per creature too, keeping everything on same-species creatures and dropping the absolute knobs only on the others. Verdict buttons still mark the selected creature's row, since a verdict can only mean one thing. SKELETON VIEW, which is what the mapping audit actually needed: audit-stadium-rig.mjs can say two of Sandslash's four legs share three bones, but a list of boneNN names is not checkable against a creature - you have to see which part of the animal each name sits on. Every bone is drawn as a segment to each of its children, coloured by the mapper's decision, with the model solid/wireframe/hidden behind it; names off, legs-only or all; click a bone for role, parent, children and world position. RED MEANS THE BONE IS IN MORE THAN ONE LEG, which is the exact signature of the mapper walking one limb out to two toes, and nothing else on screen shows it. Bones are picked with the same pickCapsule the creature selection uses - a bone segment is a capsule like any other - so there is one tested picker rather than two. Model mode is global because SkeletonUtils.clone shares materials between individuals, which is what makes a second one nearly free; setting wireframe on one would set it on all anyway, so the panel says so rather than pretending otherwise.

Four size/appearance bugs the user caught on screen. (1) The size knob did NOTHING: with a family speciesTable, sizeFor uses the species' own sizeRange and IGNORES maxSize, so every tree rendered at full ez scale, 40-100 m over the arena. Replaced with a tree-height-in-METRES setting; each species is measured off its baked geometry and normalized to hit it, since the presets range 19.7-96.2 units tall and one multiplier cannot serve both. (2) Planted trees came out a different size from scattered ones: plantAt baked a size multiplier into the stored scale and drew its variation uniformly, while sizeFor returns the TOP of the range at sizeVar 0. Both paths now store variation only, using identical size math, with one shared normalization downstream. (3) Scattered scale was silently NaN - sizeFor computes Math.exp(p.skew*1.5) and skew was never passed - and normalizeScales' `r.scale || 1` idiom masked it, because NaN is falsy. Now passes skew/varPattern explicitly and guards on Number.isFinite with a warning. (4) serialize() read the NORMALIZED records, so a save baked the normalization in and a reload applied it twice; it now serializes from the stored placed list.

Verified the palette really re-bakes rather than just swapping a material: leaves go from 10800-tri silhouettes with full-range UVs to 3600-tri atlas cards whose UVs sit inside exactly one 2x2 cell. Also fixed the leaf-count slider stomping every species: forest-palette does count = params.leafCount ?? sp.leaves.count, so a global absolute flattened pine's 21/30/18 and ash's 30/16/10 to one number - much of what makes a pine read as a pine. Authored species now keep their OWN leaf atlas cell. leafOptsFor set cell = spIdx % cells unconditionally, which is right for buildSpecies' procedural species (no atlas at all) but discards real data from a family table: the ez families pin oak 0 / aspen 1 / ash 2 / pine 3 to match tree-textures.js LEAF_FILES, and indexing by table position gave only 5 of 16 species their own foliage - pine_small wore aspen leaves and pine_medium wore ash. Falls back to spIdx % cells when a species names no cell, so env-viewer is bit-identical. Invisible while it lasted: a wrong cell renders a perfectly fine tree wearing another species' leaves, and tree-viewer never hit it because it calls createTree directly. Only surfaced because bot-viewer-v3 is the first host to pass forest-palette an authored table. Test derives the cell back out of the baked leaf UVs and names the species.

Branch tubes now close at every end that can be seen. User spotted branches ending as open pipes; the tube is skinned with side quads only and had no caps, and the pinch-to-a-point fired only when branch.level === o.levels, so the trunk and every intermediate level just stopped at their tapered radius - roughly 30% of the base radius under the families' usual taper 0.7 - and the FrontSide bark let you look straight through the hole. Two closures picked by cost: every TERMINAL branch pinches shut (free, and it also catches branches that go terminal early because their level spawns no children, which the old test missed), and whatever is still wide gets a cap fan from the new _capRing (trunk tip, intermediate tips, trunk base). Measured 0.3328 to 0.0010 tip radius on a lone terminal trunk, and +87 branch triangles per species across the 16 ez families (+1.5%; pines +8 since evergreen taper already pinched every tip). Child base rings are left open on purpose - a child's radius is capped at 0.85 of the parent's at its attachment point and it sits on the parent's axis, so its base disc is always inside the parent tube. Collider is unaffected: bot-trees builds its own 16-triangle proxy cylinders. Leaf vertex counts are byte-identical before and after, so the RNG stream and every tree's shape are untouched.

Test fallout from the cap fans, both cases where the suite was right and the assertion had to move. test-tree-presets ringRadius divided perRing out of the buffer length, which stopped being a whole number once caps were appended (it read NaN, not a wrong number); perRing is now passed in. Its 4a measured taper at the TIP of a childless trunk, which is now pinched in both modes and no longer discriminates, so taper is measured mid-trunk and the pinch is asserted separately. Section 5's vertex-run layout assertion gained the trunk's two caps - it caught the change itself, exactly as its comment promised. New test-trees-geometry section 4 counts boundary edges by merged vertex position and mutation-checks four ways.

Stray gate: a configurable threshold on how far a PLANTED foot may sit from where the gait believes it is, plus a mode that acts on it. Nothing checked a foot against its target before - advanceLeg ran the arc to t=1 and the foot was planted wherever the solver left it, and the distance was measured as strayFraction but gated nothing. Built at the footfall first, as the phrasing implies, and it caught ZERO strays across five deliberately broken regimes including ones with 97% of drawn feet off-target: clampTargetToLimits pulls a foothold inside the leg's reach before the step starts, so a landing is on-target by construction and the whole error accumulates during the stance. Moved to planted frames. strayLimit is the same number as GAIT_LIMITS.strayFraction and the demo's slider drives both the sim and the readout, so the panel can never count against a different threshold than the one being enforced - kept out of knobSpecs on purpose (scope 'gate'), because a threshold the search may move is one it will move, and 0.3 makes everything read clean. Four modes measured over four species: at the defaults nothing strays at all (0/0/0/7 frames) so the mode is inert; at speedScale 2 only 'slow' improves skating (Pikachu 48 to 30%, Ponyta 71 to 58%) while 'restep' and 'accept' zero the stray count and make skating WORSE (to 96% and 98%) by parking the leg at its reach limit. Default off. The gate cannot fix these regimes because the cause is an arithmetic overrun of the stride budget rather than foot placement - documented as an open thread rather than papered over.

Hand-assigned bone roles, so the auto-mapper can be corrected instead of only audited. New pure stadium-rig-roles.js holds a per-BONE document (what a click produces) and compiles it to the per-leg specs mapStadiumRig now accepts via opts.roles; it refuses rather than silently fixes - broken chains, a foot that is not the distal end, two knees, a top-bone knee, self-attach, unpaired rows, bones claimed twice. Roles replace the detected legs outright; merging a guess with an instruction has no good rule. Pose capture and blending in the walker demo, answering whether the retarget generalises past walking - it does, because placeGroup and solveTwoBone know nothing about gaits and the role map supplies names. New pure stadium-pose.js stores local TRS per bone NAME, which is both what a glTF animation channel targets and what makes a pose portable between clones of a species. Demo gets a Poses panel: capture, capture-rest-from-the-glTF-nodes, blend two with a slider, hold, export/import, saved per species. A held pose is written LAST in the frame, after the walker and the mixer, so it wins over both and the creature can walk around holding it. Two defects the tests found rather than review: the capture set had to widen to include the _scale leaves, because Rattata's clips put 104 translation and 192 rotation channels on pivots but all 6 scale channels on the childless leaves the skin binds to, so a pose keyed off map.names alone would silently drop every scale in the file; and poseDistance assumed unit quaternions, so a rig posed by repeated Object3D.rotateY read as 0.06 degrees from an exact copy of itself - now divided by both magnitudes. Slerp takes the short way round (sign flip tested) and a bone present in only one pose holds rather than fading, so a half-captured pose does not collapse limbs to the origin. Not built: timing/easing, and an exporter - stadium-glb.js parses and never writes, and the only glTF writer here is the glb-shrink Node service.

Second pass over the grass-look/soil-shade toggles, three real defects. (1) Off was not free: the soil crack and moisture noise ran on every terrain fragment whatever the toggles said (~140 hash evaluations), and the grass coverage FBM on every vertex - both now sit inside If (uniform > 0.5) blocks, and the crack domain warp is computed once and shared by the three gradient taps instead of three times. (3) The curled-blade normal needed an explicit faceDirection flip: three only applies its double-sided flip to the geometry normal path, never to a custom normalNode. Also: tsl-build-check.mjs now attaches a real light, without which the whole lighting path (and every normalNode graph) was dead-code-eliminated and the builds proved nothing about normals - that is what hid defects 2 and 3. test-grass-look.mjs 27/27 (new assertions for branch gating and the face flip); the one failing check in test-sdf-mesh-bake.mjs predates this and is unrelated.

Converted the mesh ITSELF into the distance field instead of fitting boxes to it, as a second tier the spike's new field dropdown switches to. Each rigid skin chunk becomes a 24-cubed cube of signed distances (measured distance to that chunk's nearest triangle, signed by the whole model), all 96 tiled into one r16float Data3DTexture at 2.53 MB per model, baked in 0.6-0.8 s. Marching both fields from the same 120 rays and measuring each hit against the real triangles: boxes land 4.05-6.75% of body height off the skin, the volume 0.11-0.19% - a sixth of one voxel, thirty to fifty times closer. Three things were wrong on first authoring and are now written down in the doc: the sign has to be a winding number rather than a crossing parity, because these models are interpenetrating closed parts and parity punches a hole exactly where two meet (Sandshrew was 65% off its enclosed volume); a seam triangle belongs to BOTH bones, so the tile is sized from the triangles it holds and not from the fitted box, or the shader's analytic past-the-tile answer stops being a lower bound; and thin geometry has no interior for the sign grid to find (a Charizard wing, 56-59-66-73% solid across four grid resolutions), which the new skin-thickness slider covers by pushing the surface outward. Stride grew 5 to 7 vec4s per bone. 14/14 in the new suite, 8/8 in test-sdf-pikachu.mjs, 14/14 static on the page; unseen in a browser.

The volume field rendered as a blobby mess, and none of it was the bake. (1) The page shipped a joint blend of 0.05 and a skin thickness of 0.006 - measured at 1.92% surface error, FIFTEEN times its own best of 0.13% - while I had quoted the 0.16% figure from a configuration the page never opened in. The blend exists to close the seam a ROTATED bone tears open, boxes leave real gaps at a joint and the volume's chunks already overlap (a seam triangle goes to both bones), so it is now 0 for the volume and 0.05 only for the boxes, and thickness drops to 0.002. Full cost table in the doc. (2) Grid resolution is NOT the limit: against the analytic field (exact distance to the triangles, no grid) 16/24/32/48 cubed score 0.21/0.07/0.12/0.10% versus 0.08%, so 24 is already at the floor, and the 10-16 degree normal error is a bad metric - the analytic field scores worse at 29.3, because an SDF gradient near an edge legitimately swings between the two faces. (3) The real other half was colour: one averaged colour per bone turns Pikachu's black-tipped ear olive, and a per-pixel triangle search is no answer since the worst bone owns 176 triangles, not the 6.5 mean I quoted. Colour is now baked into a SECOND volume on the same grid (nearest triangle's barycentric UV through the ROM image, linear RGBA8, 5.06 MB) and sampled at the same coordinate; map returns distance alone and shade returns distance plus colour, so the colour volume stays out of all 110 march steps. 9 of 10 Pikachu bones now carry more than one colour near their surface. 17/17 in test-sdf-mesh-bake.mjs, 8/8 in test-sdf-pikachu.mjs, 24/24 static on the page.

The flight sim can now fly a Terrain Generator v5 map via ?terrain=<name>, baked to a Float32 grid by bake-terrain.mjs. Baking rather than evaluating v5 live because erosion, hydrology and paint are grid-wide simulations with no point form, so no vertex shader or CPU sampler can carry them - the CLI runs the EDITOR pipeline (generateFullGridV5), not terrain-source-v5.js, which omits exactly those stages. Every consumer already imported heightAt and nothing else, so setHeightSource swaps the world without touching a call site and null restores the wave field bit-for-bit; default is unchanged. GPU side is four clamped textureLoad fetches and two lerps rather than a hardware bilinear, since r32float needs float32-filterable and hand-rolling makes the twins agree by construction - the test demands bit-identical agreement and caught the CPU lerp using a different association than GLSL mix. 30 checks incl. a headless TSL build. Measured: 8 m posts reproduce the source field to 8 mm mean / 1.08 m worst, baked heightAt is 9x faster than 16 sines (51 vs 462 ns), bases still place dry 0/2200.

Third ground for the flight sim: --stream writes the v5 project instead of heights and the viewer generates terrain around the plane forever. The static bake's edge was my choice, not a v5 limit - terrain-source-v5 already declares capabilities:['infinite'] with bounds:null and answers heightAt(1e9,-1e9); only the omitted stages (erosion/hydrology, which need an unbounded upstream catchment) cannot follow, which is the same trade Minecraft makes since its 'erosion' is a climate noise picking a spline, not a simulation. Window is toroidal: global post (gx,gz) always sits at texel (gx mod res, gz mod res), so a scroll overwrites the column that fell off the far edge in place and only newly exposed rectangles are generated. Two real bugs caught by tests: the worker filled raw v5 heights while the main-thread out-of-window fallback applied the sea shift, stepping the ground by sea*scale exactly at the window edge; and computing the bilinear fraction in window space instead of global space made a hill's height depend on where the plane was. 33 checks incl. wrap parity over 10k posts and a headless TSL build. Measured over 75 km at 250 m/s: first fill 2.3 s in the worker, then 77 scrolls at 324 ms mean = 8.3% of one core, plane never outside the window.

Macro variation for the flight sim's ground, which was four flat colours on smoothstep(height)/smoothstep(slope). The real defect there was not missing detail but that a threshold on height alone draws a perfect elevation CONTOUR, and real snowlines wander with aspect and shelter; so the first thing added is noise offsetting the height and slope fed to the ramps, then macro colour drift at 820 m and 3.2 km, then rock strata on steep faces only. Three fbm calls, 9 octaves per fragment. Detail texture deliberately deferred to the near rings: a 4 m tile across a 16 km view repeats 4000x and is sub-pixel at cruise altitude anyway. The law is twinned (groundColorRef) but the noise is not, since MaterialX fractal noise has no JS equivalent and the palette ordering is what actually breaks - same arrangement as moss-tint.js. Test pins that every term at zero is bit-identical to the old ramp, which caught enabled:0 leaving strata running because strata is height-driven not noise-driven. 21 checks incl. two headless TSL builds. Tuning in ground-look.json via a new /api/save-ground-look, never web storage.

Species can now be given a neutral stance, because several of these models do not rest standing and it was costing them their gait: Growlithe sits, so the mapper reads almost no stride envelope off it and it walks at 18% of a leg span. A stance is a sparse per-bone TRS diff applied to the glTF BEFORE mapStadiumRig, not a display setting - leg span, ride height and the whole stride envelope are derived from the rest pose. Measured on Growlithe, one 0.15 rad hip turn: stride 18.3 -> 32.1% of a leg span, body speed 56 -> 77% of commanded. Pinned leg roles ride in the same document because detection runs on the POSED geometry and a pose can delete a leg - Ponyta loses all four to a 0.2 rad turn, and 13/14 keep every leg once pinned (Sandslash cannot pin, which is its known two-limbs-read-as-four fault surfacing). Mirror flips the delta from rest in world space rather than the local TRS, since flipping in place assumes both parent frames are exact mirrors; measured, Rattatas sides differ by 4.8% of a leg span. Empty stance returns the document untouched and skips grounding, because these models sit at -0.054 to +0.012 rather than exactly y=0 and grounding an unedited file would break parity with every earlier measurement. One shared load path (stadium-species.js) so the sweep, the audit and the rig test all obey what the page authored; a stance that stops a creature standing is now a test failure. 51 Node checks across the two new suites.

Movement is now one control with three settings - idle, walk, gallop - replacing a walking checkbox in one panel section and a base-gait dropdown in another. Standing a creature still was previously a checkbox that did not look like it belonged to the same decision as walk-vs-gallop. The capability already existed: walker.update with walk:false skips steer() and scheduleSteps(), so the body holds its heading and takes no steps while the legs still settle under it - that is the state to judge a stance and a ride height in, and the Stand stage now switches to it on entry. Idle is not a gait, so the last locomotive one is remembered and still drives every derived number, otherwise the readouts blank the moment you stand the creature up to look at it; trials record gaitKey() and never idle. Nothing is measured while idle either - the monitor stops sampling and the Walk gate says so, because a standing creature trivially does not drag and a green gate earned by standing still is worse than no gate. Pause stays separate since freezing time is a different question. improve-webgpu pass over the plants plan before any of it is built: caught that every clipmap window hard-codes lod level+1 while the drawn near chunks request lod 0, so flora placed from the window would float over crests (the roads lesson) - fixed with an explicit lod option plus a low vertical bias; also pins the per-frame contract (early returns, batched setChunks, budgeted builds, strided counters, no source.heightAt on the frame thread), the two donor disposal gaps (forest-gpu leaks palette geometries, grass-compute leaks storage buffers so grass is setter-tuned not rebuilt), TSL graphs built once behind window uniforms, and a per-phase visual rubric plus an A/B baseline.

Cloud rim controls. The quads straight edge was never the risk - alpha hits zero on the circle inscribed in the square (corners at norm sqrt2 are already transparent) - but the rim is a circle at atan(height/(extent/2)) above the horizon, 5.1 and 6.3 degrees at the deck defaults, i.e. a band of clear sky under the clouds. The two constants that shape that rim (dimming floor 0.25, rim fade start 0.85 of the radius) are uniforms now with per-deck sliders, and the extent readout prints the rim elevation so the effect of a drag is legible. 59 Node checks.

TSL pass over the plants plan against the shipped r184 build (node_modules matches the importmap): biome window must be RedFormat+UnsignedByteType r8unorm decoded x255 because RedIntegerFormat only maps IntType/UnsignedIntType in this revision; toroidal clipmap windows must use the wrap-aware textureLoad sampler rather than grass-computes existing uv texture() density path, which assumes fixed non-wrapping map bounds; and the injected height/density nodes must be Fn adapters taking two scalars since the compute kernels call heightFn(wx, wz) while the window exposes a vec2 API.

Weather C2: overcast lid, light response and fog. sky.js gained an overcast uniform mixed in at the end of skyColorAlong toward a grey brighter at the horizon than overhead (default 0, so every other consumer is unchanged - and since it lives in skyColorAlong the water sky reflection greys too). The weatherRain master now drives the lid, the key light (x1-0.72r), the ambient lift and an exp2 fog, each through its own response slider so a hand-set value survives a drag of the master. Fog is attached at startup at density 0 on purpose: verified in the shipped r184 build that FogExp2 colour/density are reference() nodes (free to move) while attaching scene.fog at all is in the material cache key. CORRECTION to the plan: fog cannot soften the cloud rim - at 0.0002 density (2 percent at 500 m) it is already 98 percent at deck A 10 km rim - so the decks keep fog:false and the lid is what hides the rim by removing the white-against-blue contrast. 79 Node checks incl. a headless dome build behind a Proxy DOM stub.

The plan keeps the capsule for deterministic locomotion and broad phase, reuses the existing pure 16-joint ragdoll topology plus gait/locomotion donors, extracts one renderer-free authoritative pose owner, stores compact root-relative joint history for lag compensation, adds per-player server-validated model/profile identity, resolves semantic bone capsules for hitscan/melee/projectiles/blasts, dual-runs capsule versus rig before cutover, and leaves location damage as a later policy. Planning/docs only; no implementation code.

Verification correction to the hit-rig plan: Base Games combatCapsule passes total height as combat.js segment h, double-counting the end caps. At height 1.8/radius 0.35 the shipped ray target spans about footY-0.35 through footY+2.15 instead of footY through footY+1.8; shooter origin also depends on the oversized h, so changing h alone would lower the muzzle incorrectly. It also names the stateful remote-gait assumption and requires measured compact pose metadata, and forbids an unexpanded movement capsule from broad-phase rejecting extended limbs.
