Plants F1: streamed terrain gets biomes. New pure terrain-biome-point.js classifies each tile with the existing classifyBiomeCell over tile-local slope and the unbounded climate sampler (now with an optional octaveBandWeight band limit, 0 = unchanged); buildTile fills the long-reserved biomeIds/moisture plus a new surfaceHeights field (visible open-sky surface, aliased to heights on analytic). One deliberate divergence: a waterline gate on the beach mask, because classifyBiomeCell applies beach after ocean and detectLakeMask skips sea cells, so a flat seabed classified as beach. Measured: biome+moisture +1.2 ms/tile on v5, surfaceYAt 16.1 ms/tile (25.7 us/post) so surfaceHeights is coarse-window-only.

Rain gains what Base Game needs without changing what bot-viewer-v3 and the flight sim draw: an optional groundSlope hook so splash rings fade out on steep ground (a horizontal ring on a 40 degree face is half buried whatever its height is, so precision alone cannot fix it) and lie on the surface normal, plus four constants promoted to uniforms - the near fade, the camera lean, the splash rate and the gust period. Every default reproduces the constant it replaced and ring slope/orientation default to off, so the two existing pages are untouched; slopeCos() is exported so a zero fade collapses to never-suppressed rather than to a degenerate smoothstep. The occluder map is deliberately not differenced for slope: it is a hard step at a roof edge.

gpuHeightAt takes a mode: 'min' returns the lowest of the four posts it already fetches instead of the bilinear blend. Rain needs it because both rain materials depth-test, so a ground height read too low is hidden while one read too high shows as drops cut off in mid air in front of a cliff - the error is asymmetric, so the sample must be conservative. Same trick as terrain-lod-coverage's erode(); water keeps the two-argument call and is unchanged.

Weather R1: rain in Base Game. base-game-rain.js follows base-game-water.js (own render-origin offset, own weather profiler slot, one update) and hooks drops to the 16 m sea-depth clipmap window rather than an analytic height, asking the terrain to stream it so a world with the sea off still has ground. Two hooks not one: the conservative min sample for the cut and the ring height, the bilinear one for the gradient, because a min filter is a staircase whose central difference is zero across most of a cell - differencing the single hook, as the plan proposed, would have produced no slope at all. Heights come back global and the graph subtracts the origin Y so a rebase does not move the rain; below sea level the hook maxes with the sea level so rain lands on the water; the Traversal Lab mixes the whole hook to a flat floor with no branch. Wind (heading, speed, gust, gust period) joins the shared keys because it leans every peer the same way, while budgets and look stay local; weatherWindFollowsWaves is local and overrides the shared slider at the point of use, so a guest follows the room sea without write permission. New test-base-game-rain.mjs (65 checks) carries a CPU twin of the conservative-vs-bilinear claim and builds both rain graphs headless with the hooks and without; the clouds test now classifies settings by the value the page defaults rather than by a pattern in the key name, which had gone stale twice.

summary: Fixed the C2 ambient lift whiting out the screen: rig.ambLight.intensity *= 1 + lift ran every frame, and createLightingRig set() early-returns on an unchanged REQUESTED value while tracking that separately from the live light, so the rig never undid the multiply and it compounded - 1.15x per frame is ~4400x after a second. Both day/night branches now carry their requested ambient in a local and the lift is an assignment, which is idempotent whether or not the setter fires. My original comment asserted this could not compound because both branches call setAmbientIntensity every frame; I had checked that the call happened, not that it did anything. New test-base-game-light-response.mjs runs the response for 600 frames and asserts it equals one frame, and keeps the old multiply in the file as the thing being guarded against; lights.js set() now warns that it compares the request, not the light.

Plants F2: the streamed biome seam. Clipmap windows carry a field payload (ids nearest, values bilinear) and can request lod 0 instead of always band-limiting; new terrain-field-scheduler.js is one small deduping priority pool so water/rain/flora stop each owning a worker that competes with visible terrain; new terrain-field-window.js gives per-field textures plus wrap-aware CPU and TSL readers (r8unorm for ids, decoded x255) behind a reference-counted registry; base-game-terrain exposes biomeAt/moistureAt/treeDensityAt/surfaceFieldAt returning null until resident so placement defers rather than inventing candidates. Tree-density table moved to the pure module so both paths share it. Measured: update 0.036 ms/frame standing with the field on, 0.518 ms flying, queue peak 0, window 576 KB.

Plants F3-F5: grass over the streamed terrain. flora-field.js reconciles biome ambition against splatWeights and is evaluated once per texel at tile commit into three u8 cover channels (no TSL twin to drift); flora-chunks.js is the env-viewer chunk host generalized with readiness deferral so a chunk waits for its field instead of building against a default; base-game-flora.js owns one grass-compute instance fed by injected heightNode/densityNode - height from the new lod-0 contact window, density from the coverGrass channel, both adding the render origin because candidates are render-local while windows are global. grass-compute gained the two optional injection points, default-off. Grass is setter-tuned not rebuilt (its dispose leaks storage buffers) and its radius is clamped to the contact windows usable circle. Not yet seen in a browser.

Weather R2: wet ground. The plan said to copy applyWetSurface maths into the splat with a hand-sync note like the CPU/GPU twins; shipped the better thing instead - rain.js exports wetPuddleField/wetRippleOffset/wetAlbedoScale/wetRoughness and terrain-splat-streamed.js imports them, so there is one copy and rain cannot bead differently on the terrain than on the wall standing on it. The tide band and the rain compose through one submerged term computed before either branch, so the seabed gets no puddles and neither double-darkens what the other darkened. Wetness LAGS the master rather than tracking it (8 s up, 90 s down, both sliders) - neither donor page has this, so ground went bone dry the frame a storm stopped - and it advances even on frames that draw nothing, or a storm ending would freeze the ground where it stood. Puddles anchor to global XZ so a rebase does not slide them. Found and stated a trap: applyWetSurface skips albedo darkening when a material has no colorNode, so the Traversal Lab would have gone glossy without going dark; it passes baseColor explicitly and the behaviour is documented rather than defaulted, so bot-viewer keeps its look (whose walls may have the same silent gap). Deferred applyWetSheen on bodies: base-game-player-bodies.js owns those materials and another session is mid-rewrite there, so the three sheen settings were dropped rather than shipped dead.
